Chapter 246: The Start Of Round
15 (2)

[Hello, humans? Welcome to Round 15. Now, shall we check the quest?]

The angel smiled, as if saying there was no need for lengthy explanations,
and flapped its wings.

◀ ROUND 15 ▶

└ Pass three missions

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

└ Participants: 2,304

└ Completers: 0/576

“Three missions?”

“What kind of missions?”

“Look at the number of survivors.”

“It’s cut down to a quarter?”

Hearing the players’ murmurs, the angel frowned.

[Didn’t the previous angel mention it? The difficulty increases with every
fifth round. This round is no exception. Only 576 out of 2,304 will survive.]

“Not even 600…”

“Will I be one of the 576?”

Outwardly, people seemed worried, but inwardly, they were hopeful.

Surely, I can make it into the top 500…

There should be a spot for me, right?

But contrary to people’s expectations, this round would fall short.

By a wide margin.

‘Not even 50 will survive, let alone 500. At least, that’s how it was in the
last cycle.’

This time would be different from before.

The situation was no longer one where he didn’t care if others died.

‘This time, I’m bringing all 576 survivors.’

Thinking ahead to the 20th round, saving as many as possible was
necessary.

“It looks like we’ll need to compete hard to be in the top ranks.”

“Why compete? Aren’t we all on the same team?”

“Angel! Is this round a solo or a team competition?”

To one player’s question, the angel smiled and said,

[I can’t tell you that. All I can say is that you’re not in a party.]

“Not in a party?”

“Does that mean it’s a solo mission?”

People seemed confused, but Ryu Min knew the answer.

‘It’s not exactly solo. Without cooperation, everyone will be wiped out.’

He wanted to tell them about the mission, but he held back, knowing the
angel was watching.

It wasn’t time for him to step up yet.

“Angel! What about the three missions?”

“What will they be?”

[That’s for you to find out as you proceed.]

“What about side quests?”

“What’s the ranking criteria?”

[Side quests and ranking criteria are also secrets. Telling you now would
spoil the fun, wouldn’t it? Hehe.]

The angel chuckled smugly, then changed its expression and flapped its
wings.

[Shall I send you to the mission site now?]

As soon as the angel spoke, darkness engulfed the 2,000 players.

---

“W-Where is this?”

“Is anyone there?”

“I can’t see anything.”

The monochrome space had turned into a pitch-black one in an instant.

The confusion was short-lived; as their eyes adjusted to the darkness, they
could faintly make out each other’s silhouettes.

The problem was that there were no visible landmarks or terrain in the place
they had been transported to.

“There’s nothing here?”

“It’s just a flat, empty space.”

“This isn’t space, right? I can feel the ground beneath my feet.”

“Where’s the angel? I don’t see it anywhere.”

“I guess this means we have to handle this ourselves now.”

What kind of mission would take place in this dark, seemingly infinite
space?

The question was answered when a message appeared.

[Welcome to the mission site for Round 15.]

[You must complete all three missions within the time limit to survive this
round.]

[Now, let’s begin the first mission.]

└ Survive for 30 minutes against the Dark Illusion

[If successful, you may proceed to the second mission.]

[Current number of survivors: 2,304]

[Time remaining until the next mission: 00:29:59]

“What’s a Dark Illusion?”

“Is it a type of monster?”

“Well, as long as we survive, we’re fine, right?”

“Running and hiding is my specialty.”

Some players wore confident expressions, but this wouldn’t be as easy as
they thought.

‘Darkness is the ideal environment for the Dark Illusion.’

Some players voiced their skepticism.

“Who says we have to run?”

“Yeah, why can’t we just defeat whatever it is?”

“If it’s a monster, we just have to kill it, right?”

But as if on cue, another message appeared, wiping the smirks off their
faces.

[Just so you know, the Dark Illusion is invincible.]

No matter how strong Ryu Min was, he couldn’t break through invincibility.

This meant he, too, would have to avoid the Dark Illusion.

‘But there’s an easier way than just running.’

That way was invisibility.

The Dark Illusion couldn’t detect players who were invisible. If one used
the potion and stayed still, survival was guaranteed.

This was why Ryu Min had given invisibility potions to the key members.

‘Use them. Now.’

He had made sure to tell them to drink the potions as soon as the mission
started. Christine, John, Min Juri, Yamti, and Seo Arin all disappeared from
sight as they drank their potions.

Ryu Min could have hidden himself too, but he chose not to.

‘This round isn’t about surviving alone. It’s about everyone surviving
together.’

He needed to guide the other players who didn’t have invisibility.

Just then, a low, eerie wailing sound filled the space—

Wooooooooooo—

The Dark Illusion had appeared.

Chapter 247: Dark Illusion (1)

“D-Did anyone else hear that sound just now?”

“Ugh, this is giving me chills.”

“Ughhh…”

The wailing of the Dark Illusion was anything but ordinary. It was a sound
that triggered primal fear, inflicting the status effect ‘Fear’ according to the
system. That’s why some players were visibly trembling.

‘Although it doesn’t trigger with 100% certainty.’

Thanks to the Blessing of the Saintess cast by Christine before the start,
many players were able to resist the fear.

Ryu Min, of course, was an exception and did not succumb at all.

‘With the blessing, the chance of falling into fear is 2.45%. Even if I do, it
only lasts 0.07 seconds.’

Given his already high resistance, combined with the blessing that halved
the probability of status ailments, there was virtually no chance of him
being affected.

‘The wail of the Dark Illusion doesn’t faze me at all.’

But its true threat wasn’t in its status effects.

“W-Where is it?”

“I heard the sound, but I don’t see anything.”

For the Dark Illusion, darkness was like water to a fish. It was fast, barely
visible, and a truly troublesome monster to deal with.

‘It doesn’t register on presence detection and is hard to spot with the naked
eye.’

Of course, there was a simple countermeasure. Emitting light would force it
out of the darkness, making it easier to kill. But that method wouldn’t work
here, as the environment was tailored to favor the Dark Illusion.

As expected.

“Huh? The light isn’t coming through.”

“Guys, something feels wrong!”

“Someone use a skill to light this place up!”

“It’s not working! At all!”

Attempts to light the area were extinguished as easily as a candle in the
wind. In the pitch-black darkness, players grew tense, scanning their
surroundings.

“Ahhhh! M-My arm!”

A scream rang out from somewhere. Turning toward the sound, a player
was faintly visible, trembling with their arm severed. Soon, a blade burst
through their chest, and they fell lifelessly to the ground. The first casualty
had occurred. Yet, no one could pinpoint where the monster was.

Only terrifying sounds echoed.

“Argh!”

“Here! The monster is here!”

As soon as the second scream was heard, chaos ensued.

“Guh!”

“Ah!”

Screams erupted all around. Looking up, figures clad in ragged clothing
flitted through the darkness. These were the Dark Illusions.

“Where did so many come from all of a sudden?”

“Everyone, be careful!”

“Damn it, that thing cut my arm!”

“Kill it! Fight back!”

“Didn’t you see the message? It’s invincible!”

“We have no choice but to run!”

There were more than 100 Dark Illusions moving through the darkness like
fish in water. Even though players now recognized the threat, evading them
was nearly impossible due to their sheer numbers and speed.

“Agh!”

“It hurts! It hurts!”

“Guhhh!”

As the monsters passed by, they slashed with their long claws, sending jolts
of pain through their targets.

“Are we really supposed to escape from all these creatures?”

“But aren’t these things monsters? Why aren’t they detected?”

“Shut up and just run!”

In the chaos, the only ones maintaining any composure were those using
invisibility or the members of the Death Church who had been briefed on a
strategy. And, of course, Ryu Min, who planned to turn the tide of battle.

‘Everyone’s panicking.’

People were running for their lives as if a beehive had been disturbed, but
there was no real need for it.

‘They’re all fakes. Except for one.’

Despite what appeared to be over 100 Dark Illusions, all but one were
decoys. These clones only induced false pain and didn’t cause actual
damage.

‘They’re just being tricked by a single monster’s illusions.’

With this in mind, Ryu Min calmly stepped through the darkness, searching
for the real Dark Illusion. The first task would be easily cleared if he found
the true body.

‘Where are you? Show yourself.’

He moved skillfully, dodging the attacks of the decoys that struggled to
keep up with him.

‘Even if they’re fakes, there’s no reason to get hit.’

Identifying the real one was straightforward. He cast the Death Mark on
every Dark Illusion he came across.

‘If the real one is marked, its health bar will appear. The decoys won’t show
it.’

This method allowed him to distinguish real from fake quickly. What once
seemed like a trivial skill now proved invaluable.

Soon enough.

‘There it is.’

He spotted a Dark Illusion with a visible health bar, lurking among its
clones and hunting for prey.

Uuuuuuuuuu—

The creature emitted its wail, signaling that it had chosen a target. While
others were paralyzed with fear, it darted toward a defenseless female
player.

‘It’s invincible, so I can’t kill or push it…’

But Ryu Min, with his overwhelming speed, intercepted the creature before
it could strike.

‘…but I can disrupt its hunt.’

Chapter 247: Dark Illusion (2)

‘It’s invincible, so I can’t kill or push it…’

But Ryu Min, with his overwhelming speed, intercepted the creature before
it could strike.

‘…but I can disrupt its hunt.’

Just as its claws were about to pierce the player, Ryu Min scooped her up.

“Kyah!”

The woman shrieked as she was lifted into the air, only to realize it was the
infamous Black Scythe setting her down safely.

“That was close. Are you alright?”

“M-Me?”

The woman turned to see the Dark Illusion glowering at her.

“Th-Thank you, Black Scythe.”

Ryu Min nodded and shouted to the crowd:

“Listen up, everyone! I’ll tell you how to beat this round!”

The crowd’s attention shifted to him at the promise of a strategy.

“There may seem to be dozens, but there is only one true Dark Illusion.
That one over there.”

Ryu Min’s scythe pointed directly at the real one. From its perspective,
losing its prey and being revealed must have been infuriating.

“All the others are clones. Only worry about the one I just pointed out!”

“Clones?”

“That’s impossible. How can that be?”

“What nonsense is this?”

Players found it hard to believe. The pain they felt was too vivid to be fake.
Was it really possible that this pain was all an illusion?

Reading the doubt on their faces, Ryu Min shouted again:

“It’s an illusion! All the pain you’re feeling is fake. Don’t be deceived!”

“An illusion…”

“I can’t believe it…”

The players stared at him in disbelief as clones attacked again.

“Ahh!”

“It hurts! It really hurts!”

“How can this be fake?”

“I can see the wounds, the blood…”

“Stop talking nonsense…”

But Ryu Min had anticipated this.

“Trust me! Look at the death count! How many have actually died?”

The players glanced at their quest screens with uncertainty.

[Survivors Remaining: 2,303]

[Time Until Next Mission: 00:27:12]

“What?”

“Weren’t there 2,304 of us?”

“Why has only one died?”

Despite all the attacks and injuries, only one person had died?

“It’s like I said. They’re clones. The pain you’re feeling is false, and only
one is real. Recognize that, and you’ll be free of the pain.”

The players who dismissed Ryu Min’s words now listened closely, doubt
turning to realization. And, just as he said, the pain vanished like a wave
receding from shore.

“Wait, it was really an illusion?”

“All this pain I felt was fake?”

With this realization, even the Dark Illusions in the air seemed like mere
shadows. The attacks now only caused a brief sting, dissipating once they
were perceived as false.

Seeing this, Ryu Min’s lips curled into a satisfied smile.

‘Breaking illusions is simple. Realization is the key.’

Once someone accepts it’s an illusion, it no longer holds power. While this
didn’t mean they could identify the real one automatically, it was enough.

“Ignore the others! There’s only one real threat!”

“Which one is it?”

“Say it again, Black Scythe!”

The Death Mark was visible only to its caster, so only Ryu Min could see
the health bar.

“That one.”

He pointed his scythe at the true Dark Illusion.

Uuuuuuuu—

Enraged, the creature lunged.

Swoosh—

Ryu Min dodged effortlessly and continued to inform the players, “Avoid
this one! This is the real one!”

Thanks to his guidance, players managed to evade the true monster,
effectively stalling for time.

‘Great. At this rate, surviving for 30 minutes is a breeze.’

Since they knew which one to avoid, players could move around and buy
time easily. The result? Despite 20 minutes passing, only one death
occurred. For the Dark Illusion, this was infuriating.

Uuuuuuuuuu!

Desperation drove it to repeatedly wail and cast fear. But each time, Ryu
Min thwarted its attacks by intercepting its prey.

Uuuuuuuuuu! Uuuuuuuuuu!

No matter how many times it shrieked, the result was the same.

‘There will be no more casualties.’

And so, after 30 minutes of relentless disruption—

Ssssh—

The Dark Illusion and its hundreds of clones dissipated into smoke.

[The time limit has ended.]

[The first mission has been completed successfully.]

[Survivors: 2,303. Deaths: 1.]

[Congratulations! The second mission will begin shortly.]

“Phew! Finally, it’s over.”

“Nice! Only one person died!”

“It’s all thanks to the Black Scythe!”

Players cheered, with some bowing their heads in gratitude toward Ryu
Min.

‘Saved quite a lot this time.’

Given that previous attempts had seen hundreds dead, it was indeed a
commendable outcome. However, there was no time for complacency.

The second mission would be painted in blood.

Chapter 248: The Second Mission
(1)

Whoosh—

The dark space suddenly brightened.

The place where everyone stood was a vast chamber that could hold up to
two thousand people.

“Phew, now we can finally see.”

“It looks like we can use our skills properly now.”

“So, what could the second mission be?”

“Doesn’t the Black Scythe know? Judging by what he said, it seems like
he’s aware of the strategy.”

“Why don’t you ask him?”

“N-no way. I’m not that curious. If you’re curious, ask him yourself.”

“W-well, I’m not really that curious either.”

Despite their words, people stole glances at Ryu Min.

They were curious to know if he was aware of what the second mission
entailed.

But no one dared to ask him.

This was because Ryu Min’s expression and the atmosphere around him
were ominous.

“He doesn’t look happy.”

“What’s up with him?”

“Is the second mission going to be difficult?”

Although people whispered among themselves, it wasn’t just Ryu Min
whose expression was tense.

The followers of the Death Church were also nervously waiting for the next
mission.

They already knew from Ryu Min that this mission was one where they’d
be forced to kill or be killed.

A moment later, a message appeared, the one everyone had been waiting
for.

[The second mission will now commence.]

└Kill each other.

└Within the 30-minute time limit, kill at least one person to pass.

[Only half of the participants, totaling 1,152, will pass.]

[Anyone who fails to pass within the time limit will be eliminated.]

[Successful participants may advance to the third mission.]

[Current number of survivors: 2,303]

[Time remaining for the mission: 00:29:59]

People’s eyes widened as they read the mission.

“W-what? We have to kill each other?”

“Like in Round 4?”

Unpleasant memories came to mind.

The death-filled Round 4, where they had killed and been killed to survive.

Gulp—

They swallowed nervously and looked at each other.

Already, some people’s eyes shone with a murderous glint.

Everyone cautiously kept their distance from one another.

‘Kill each other within 30 minutes…’

‘Now I understand why the Black Scythe’s face was so serious.’

To be honest, who would willingly commit murder unless they were a
deranged psychopath?

What benefit would there be in killing someone?

But now, there was a clear benefit.

Survival.

Taking another’s life granted you the right to live.

Still, no one moved right away.

It was difficult to turn a blade on another, no matter the circumstances.

‘Now, we’re being forced to kill each other…’

‘What kind of twisted mission is this…?’

Companions who had survived together for 14 months suddenly became
enemies.

Some hesitated, torn between ethics and morality.

‘Just close your eyes and do it.’

‘There’s no other way if you want to survive.’

‘The world is about stepping over others to climb higher. This is just
another competition.’

Others rationalized that they had no choice but to kill.

Amidst this silent tension, the followers of the Death Church moved closer
together.

They did so because of a command they had received earlier from the Black
Scythe.

The second mission involves killing each other. It will likely be as brutal as
it was during Round 4. However, don’t be swept up in the chaos. Do not
participate in the killing. Do not even point your blades at each other. Just
stay with your fellow followers and watch the situation. If someone attacks
first, you may retaliate. But until I signal, do not act.

Don’t join the slaughter.

You can kill someone who attacks first.

Trust and protect one another as comrades.

Wait until I give the signal.

The followers gathered and trusted one another to carry out these four
commands from the Black Scythe.

It was logical to wait and see how things unfolded, as they didn’t know
what might happen.

They also had faith in the Black Scythe.

On the other hand, those outside of the Death Church were becoming
restless.

“A-are we just going to keep watching like this? Shouldn’t we do
something?”

A sharp voice responded to the outcry.

“What do you suggest we do? Kill each other?”

“If we don’t, we’ll all be eliminated. We have no choice.”

“If each person kills just one, then exactly half will pass.”

“Thanks, math genius.”

“Don’t be sarcastic. Do you have a better idea?”

“Me? I don’t have any ideas.”

“Then, why don’t we hold a tournament?”

“A tournament? What a dumbass!”

“Hey, just because this is another world, it doesn’t mean you can talk like
that.”

“Say something reasonable. Who’s going to arrange the matches? And
who’s going to face the Black Scythe?”

“The idiot who suggested the tournament can go first.”

“I’m sorry. That was stupid of me. So, do any of you geniuses have a better
plan?”

“The Black Scythe would know, right? He knew the strategy for the first
mission.”

“Black Scythe, do you know how to beat this mission?”

“If you do, please tell us.”

All eyes turned to Ryu Min, but he had nothing to say.

There was no other way than to kill.

Breaking the silence, Ryu Min coldly muttered.

“We have to kill. There’s no other choice.”

“……”

The answer wasn’t what the players hoped for, and they collectively sighed.

The more they thought about it, the more it seemed there was only one
solution.

‘Do we really have no choice but to kill…?’

The system was set up so they had to kill each other.

It took them 10 minutes to realize this.

“We’re running out of time. Ten minutes have already passed.”

“If this keeps up, we’ll all be eliminated. At least half of us need to
survive.”

“Then why don’t you start killing someone first?”

“W-well, that’s…”

A stalemate continued.

Even those who had experienced murder during Round 4 hesitated.

It was precisely because of that hellish experience that they were now
reluctant.

In a way, they were not just competitors who had shared life and death for
over a year; they were comrades.

‘Everyone is hesitating, just as I expected.’

Ryu Min had anticipated this standoff.

It had happened during Round 4 as well.

‘I need to break the ice.’

They needed to start killing.

For this, Ryu Min decided to use the Despair Cult.

His gaze met that of John Delgado, who stood in the distance.

‘Execute.’

John Delgado nodded slightly in response to the signal.

Before long—

Thunk—!

Chapter 248: The Second Mission
(2)

‘Execute.’

John Delgado nodded slightly in response to the signal.

Before long—

Thunk—!

“Guh-urk!”

The chilling sound of flesh being pierced resounded.

Thud—!

The eyes of those nearby turned to the fallen man.

The first victim had appeared.

He was a follower of the Despair Cult.

And the one who killed him was also—

“A-a murder!”

“Look! His nickname turned red!”

“What’s going on? He killed one of his own?”

Nearby followers of the same cult were stunned.

It was a ridiculous situation for a follower to kill another, but they didn’t
know.

They had no idea that John Delgado, their leader, was behind it.

Ryu Min watched the murder unfold from afar, smirking.

‘The followers really do follow the necromancer’s orders.’

John Delgado had privately met with a follower earlier and made a
proposal:

Kill a nearby follower when I give the signal.

In return, I will share the next round’s strategy and grant you a rank
equivalent to that of a cardinal.

‘To think they’d all fall for that.’

What was even funnier was that more than one follower had agreed to this
proposition.

Thunk—! Thunk—!

“Urk!”

“Gah!”

The followers of the Despair Cult turned their weapons on each other.

They killed without hesitation, trusting in the leader’s promise.

Ha-ha-ha, ugh—

A follower who laughed as he killed was in turn stabbed by another
follower.

That one was then cut down by yet another follower.

The scene among the Despair Cult members was one of ruthless bloodshed.

They were all fanatics, seduced by John Delgado’s promise.

Thunk—! Thunk—!

“Argh!”

“Kill them!”

When the followers suddenly started killing each other, Berber was
shocked.

“What’s going on? Why all of a sudden!?”

He hadn’t imagined any hidden manipulation behind it.

“Hey, you maniacs! Why are you attacking your own comrades?”

To him, the followers of the Despair Cult were valuable assets and soldiers.

They shouldn’t be wasted like this.

But no matter how much he tried to stop them, they were too busy killing.

Why had they suddenly started fighting?

For Berber, who planned to kill John Delgado and expand his power, this
was incomprehensible.

However, murder wasn’t confined to the Despair Cult.

“Kill them!”

“Damn it, you! Come here!”

“Die! Die!”

The ice had broken, and people began to slash at one another without
hesitation.

Seeing the Despair Cult members fighting, others felt compelled to join in.

Justifying their actions as necessary for survival was an added bonus.

Hmm.

Amidst the chaos, Ryu Min observed quietly.

The followers of the Death Church refrained from participating, only
watching as instructed by Ryu Min.

He continued to monitor the quest progress bar, waiting for the
rightmoment.

[Current number of survivors: 2,102]

[Current number of passers: 201/1,152]

……………

[Current number of survivors: 2,050]

[Current number of passers: 253/1,152]

……………

[Current number of survivors: 1,991]

[Current number of passers: 312/1,152]

……………

As the number of survivors dwindled and the number of passers increased,
Ryu Min continued to wait.

‘Not yet. More need to die.’

Even though Ryu Min remained composed, the increasing number of
passers made the followers of the Death Church anxious. They started to
worry if they should join in the killing now. Would they miss their chance to
survive if they continued to sit idle?

But they kept their trust in the Black Scythe, anxiously waiting for his
signal.

Finally, when the number of passers exceeded 400, Ryu Min signaled John
Delgado with a look.

‘Summon them.’

John, catching Ryu Min’s gaze, nodded and activated his corpse
reanimation skill.

“Arise.”

A light emanated from the tip of his staff, spreading out to the corpses
strewn across the ground.

Soon—

“Groooaaaar…”

Hundreds of bodies rose, moving like zombies.

The frenzied combatants stopped mid-strike, their attention caught by the
surreal sight.

Step, step, step—

The undead, moving in unison like a trained army, began advancing
towards—

“W-what are those things?”

“They’re coming this way?”

The group they seemed to be heading for was none other than the Death
Church followers.

It looked as if the undead were about to attack them en masse.

‘In reality, they’re here to offer themselves as sacrifices.’

Contrary to appearances, the undead had no intention of attacking. They
were merely presenting themselves to be killed.

‘It’s less morally taxing to slay already-dead bodies than living people.’

Ryu Min’s strategy banked on the fact that eliminating summoned creatures
would still count toward the mission’s kill count.

Step, step—

As John Delgado’s summons approached, Ryu Min shouted decisively.

“All members of the Death Church! Slay those undead! One each!”

Executing the order wasn’t difficult.

They weren’t real, living people; they were merely summoned creatures.

Slash! Thud!

Moreover, the undead didn’t resist, making them easy targets.

“Huh? Why aren’t they fighting back?”

Their curiosity was short-lived.

One by one, the Death Church members widened their eyes in
astonishment.

‘Wait a second, this message…?’

‘I killed an undead and received this?’

When Ryu Min himself struck down an undead near him, he saw the same
message the others did.

[You have committed murder.]

[You have passed the second mission.]

Chapter 249: The Third Mission (1)

The undead, who moved like zombies, were effortlessly taken down by the
blade’s strike.

Each time, the followers of Death Church were astonished by the
notification that someone had passed.

Ryu Min, who had anticipated this outcome, did not show much surprise.

‘So, killing undead that were once human counts as murder.’

Even though he was killing summoned beings, the system perceived it as
murder.

It was the same when he had slain the undead angels in the past.

‘I was surprised then when an additional reward was given.’

Just as Ryu Min had once been astonished, the followers of the Death
Church now wore stunned expressions.

No one had expected that killing the undead would count towards passing
the mission.

‘Neither did I, to be honest. I just hoped it would work because it had
applied to the angels.’

This had been the plan he devised, based on that very hope.

‘Initially, the plan was just to let them kill each other off without
intervention….’

But with the card of necromancy in hand, he thought of a different strategy.

After all, wasn’t it better to kill undead than to kill living people?

Squelch-! Stab!

“Argh!”

“Gah!”

Hundreds of summoned beings, created by John Delgado, were cut down by
the members of the Death Church’s attacks.

Ryu Min watched this with satisfaction but was unaware of the strange look
he was receiving from behind.

‘Why are John Delgado’s summons allowing themselves to be killed?’

When she first saw the approaching horde of summons, Christine had
prepared for a fierce battle.

She assumed John Delgado had come to kill her again.

But strangely, the undead showed no intention of attacking.

Even she, who had no combat ability, could kill them easily with her blade.

That made it even more surprising.

‘Why? Why are they coming to be killed? I thought John Delgado had sent
them to attack the Death Church?’

Christine was not the only one puzzled by this.

‘What is that idiot doing?’

It was none other than Berber.

‘He’s wasting valuable summons!’

Berber couldn’t comprehend John Delgado’s actions. He was already
furious that the followers of the Cult of Despair had been wiped out, and
now their leader was raising corpses only to throw them away pointlessly.

‘Damn it, I can’t just sit and watch this.’

Berber moved stealthily.

‘This is my chance. If I kill the cult leader now, I can become the new
leader of the Cult of Despair.’

Though he would have to start from scratch without any followers, he was
confident he could gather them over time.

He crept up behind John, raising his axe high.

‘Die.’

But before he could bring it down, something fell.

‘What?’

It was his own arms, still gripping the axe.

So stunned that he forgot to scream, Berber then saw a winged, ethereal
undead holding a curved blade.

It was Sariel, John Delgado’s strongest summon.

“Ahhhh!”

Whether he screamed out of shock at seeing an archangel or from the pain
was unclear, but it didn’t matter.

For John Delgado, the most important thing was to eliminate traitors.

“You thought I didn’t know you were after my position?”

“You, you…!”

John Delgado smirked and gave a cold command.

“Kill him, Sariel.”

Before he even finished speaking, the curved blade swept across Berber’s
neck.

Thud—

John Delgado watched the fallen face dispassionately, feeling a surge of
gratitude towards his master.

If not for the warning from the Black Scythe, it would have been his own
head rolling on the ground.

From a distance, Ryu Min, who saw that John had survived, smirked.

‘Now, the Cult of Despair is finished. No more unforeseen variables.’

The only remaining variable was the impending assault by the archangels,
which could come at any time, so he couldn’t let his guard down yet.

Squelch—!

With the sound of a blade sinking into flesh, the last summoned being fell.

Once all the undead had perished, Ryu Min turned to the followers of the
Cult of the Reaper.

“Is there anyone here who hasn’t passed yet?”

All the followers shook their heads.

All 400 members of the Cult of the Reaper had made it to the list of
survivors.

“That was fortunate. Who would have thought killing the undead would
count towards passing?”

Feigning ignorance, he acted like he didn’t know that this had all been part
of his plan.

As the situation settled, a voice suddenly called out.

“Stop fighting now! We’ve reached the limit for the survivors!”

Everyone’s gaze turned to the progress display.

[Current number of survivors: 1,152]

[Current number of successful participants: 1,152/1,152]

Survivors and successful participants were now equal.

This meant further killing was meaningless.

Those who hadn’t planned to kill more than necessary laid down their
weapons and backed away.

‘Only one task remains now.’

All they had to do was endure until the time limit was up.

Though they couldn’t be completely at ease, as someone might suddenly
decide to attack.

Amidst the tense silence, Christine still couldn’t shake her doubts.

‘What’s going on? John Delgado’s summons showed no intent to attack. It
was as if they wanted us to kill them to survive.’

The Black Scythe had said to observe the situation, and the summons had
appeared at just the right moment.

They had shown no intention to attack.

Was this all a coincidence?

Christine shook her head as if trying to erase her suspicions.

‘No, it can’t be. It’s absurd to think the Black Scythe orchestrated this. It
makes more sense to believe he foresaw the future.’

Just as she cleared her mind of these thoughts, the time limit ended.

[The time limit has ended.]

[You have successfully completed the second mission.]

[Survivors: 1,152; Deaths: 1,151]

[Congratulations! The third mission will begin shortly.]

Ryu Min looked for Christine upon seeing the message.

“You know, right? Your role in the third mission is crucial.”

“Yes… I know.”

Christine nodded, but Ryu Min caught a momentary flicker of worry on her
face.

“Don’t worry. I’ll protect you. Just focus on maintaining your skill. A
thousand lives depend on it.”

“Understood, Black Scythe. I won’t let you down.”

Christine finally showed a determined gaze.

The followers of the Death Church, who had been briefed beforehand,
swallowed nervously, knowing how dangerous and difficult the third
mission would be.

Of course, those outside the Death Church awaited the announcement
without much concern.

Then it happened.

“Huh? What’s that?”

Chapter 249: The Third Mission (2)

Then it happened.

“Huh? What’s that?”

Suddenly, countless green lines appeared on the floor.

Each line, about shoulder-width apart, stretched out horizontally.

As people exchanged puzzled glances, the awaited message appeared.

[Before the third mission is revealed, please move to the green marked lines
on the floor.]

[There are 1,152 lines, one for each survivor.]

“Marked lines?”

“Looks like we need to stand there.”

People moved as instructed without complaint.

“Does everyone stand on a line?”

“Oh? The line turns red when you step on it.”

“It’s like a parking guide light.”

The green lines on the floor gradually turned red as people found their
spots.

Some scurried around, frantically searching for a place.

As everyone stood in their designated spots, they realized they were lined
up in a row.

The final person stepped on the line, and a new message appeared.

[The third mission will now begin.]

└Endure the Pain.

└Endure without dying for 30 minutes to pass.

[A projectile that deals consistent damage will be fired every 2 seconds.]

[Each player will be targeted by one projectile.]

[The damage from the projectiles will gradually increase over time.]

[Successful completion will yield round rewards.]

[Current number of survivors: 1,152]

[Time left until the end of the round: 00:29:59]

“What is this? Endure the pain?”

“We’re supposed to endure for 30 minutes?”

There was no time to stay confused.

Before they could ask more questions, projectiles shot from the front.

Bang-bang-bang-bang-bang-!

The projectiles, like bullets, hit everyone squarely in the chest.

Each and every one.

“Ugh, w-what was that?”

“Black bullets?”

Bang-bang-bang-bang-!

Looking in the direction they came from, the projectiles were being fired at
regular intervals from the other side of the hall.

As if bullets were being shot every 2 seconds.

Bang-bang-bang-bang-!

“We have to endure this for 30 minutes?”

“It’s not too painful, but it’s unsettling.”

The projectiles hit the chest every 2 seconds.

It felt like being lined up for a firing squad.

Unpleasant, but bearable.

It stung like being hit by a BB gun.

For those with high defense, it barely registered.

“Nothing to worry about.”

“If it stays like this, we can manage.”

“Don’t get too comfortable. Things can change quickly.”

“Yes, did you hear? The damage increases over time.”

“Oh, but if it’s this little damage at the start, we’ll be fine.”

“I’m a tank anyway, so no worries.”

Some worried, others reassured, and some even showed arrogance.

But they all shared one common ignorance:

Enduring pain was harder than they thought.

‘They call it enduring pain, but in other words, it’s enduring torture.’

Right now, the damage was minor, so many were confident, but their
expressions would change after just 10 minutes.

‘In 10 minutes, they’ll be too overwhelmed to make a sound. By the 20-
minute mark, they’ll be screaming for mercy.’

Imagine being pierced by a sharp needle every 2 seconds. No one could
hold out for long.

‘After 5 minutes, it’ll feel like they’ve been stabbed 150 times. By the 25-
minute mark, most will be on the verge of collapse.’

Of course, this applies to those with average defensive gear. Tanks might
hold on a bit longer, but even they would struggle to last the full 30
minutes.

‘Before that, many will start leaving their positions, unable to bear the
pain.’

For now, the atmosphere was calm, but after 10 minutes, some would try to
hide behind others.

Then, the person in front would take double the hits they were supposed to,
effectively becoming a human shield.

‘That will lead to inevitable conflict. In the chaos, people might end up
fighting each other while bullets continue raining down. Everyone
scrambling for survival will add to the confusion.’

The scene would become pure pandemonium.

Just wait for 10 minutes.

‘There’s a reason this round is called the “Extreme 15th Round.” Only
fewer than 50 people ever made it through.’

Even the strong ones like Tae-seok, Russell, and Jo Yong-ho had failed at
this round.

Christine, too, had not survived.

‘I remember back in the 11th round, I saved Christine from John Delgado’s
summon by chance, but unfortunately, she died trying to save others here.
Her wide-area healing skill left her defenseless, leading to her death.’

The moment Christine died, hundreds of others quickly succumbed, unable
to withstand the pain.

They all fell like a dam breaking.

Once she was gone, people started using each other as shields, leading to
more deaths.

Only those with strong defensive abilities like Ma Kyung-rok, An Sang-
cheol, and a few other tanks and grand wizards survived.

‘Without healing, it’s nearly impossible to pass this round.’

That’s why Christine’s role in this mission was crucial.

‘This time, things will be different. I’ll make sure Christine stays alive, no
matter what.’

About 5 minutes had passed.

The damage was now enough to be bothersome, and some people started
using emergency treatment skills.

“Using emergency treatment helps a bit.”

“Let’s all hang in there together!”

“Can this be avoided?”

“I tried, but it’s too fast to dodge.”

The projectiles were faster than bullets, making them impossible to dodge.

Hiding behind someone else was the only way to block them.

Bang-bang-bang-bang-!

At around the 8-minute mark, the damage increased again.

Expressions around the room noticeably darkened.

Less than 10 minutes had passed, but people were beginning to feel the
strain.

It was then that Christine activated her wide-area healing skill.

Swish—

A soft, green glow, like the light of fresh sprouts, enveloped everyone,
soothing their pain.

It was a large-scale, continuous healing skill called [Sanctuary], affecting
everyone within a 500-meter radius.

“Th-this is…”

“The pain is fading.”

“A Priest’s skill!”

The healing range was wide enough to include all 1,152 players, thanks to
Christine positioning herself in the center.

“Everyone, stay in place! I’ll keep healing you!”

The continuous healing effect restored health with every passing second,
washing away pain. The skill’s healing power was far superior to
emergency treatments.

While the crowd calmed down, Christine’s own face grew pale.

She had excluded herself from the healing effect.

“Ugh, it hurts…”

“Don’t worry.”

A warm light wrapped around Christine’s wounds.

“I’ll protect you.”

Ryu Min, standing beside her, placed a supportive hand on her back.

Thanks to his temporary skill, Christine’s injuries were quickly healed.

Although her pain disappeared, she didn’t have time to dwell on that.

‘W-what do I do…?’

Her heart pounded so wildly, it felt like it might burst.

Chapter 250: Shield Bearer (1)

‘Why is she embarrassed?’

Whether Christine was embarrassed or not, Ryu Min focused solely on
protecting her.

If she collapsed, thousands of others would fall too.

‘It wouldn’t even take a few minutes before we’re all wiped out.’

This was why healers were crucial in this round.

Some of the other players seemed to understand this as well, offering
grateful nods to Christine.

It wasn’t just nods; some even spoke directly to her.

“You’re the one healing us now, right?”

“Thank you, Miss Chrissy.”

“Are you a healer? Your recovery is insane!”

Christine had no time to respond.

Losing focus or stopping on her own would immediately interrupt her
Sanctuary skill.

And if it stopped, she’d need to wait 30 minutes to cast it again.

‘That’s why Christine’s role is so important.’

Determined to protect her at all costs, Ryu Min infused healing into her
back.

“Uh, Mr. Black Scythe?”

“What?”

“Could you take your hand off my back…?”

“It’s much faster to heal when I’m touching an area close to the wound.
Didn’t you know?”

“Oh…?”

Christine’s eyes widened in surprise, seemingly unaware even as a healer
herself.

“Thanks for the tip.”

“So stop worrying about unnecessary things and just focus.”

“Yes…”

Although she answered, Christine still seemed embarrassed.

Tupapapapapapa-!

“Ugh!”

“Argh!”

Fifteen minutes had passed, and groans started to come from all around.

It was the time when everyone could definitely feel the increased intensity
of the pain.

Shwaaaa—

But as soon as they received the Sanctuary’s effect, their expressions turned
peaceful, as if the pain had never happened.

Without Christine’s healing, they would have collapsed from exhaustion in
this phase.

Christine, who had also received Ryu Min’s healing, was in the same
situation.

‘The pain… it’s completely gone.’

A surprised Christine looked at Ryu Min beside her.

“Mr. Black Scythe. Are you using the Emergency Treatment skill right
now? Why is it so effective?”

“It’s not Emergency Treatment, it’s just a heal.”

“What? A heal?”

‘It’s not an ordinary heal thanks to the Rune of Radiance.’

Healing was a holy-type skill.

The Rune of Radiance doubled the efficacy of holy-type skills, so the
recovery was extraordinary.

‘Besides, I’m timing the heal right when Christine takes damage, so she
probably doesn’t even feel the pain.’

It was a method he devised to minimize pain.

Other players, without this coordinated healing, had to endure alternating
pain and recovery.

“Ugh, this hurts more than I thought.”

“But with the heal, it’s bearable.”

“This mission is easier thanks to Chrissy the healer.”

“Let’s hold out for just 15 more minutes!”

Voices of encouragement and determination echoed from all sides.

They were confident they could clear this round if Christine’s healing
continued without interruption.

But Ryu Min’s expression remained serious.

The damage would increase to an absurd level as they moved forward.

‘Continuous healing won’t be enough. The incoming damage will be too
overwhelming.’

At the three-minute mark, damage so severe it rendered healing ineffective
would strike every two seconds.

At that point, there would be no room for the current sense of calm.

Even if they received healing.

‘This round was designed with the assumption that people would receive
healing. That’s why it’s called “Pain Endurance.”’

Especially in the last 10 seconds, the damage would be unbearable.

Even with healing, more than half the players would inevitably die.

‘Unless they’re wearing highly defensive gear or guzzling multiple potions
like me, they won’t survive.’

Wearing the Black Armor of Thanatos, Ryu Min had an impressive 88%
chance to deflect bullets.

Originally, it was 67%, but thanks to the set bonus and Russell’s gear
reinforcement buff, the effect increased by 1.32 times.

‘Most bullets deflect off me, so I’m taking almost no damage…’

Others, however, would soon begin to experience hell.

Even Ryu Min, during his first time clearing 15 rounds, had nearly lost his
mind.

It wasn’t just like being pricked by needles—it was more like being carved
with knives.

‘Nobody else will survive the last 10 seconds unless I block for them.’

Ryu Min’s mind drifted to an item in his inventory.

The Elixir of Super Regeneration he had received in the 8th round.

‘It wouldn’t matter if I was alone, but to save others, I need this elixir.’

To prepare for the 20th round, as many people as possible had to survive.

It would come at the cost of tremendous pain, but he was ready to make that
sacrifice.

[Time remaining until the end of the round: 00:09:58]

Twenty minutes had already passed.

They only had to endure for 10 more minutes, but screams began to fill the
air, signaling that many were reaching their limits.

Tupapapapapapa-!

“Aaaah!”

“It hurts!”

Pain that felt like being pierced by an awl came and went.

Normally, it would be too much to endure, but thanks to the continuous
healing, they could manage.

Of course, those with weaker mental fortitude were already at their
breaking points.

“Ugh…”

“Hold on, Chrissy. Whatever happens, don’t pass out.”

“Yes…”

Christine gritted her teeth and held on, but not everyone had her mental
strength.

“Aaaah!”

One man subtly slipped behind another, causing the person in front to take
the brunt of two bullets instead.

“H-hey! What are you doing? Aaah! Get back here! Urgh!”

“I’m sorry. I need to rest; this pain is too much.”

“Get back in your spot! Aagh!”

The difference between taking one bullet and two was massive.

But the man, unconcerned, abandoned his position and used others as his
shield.

‘Haha, this doesn’t hurt at all. Should’ve done this sooner…’

The man’s thoughts ended abruptly.

A winged ghost appeared before him and slashed his throat.

Thud

The man fell, unable to leave any last words, as his body crumpled
lifelessly.

The bullet that was meant for him vanished in an instant.

The person who had been shielding him showed visible relief.

Watching this, Ryu Min’s lips curled into a smile.

‘Well done, John Delgado.’

Before the round began, Ryu Min had given John Delgado specific
instructions.

If anyone tried to flee, execute them without hesitation.

‘Trying to use others as a shield just to save yourself? Such scum doesn’t
deserve to live.’

It was better to eliminate such individuals early on; they only caused chaos
and problems.

“Hey! Come back!”

“Because of you, I’m taking two bullets!”

“What are you doing behind my—!”

Slash-!

Swish-!

Swish-!

When others tried to flee, Sariel stepped in, swinging his scythe.

The sight of the Angel of Death cowed everyone into silence, though he
turned away without further action.

Sariel’s message was clear: he wouldn’t touch those who didn’t flee.

When around a hundred bodies piled up, people no longer tried to leave
their positions.

They didn’t hide behind others anymore.

Anyone with a brain could tell: leaving their spot meant immediate death at
the hands of a scythe-wielding specter.

‘It worked.’

With Sariel patrolling like a warden, everyone gritted their teeth and held
out.

No more defectors emerged.

Chapter 250: Shield Bearer (2)

‘It worked.’

With Sariel patrolling like a warden, everyone gritted their teeth and held
out.

No more defectors emerged.

[00:05:08]

Tick—

[00:04:32]

Tick—

[00:03:28]

Tick—

They lasted until the three-minute mark without anyone breaking rank, but
it would get much harder from here.

Now, the true agony would begin.

“Everyone, listen to me!”

Ryu Min shouted, directing his voice to the whole group.

Although they could only see those next to them, they strained to hear the
voice of the Black Scythe.

“If you want to live, get behind me! Form a single line—exactly one line!”

“A line?”

“You know I have the strategy for this mission. If you want to survive,
cooperate now!”

When people hesitated, Ryu Min roared again.

“What are you waiting for? Move, now!”

There was no need to ask why.

It was the Black Scythe speaking; there was no reason to doubt him.

Thud-thud-thud

The crowd quickly formed a line behind him.

Although they used him as a shield, Sariel did not react.

It was as if he had no intention of interfering.

‘Phantom undead are immune to physical damage, but they can’t block
bullets.’

Sariel’s role had ended here.

Now it was up to him to protect everyone using his body.

Tupapapapapapap-!

The bullets converged into a single point as everyone lined up.

They all targeted the person at the front—Ryu Min.

Clang-clang-clang-clang-clang-!

Most bullets deflected due to the 88% chance granted by his armor.

Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!

He also used a barrier formed with the Dark Rune to block hundreds of
incoming bullets.

Ryu Min glanced at the countdown timer.

[Time remaining until the end of the round: 00:00:28]

Only 30 seconds remained.

Looking back, not everyone had managed to get in line.

It took longer than expected for a thousand people to organize.

“Christine!”

“Yes?”

“There’s no time. Get behind me now.”

“But if I do that, Sanctuary will…”

“It’s not needed anymore. Just get behind me now!”

People stepped aside to let Christine through.

The Sanctuary that had been healing everyone suddenly stopped.

Thud-thud-thud!

Dozens of bullets struck Ryu Min’s body from among the hundreds.

The pain was immense, but he kept a neutral expression as he used his
healing skill to mend the wounds.

‘I need to take the elixir at the exact right moment. That’s the only way I’ll
survive.’

Christine, now behind him, placed her hand on his back and used healing as
well, hoping he wouldn’t fall.

‘Please, stay strong.’

Finally, everyone was lined up.

With a thousand people in a single file, every attack was directed solely at
Ryu Min.

Tupapapapapapap-!

He summoned another barrier of darkness, but it shattered almost instantly.

Clang-clang-clang-clang-clang!

Even though his armor deflected most bullets, about a hundred still pierced
his body.

‘Ugh, not yet… not yet.’

17 seconds, 16 seconds, 15 seconds…

Just a little longer.

He had to take the elixir exactly at the 10-second mark.

If he missed by even a second, he would die.

‘At the 10-second mark, the damage spikes dramatically.’

The other players still didn’t know why the Black Scythe was acting as their
shield.

They simply followed because he ordered it.

But when the last 10 seconds came, everyone finally understood.

Why he was standing at the forefront, shielding them.

Thudthudthudthudthudthudthud!

The sound of the powerful bullets alone was terrifying.

If they had been hit, they would have been obliterated.

Everyone realized that, and a collective shiver ran down their spines.

They worried if the Black Scythe, taking all the shots, would survive.

Would he disappear without a trace?

Thankfully, that concern never materialized.

Ryu Min had timed it perfectly, using the elixir as the bullets struck.

[You have used the Elixir of Super Regeneration.]

[For 10 seconds, your regenerative power will increase dramatically.]

Almost immediately, darkness-infused bullets pounded his body.

His skin tore and his organs were battered, but his wounds mended as if
nothing had happened.

The transcendent power of Super Regeneration healed every injury
seamlessly.

Thudthudthudthudthudthudthud!

Even as a hundred bullets struck him, Ryu Min stood tall.

Thudthudthudthudthudthudthud!

Acting as a human shield, he absorbed the brunt of the attack for everyone.

Summoning another dark barrier was futile—it shattered like glass, letting
the bullets strike him directly.

But none of them could pierce him completely.

Each wound was instantly healed by his unparalleled regenerative ability.

[Time remaining: 8 seconds.]

[Time remaining: 7 seconds.]

…

…

Though the countdown continued, he barely registered it.

Those 10 seconds felt like an eternity.

Grit!

He clenched his teeth, enduring the pain.

Even at the edge of passing out from the agony, Ryu Min held on with
superhuman willpower.

He endured and endured again.

Thudthudthudthudthudthudthud!

Although his body regenerated, the pain was all his to bear.

Ten seconds felt like ten hours.

He silently wished for time to pass faster.

He knew he couldn’t last much longer.

‘No, I can’t collapse yet.’

He steadied his wavering mind and braced against the onslaught, both
physically and mentally.

Thudthudthudthudthudthudthud!

The final barrage of bullets tried to tear his body apart but failed.

As his wounds healed, a message rang in his ears.

[The Elixir of Super Regeneration has expired.]

Chapter 251: Authority (1)

Ten seconds passed.

Ryu Min’s blurry eyes suddenly opened wide.

“Is it over?”

He had managed not to lose consciousness.

Thanks to the Elixir of Rapid Regeneration, he was able to protect the lives
of over a thousand people.

Ryu Min instinctively turned his head.

Hundreds of pairs of eyes were looking at him with admiration.

They were people who would have all died if Ryu Min had not stepped
forward.

“Black Scythe…”

“Oh, my god…”

Some of the followers, including Huh Tae-seok, were looking at him as if
they had seen a deity.

Some even clasped their hands together and prayed.

Christine’s eyes were filled with awe as well.

As if she were witnessing the reincarnation of a god who sacrificed himself
for humanity.

[The time limit has expired.]

[You have successfully completed the third mission.]

[Survivors: 1,048, Deaths: 104.]

[Congratulations! You have completed the main quest!]

[You will be relocated shortly for the final calculation.]

It was a welcome notification, but no one could bring themselves to smile.

The bloodstains around Ryu Min were overwhelming.

Perhaps because they understood the cost of the sacrifices made, no one
dared to celebrate openly.

Ryu Min, noticing the somber atmosphere, spoke in a calm tone.

“Why is it so quiet? Don’t hold back; you can rejoice.”

“But, Black Scythe, your condition…”

“You don’t have to worry about me. I may look like this, but I’m fine. And
even if I were injured, it wouldn’t matter. Just saving so many lives is
enough for me.”

“Oh…”

“Black Scythe…”

Moved by his magnanimity, people looked at him with admiration.

With just a few words, he had solidified his image as a savior.

‘Having a good reputation isn’t a bad thing,’

Smiling kindly and savoring the moment, a welcome notification appeared
before him.

[A hidden sub-quest has been discovered!]

Take the most damage during the third mission.

Reward ▶ Rune of Sacrifice.

[You have completed the sub-quest!]

[You have been granted the Rune of Sacrifice as a reward!]

[The acquired rune will automatically be engraved on the player’s body!]

‘As expected, I got it. The sub-quest reward.’

Although Ryu Min had stepped forward to protect others, his true goal had
been this sub-quest reward.

[Rune of Sacrifice]

Effect: Designate one target within a 100-meter radius to take their damage
on yourself.

The damage taken will decrease based on the caster’s defense.

The effect can be deactivated at will. However, if the target leaves the
range, the effect will automatically deactivate.

‘Rune of Sacrifice. Not a bad rune.’

No, it was actually excellent.

It was one of the 18 essential runes he had to acquire.

‘There’s no better rune for protecting someone.’

The rune allowed him to take damage on behalf of the designated target.

It was, quite literally, a sacrificial rune.

‘If I apply it to someone important in the party, like Christine, I can protect
them perfectly.’

While it meant taking Christine’s damage onto himself, Ryu Min wasn’t
concerned.

The damage would scale according to his defense.

‘As long as I can endure it, Christine will essentially become invincible.’

It was a great rune, but it wasn’t the only reason he had cleared the sub-
quest.

‘This round’s sub-quests are more important than ever.’

The reason would soon be revealed by the angel.

Shortly after, the scenery blurred, and the players returned to a
monochromatic space one by one.

[Well, how was the mission? Was it harder than… you thought?]

The angel’s smiling face froze as she saw the over one thousand survivors.

[So many of you survived? I only expected about a hundred at most…]

‘A hundred? That’s being generous. Normally, less than fifty survive,’ Ryu
Min thought, smirking inwardly as he looked around.

In his 100 regressions, he had never seen a sight like this.

Never before had there been this many people alive after the 15th round.

[Let’s see… 1,048 survivors? How did so many survive? This is beyond
expectations!]

The angel’s shock mirrored the players’ feelings from moments earlier.

They hadn’t expected Black Scythe to shield them, sacrificing himself like a
living barrier.

“Black Scythe…”

“Black Scythe truly is our savior.”

People looked at Ryu Min with such expressions.

Feeling the weight of thousands of gazes, Ryu Min thought of what he still
had to do.

‘Those looks of admiration will soon turn to hatred.’

He sighed inwardly as the angel made a shocking announcement.

[You may not know this, but there was a hidden sub-quest in this round.
The player who took the most damage during the third mission was the
winner. Not surprising, right?]

This wasn’t shocking, as sub-quests were included in almost every round
except the 1st and 6th.

The real surprise came next.

[But this sub-quest is different. Unlike other rounds, the winner of this sub-
quest gains authority. What kind of authority, you ask?]

The angel grinned wickedly.

[The authority to determine the rankings of the players.]

“What? Rankings of the players?”

“What does that mean?”

Seeing the confusion, the angel laughed and explained.

[Until now, rankings were based on performance metrics, and rewards were
distributed accordingly. But this round is different. The winner of the sub-
quest gets to assign the rankings for 2nd to 576th place personally.]

“What…?”

“Personally assign rankings?”

[In other words, the one who sacrificed the most now holds the power of
life and death over others. Isn’t that ironic?]

It truly was ironic. The one who endured the most sacrifice was now in
control of others’ fates.

People were stunned, feeling as though their heads were spinning.

Chapter 251: Authority (2)

[In other words, the one who sacrificed the most now holds the power of
life and death over others. Isn’t that ironic?]

It truly was ironic. The one who endured the most sacrifice was now in
control of others’ fates.

People were stunned, feeling as though their heads were spinning.

[Let’s see who won… The player who took the most damage is…]

The angel’s eyes widened.

[Black Scythe? Over two trillion damage taken…?]

The angel was genuinely astonished.

[Now I see how so many survived. Did you really take all that damage on
your own?]

Ryu Min remained silent. There was no need to dignify the angel’s sarcasm
with a response.

[But it’s a shame. Half of you will still have to go.]

Only 576 players could survive. That was the harsh reality.

[Now, Black Scythe, you have been granted the power over others’ lives
and deaths.]

As soon as the angel finished speaking, a message appeared.

[The winner of the 15th round sub-quest is ‘Black Scythe.’]

[You have been granted the authority to adjust the rankings for the 15th
round.]

[Your rank (1st place) cannot be changed.]

[Assign rankings for 2nd to 576th place.]

[2nd and 3rd place receive special rewards. The rest will receive equal
rewards regardless of their rank.]

[Please speak the name of the player you wish to designate as 2nd place.]

Ryu Min stared at the message.

In his hands lay the fate of everyone else.

He turned to look at the hundreds of eyes staring back at him.

Unfazed by the pressure, Ryu Min made his decision.

“Christine.”

[2nd place: Christine.]

[Please designate 3rd place.]

“Min Juri.”

[3rd place: Min Juri.]

Special rewards were granted up to the 3rd place, and Ryu Min made these
decisions without hesitation.

‘Christine and Min Juri contributed the most; they deserve it.’

Beyond this, there was no special meaning to the rankings. From 4th to
576th place, the order didn’t matter. What mattered was simply being
included in the list.

Whether you were 4th or 576th, the outcome was the same.

‘The real issue lies in who gets to be part of the 576 and who doesn’t.’

[Please designate the 4th place.]

“Seo Arin.”

[4th place: Seo Arin.]

[Please designate the 5th place.]

Ryu Min continued calling out names without hesitation. These were the
players he considered most crucial to his strategy: key allies, dependable
fighters, and those who had supported him.

“Russell.”

“Jo Yong-ho.”

“Victor.”

“Sophia.”

“Yamti.”

He filled the upper ranks quickly with his main allies. From 4th to 400th, he
prioritized those who had helped him or were part of his trusted team.

‘I’ll naturally include the followers of the Death Church who put their faith
in me.’

Thanks to this, he reached the 400th spot without much deliberation.

[Please designate the 401st place.]

This was where the real dilemma began.

‘Who should I save next?’

For the first time, Ryu Min hesitated. He fell into deep thought.

The remaining 176 slots would decide who lived and who died. The
difference between being included and excluded was the boundary between
salvation and despair.

As he deliberated, the players who weren’t yet chosen grew restless.

“Black Scythe! Please, save me!”

“Me too! Please add me to the list!”

“Who pushed me? Move! I can’t see!”

A mass of desperate players crowded closer to Ryu Min. Though they dared
not get too close due to his intimidating aura, they raised their voices,
pleading for salvation.

“Please, save me. My mother is waiting for me at home. She’ll be
devastated if I don’t make it.”

“Family? I’ve got a newborn baby waiting for me!”

“I’m the father of twins! If I die, my whole family will starve!”

“I’ve got quadruplets!”

“Stop spouting nonsense!”

The shouting turned into chaos, with some players even grabbing at each
other’s collars in frustration. Nearly 600 people scrambled and fought to
plead their case for survival.

Their desperate cries echoed in the monochromatic space. All dignity was
forgotten.

‘This is what people are like when their lives are on the line,’ Ryu Min
thought, watching the chaos unfold.

Among the crowd, however, a few stood apart, maintaining their
composure. Ryu Min’s gaze landed on one of them.

‘That’s… Archmage Alex.’

Alex, a renowned player in his previous regressions, stood silently, exuding
an aura of calm authority. In the past, only two players besides Ryu Min had
survived up to the 19th round: Ma Kyung-rok and Ju Seong-tak.

‘By the 18th round, there were seven survivors excluding myself.’

Ma Kyung-rok and Ju Seong-tak were two of them. The remaining five
included Min Juri, Yamti, Victor, and…

‘Alex, and the one over there… Dorothy.’

Dorothy, known as the Divine Archer, also stood quietly among the crowd.
She and Alex were among the few who had reached the later rounds,
exceptional talents from foreign regions.

‘Alex was German, and Dorothy was Dutch. I never had the chance to get
to know them properly in my previous regressions.’

Ryu Min had only heard about Alex’s prowess as the Archmage and
Dorothy’s reputation as the Divine Archer.

‘This time, I’ll make sure to keep them close.’

Ryu Min’s voice rang out clearly, cutting through the noise of the crowd.

“Alex.”

[401st place: Alex.]

[Please designate the 402nd place.]

Alex flinched, startled to hear his name called. He hadn’t expected to be
chosen.

“Dorothy.”

[402nd place: Dorothy.]

Dorothy’s reaction was similar. She, too, was taken aback by Ryu Min’s
choice.

Ryu Min continued calling out names. By now, his priorities had shifted. He
had already secured all the vital people he needed.

‘The rest… I’ll pick based on my gut.’

From 403rd place onward, he quickly scanned the remaining players, trying
to gauge their personalities and potential value. He focused on saving those
who seemed decent and trustworthy.

As the numbers climbed closer to 576, tension among the remaining players
reached its peak.

By the time only one spot remained, chaos broke loose.

“Please! Black Scythe! I’ll do anything you ask! Just let me survive!”

“I’ll swear eternal loyalty to you! Just give me one chance!”

“Don’t leave me behind! Please, I’m begging you!”

Some fell to their knees, crying and pleading. Others resorted to screaming,
shouting promises, and even swearing loyalty.

But Ryu Min remained unmoved. He had already made his decision.

The final survivor… Ryu Min’s gaze fell on a single person.

Chapter 252: End Of The 15Th
Round (1)

“John Delgado.”

[Rank 576 is ‘John Delgado.’]

[All 576 survivors have been determined.]

[Remaining players will be automatically eradicated.]

“W-wait! Eradicated?”

“I don’t want to die! I don’t want to die!”

“Black Scythe, you bastard! You said you’d save me!”

“You f***er! I’ll curse you even in hell!”

“Enjoy your life, you son of a bi…”

The words were abruptly cut off.

Fzzz!

All that remained was a wisp of ash, dissipating into the air at the molecular
level.

‘Seeing him cursing like that, I’m glad I didn’t choose him.’

Although he had earned the hatred of hundreds, Ryu Min’s expression
remained composed.

Truthfully, he would have preferred to advance to the next round with a
thousand players, but the system made that impossible.

‘In past rounds, fewer than 50 survived, so there was no one to eliminate…’

This time, however, the survivors outnumbered the capacity, leaving him no
choice but to cut some out.

It felt like pruning the branches of a tree.

‘I’m sorry. But to clear the 20th round, this was necessary. I had no choice
but to prioritize those who could help us win.’

Among them, John Delgado was a priority.

Saving him would grant an extra reward, making it worth the decision.

The reason Ryu Min pretended to hesitate before choosing was simple.

‘It was Christine. I didn’t want her to catch on.’

Ryu Min subtly turned his head, only to see Christine staring at him blankly,
as expected.

Why would the Black Scythe… choose to save John Delgado?

Reading her thoughts, it was clear that she couldn’t understand the decision.

Ryu Min could empathize with her reaction.

‘After all, from her perspective, I’ve essentially saved her mortal enemy.’

He resolved to explain later, then shifted his gaze. Min Juri and Seo Arin
were nearby.

‘Will the Black Scythe be alright? The burden must have been
overwhelming…’

‘Deciding with your own hands who lives and who dies… I could never do
it.’

Both were secretly worried about him, but there was no need.

Having witnessed countless deaths, Ryu Min had grown desensitized.

‘Compared to that, deciding who to erase myself isn’t such a big deal.’

He had long since accepted that the system’s rules were immutable.
Resistance was futile.

His gaze eventually landed on the members of the Death Church.

‘Phew, I survived. That was close.’

‘If not for the Death Church, I would’ve been erased, no question.’

‘Joining this sect was the best decision of my life.’

Without exception, the members were all relieved, grateful that their
association with the sect had saved their lives.

[Finally, all 576 survivors have been chosen. Congratulations to those
selected by the Black Scythe.]

Ryu Min narrowed his eyes slightly.

Somehow, Milen, the angel, sounded like she was mocking him.

When their gazes met, Milen flinched, quickly looking away and clearing
her throat awkwardly.

Even angels knew the truth.

That the one who had killed an Archangel was none other than the Black
Scythe.

[W-well, shall we review the results?]

★ 15th Round Results ★

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

└

└1st Place: Black Scythe (Lv95, Grim Reaper)

└2nd Place: Christine (Lv65, Priest)

└3rd Place: Min Juri (Lv65, Buffer)

The rankings weren’t based on performance but on connections, yet the
rewards were calculated without issue.

[As a reward for clearing the 15th round, all survivors have been granted
experience and gold.]

[EXP +237.9%]

[Gold +1,000,000]

[You have leveled up!]

[You have leveled up!]

Ryu Min gained two levels, but others gained as many as four or five, with
most nearing level 70.

[Congratulations! You have achieved the quest as the top player in this
zone!]

[Your current rank in this zone is 1st place.]

[As a 1st place reward, you have been granted the ‘Infinite Materials
Pouch!’]

[As a 1st place reward, you have been granted the ‘Special Reward
Selection Box!’]

Among the rewards, the Infinite Materials Pouch stood out.

It was an item that could dispense up to five random materials upon use.

However, for someone like Ryu Min, who already possessed god-tier
equipment, materials weren’t particularly useful.

‘I can’t hold onto it without using it, though.’

Unused rewards came with a penalty—they would vanish if not used before
the next round.

‘I’ll open it after I return. It’ll probably just give me materials I don’t need.’

If they turned out to be useless, he could give them away or use them to
craft something for someone else.

‘But the Special Reward Selection Box is mine to use.’

When he activated the box, a list of options immediately appeared.

[Please select one of the following special rewards:]

[Tap the reward you desire.]

└1. Temporary Skill – Sweeping Strike (16th Round Only)

└2. Temporary Skill – Clairvoyance (16th Round Only)

└3. Information on the 16th Round

Two temporary skills were among the choices this time.

Sweeping Strike was a passive skill that transformed a weapon into an area-
of-effect damage dealer upon learning it.

‘A skill perfect for wiping out hordes of enemies.’

However, it was unnecessary for Ryu Min, who could already widen the
area of effect of his attacks using the Scythe of Thanatos.

‘Given the circumstances, there’s only one real choice.’

He selected Clairvoyance, a skill he had used effectively during the 11th
round in the gambling den.

‘Though it won’t be as crucial this time, it’ll still be useful in the 16th
round.’

With no better options, it was the logical choice.

◀ Round 15 Complete ▶

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

└Survivors: 576

[Your soul will soon return to your physical body in the current dimension.]

[The 16th round will commence at midnight on April 1, 2023. Until then,
congratulations on surviving.]

Upon returning to reality, the general public was shaken as they read the
news:

[Breaking News! Only 576 players remain worldwide after the 15th round.]

[In just 14 months since the Great Cataclysm, the number of players has
dropped from 1.8 billion to just over 500.]

[Among the 576 remaining players, 174 are from South Korea.]

The drastic reduction in player numbers startled many. While some viewed
this as good news, others saw it differently:

└This isn’t good. Fewer players mean there are fewer people to fight
against the monsters.

└Looks like the era of players dominating everything is here.

└If players team up and run wild, who could stop them?

└

└True. Shouldn’t there be some kind of countermeasure for this?

Negative opinions existed but remained in the minority.

Most people weren’t overly concerned.

That was because the players were under control—thanks to one person.

└Why worry? The Black Scythe is here.

└Exactly. He’s punished every criminal player so far.

└If I were a player, I wouldn’t dare commit a crime. Just the thought of him
is terrifying.

└But is the Black Scythe really that strong? What if all the players gang up
on him?

└What do you think will happen? They’d all get destroyed.

└I heard there’s still a huge level gap. The highest other players can get is
around level 69, but he’s already at level 97.

└Anyway, as long as we have the Black Scythe, there’s no need to worry.
South Korea has 174 players left, and they’re all part of the Death Church,
so they’ll follow his orders.

└Hey, what’s the Death Church?

└It’s a religion created by the Black Scythe. But it’s more like a community
for players to band together.

└Oh, like some player fan club?

└Fan club? Forget it. Player communities like that are pretty much dead
now.

└Still, 174 out of 576 players being from South Korea… I didn’t expect our
country to be such a player powerhouse. LOL.

└

└And, by the way, the Death Church wasn’t created by the Black Scythe. It
was founded by some guy named Heo Tae-seok. It’s not just a name; it’s an
actual religion. The Black Scythe is worshipped as a god there. Get your
facts straight before you comment.

└Wait, it’s an actual religion? I didn’t know that.

└Stop talking nonsense. The Black Scythe is no god—he’s just a man. And
who the hell is Heo Tae-seok, anyway?

└Heo Tae-seok is no nobody. He’s a level 69 dark sorcerer, founder, and
leader of the Death Church.

└Who cares about Heo Tae-seok? Don’t tell me anything about him.

└Let it go. That commenter must be Heo Tae-seok himself.

At that moment, Heo Tae-seok’s hand hesitated over the keyboard.

Feeling exposed, he debated whether to delete his comment. Ultimately, he
decided against it.

“Why should I delete it? It’s true.”

Chapter 252: End Of The 15Th
Round (2)

At that moment, Heo Tae-seok’s hand hesitated over the keyboard.

Feeling exposed, he debated whether to delete his comment. Ultimately, he
decided against it.

“Why should I delete it? It’s true.”

Heo Tae-seok let out a long sigh, looking as dejected as someone nursing a
heartbreak.

Strictly speaking, his dejection wasn’t over a person—it was over a god.

‘No matter how much I think about it, I just don’t understand. What is the
Black Scythe thinking…?’

The fact that he had given everything in the 15th round to help the Black
Scythe was a source of pride for him.

At that moment, Heo Tae-seok was ecstatic, overflowing with joy.

But his excitement was short-lived.

When he saw his ranking, the euphoria quickly dissipated.

“I’m in 10th place? Me, 10th place?”

He hadn’t dared to hope for 2nd or 3rd place.

To be honest, he had secretly hoped for a top-three position.

After all, he was the founder and leader of the Death Church.

As the Black Scythe’s “right-hand man,” wasn’t that reasonable?

‘No, I should be realistic. I can’t be greedy. I didn’t do enough in the 15th
round to justify that rank.’

He admitted that 2nd place Christine’s Sanctuary skill played a huge role in
completing the third mission.

Similarly, 3rd place Min Juri’s buffs had been crucial to succeeding in the
first and second missions.

Given their contributions, aiming for 2nd or 3rd place was absurd.

“But why was I pushed all the way down to 10th place?”

He understood that rankings had no practical significance, but still, it hurt
his pride.

Being ranked 10th felt like he had been forgotten—like he didn’t matter as
much.

‘To the Black Scythe, what am I? Did my efforts mean anything to him?’

Even though he was ready to lay down his life for the Black Scythe, the
rewards he received in return felt disproportionately small.

The only tangible benefit he had received was the relocation of the Death
Church’s headquarters from a rural area to Seoul.

‘Hmm… when I think about it, that building is worth hundreds of millions.
And he also provided 100 million won a year for operational costs.’

While it seemed like adequate compensation on the surface, in reality, it felt
less so.

The building wasn’t technically his—it was more like borrowing a space.

The operational funds? Barely enough to cover the basics.

Most of the money went toward supporting and managing the Death
Church’s members and maintaining the building, leaving Heo Tae-seok with
little for himself.

‘I’m not asking for material rewards.’

He wasn’t expecting grand compensation.

What he wanted was simple recognition.

Acknowledgment of his efforts and validation of his role as a leader.

“Should I just accept being 10th?”

As Heo Tae-seok grappled with his feelings of disappointment, he suddenly
froze, startled by his own thoughts.

How could he—a mere servant—feel resentment toward a god?

Slap! Slap!

He slapped himself across the face, trying to suppress his wavering faith.

“Unworthy… I am unworthy. My faith is lacking…”

“What’s lacking?”

Startled by the sudden voice, Heo Tae-seok whipped around.

Standing there was Cardinal Em Jun-seok.

“What are you mumbling about, Leader?”

“Ahem, it’s nothing.”

“This isn’t the time for idle thoughts.”

“What’s going on?”

“Some visitors have arrived at the Death God Sect. Follow me.”

Without further explanation, Em Jun-seok led the way, and Heo Tae-seok
followed him, confused.

It wasn’t a time when worshippers usually gathered, so who could it be?

‘Huh?’

As they stepped outside into the courtyard, they saw a group of people—ten
in total.

All foreigners.

‘Who are these people?’

Had they heard rumors about the Death Church and come for a tour?

At first, he thought so, but he quickly realized otherwise.

Several of them were equipped with player items.

“They’re players?”

“Is this the temple of the Black Scythe?”

Since the translation system only worked in the otherworld, Heo Tae-seok
couldn’t understand them.

“Cardinal Em, what are they saying?”

Fortunately, Em Jun-seok spoke English.

“Wait a moment.”

After a brief exchange, Em Jun-seok turned back, his face full of surprise.

“They said they want to join the Death Church.”

“All of them?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

After another exchange, Em Jun-seok relayed their response.

“They said they survived the last round thanks to the Black Scythe choosing
them. They were also deeply moved by his self-sacrifice and are determined
to join.”

“Haha…”

Given the dwindling number of players, welcoming new members to the
sect could only be a good thing.

The Black Scythe had already made it clear—new members were always
welcome.

“Very well. Let’s arrange an interview. I’ll call the Black Scythe.”

Welcoming ten new members was a blessing, but Heo Tae-seok had no
idea.

This was just the beginning.

Soon, all 175 players saved by the Black Scythe would come flocking to
join.
