Chapter 253: Integration (1)

Ryu Min received word that the foreign players he had rescued wished to
join him.

Although it seemed their gratitude for saving their lives motivated their
decision, Ryu Min thought otherwise.

‘They must’ve realized it by now—sticking with me significantly increases
their chances of survival.’

His actions during the 15th round, particularly how he looked out for the
members of the Death Church, likely reinforced their desire to join. Perhaps
they also believed he would reveal the strategy for the next round.

‘In any case, this is good. Unifying all players under the Death Church is
the ideal scenario.’

Collaboration would be critical in the upcoming quests, making it vital to
rally the players into a single group. The Death Church offered the perfect
means for this unity.

‘Let’s see how far things have come.’

As Ryu Min stepped into the Death Church’s courtyard, all eyes
immediately turned to him.

Understandably so—after all, a man in a white mask walking around in
reality was a rare sight.

“It’s the Black Scythe!”

“Black Scythe!”

Thanks to his heavy exposure in the media, people recognized him at a
glance.

“Huh, Sect Leader.”

“You’ve arrived, Black Scythe.”

“Why are there so many people here? Didn’t you say there were only about
ten on the phone?”

“They multiplied before I knew it. Haha…”

Roughly twenty individuals were gathered in the courtyard, all players of
diverse nationalities.

“Alright. Let’s proceed with the interviews.”

“Yes, sir.”

Tae-seok promptly turned away, giving Ryu Min no chance to read his
thoughts. Ryu Min merely sat at the designated spot and prepared to
conduct the interviews.

“Those wishing to join, please form a single line.”

At Em Jun-seok’s words, the crowd moved in perfect order.

“Greetings. I am Cardinal Em Jun-seok. I’ll distribute these application
forms. Please read through them and check the consent box. It would also
help if you filled in some personal details.”

Once they had diligently completed their forms, the players approached the
masked man one by one.

With fluent English, Ryu Min asked, “You want to join the Death Church?”

“Yes, sir!”

“Why?”

“I was deeply moved by your sacrifice during the last round. I felt I could
trust and follow you without hesitation…”

The man listed his reasons at length, but Ryu Min knew the truth lay
elsewhere.

“To survive, I have to stick to Black Scythe.”

Despite knowing their real motives, Ryu Min did not reject them. After all,
seeking shelter under the strong for survival was a perfectly human
reaction.

“Your membership is approved.”

“Th-thank you!”

The man’s character didn’t seem bad, so Ryu Min granted his request
without much fuss.

“Next.”

As the interviews continued, new players kept arriving. Some appeared as if
they had boarded a plane to Korea the moment they woke up, lining up like
sausages in a row.

‘The 15th round must have shaken them to their core.’

The growing number of recruits was a good thing, so Ryu Min continued
the interviews without complaint.

Two days passed like this.

Ryu Min informed his brother he wouldn’t be home and decided to stay at
the Death Church’s quarters. Since new applicants kept showing up
whenever he tried to rest, he conducted interviews day and night.

By the third day, over 150 new players had joined.

‘Might as well aim for 25 more to round it off.’

With 25 more recruits, practically every player in the world would be part
of the Death Church. Among them, he particularly hoped to recruit the

archmage Alex and the divine archer Dorothy.

‘I need to bring at least those two aboard.’

Although he briefly considered the possibility that they might not come, he
dismissed the thought.

‘No, they have no choice if they want to survive the next round.’

Ryu Min waited patiently.

By midday, a group of players finally arrived.

“Is this the Death Church?”

“It is. Are you here to join?”

“Yes. Could we meet Black Scythe?”

“Of course. Please fill out this application form, and you’ll have a one-on-
one interview with him.”

The man handed his completed form to Ryu Min, whose pupils
momentarily trembled as he read the details.

[Name: Alex Pearson]

[Nickname: Alex]

[Nationality: Germany]

[Level: 69]

[Otherworld Class: Archmage]

[Age: 25]

[Date of Birth: September 24, 1997]

[Reason for Joining: Survival.]

‘So this is Archmage Alex?’

The man’s chubby frame and glasses made him look far from the sleek
figure he had envisioned.

“Your nickname is Alex?”

“That’s correct.”

“Why do you wish to join the Death Church?”

“I’ll be honest. I think I stand a better chance of surviving with you, Black
Scythe.”

It was a reminder not to judge people by their appearance. While Alex’s
physique suggested laziness, the determination in his eyes was
unmistakable. And there was no need to question his talent.

“Very well. You’re approved.”

“…”

Stunned by how quickly he had passed, Alex stared at Ryu Min in disbelief.

“What are you waiting for? Make way for the next applicant.”

“Ah, um, before I leave, may I ask a question?”

The earnestness in Alex’s gaze suggested this was something he had long
wondered about.

“Go ahead.”

“Why did you call my name during the 15th round?”

‘Because I know you’ll survive until the 18th round.’

Ryu Min couldn’t say that out loud. For now, he was Black Scythe, not a
prophet.

“For no particular reason.”

“Pardon?”

“You just caught my eye. That’s all.”

“Ah…”

Though surprised, Alex wasn’t disappointed.

“So that’s it? I guess I overthought it.”

Accepting the answer calmly, Alex maintained a positive outlook. True to
form, his character was as reliable as ever.

“Thank you for your answer. I’ll see you around.”

“Take care.”

Chapter 253: Integration (2)

Accepting the answer calmly, Alex maintained a positive outlook. True to
form, his character was as reliable as ever.

“Thank you for your answer. I’ll see you around.”

“Take care.”

After Alex left, a few more interviews followed. Finally, someone Ryu Min
had eagerly anticipated appeared.

[Name: Dorothy Clayton]

[Nickname: Dorothy]

[Nationality: Netherlands]

[Level: 69]

[Otherworld Class: Archer]

[Age: 22]

[Date of Birth: December 24, 2000]

[Reason for Joining: Out of respect for Black Scythe.]

‘She’s here—Dorothy, the divine archer who survives until the 18th round.’

While the archer class was common, surviving with such a class was no
small feat.

“You’re approved.”

“Pardon? But you haven’t asked me anything yet.”

“I already know enough.”

Without further ado, Ryu Min approved her application.

Thus, in just three days, all 175 players rescued by Ryu Min had joined the
Death Church.

The Death Church now held every surviving player in the world.

‘This is perfect.’

Now came the crucial part: ensuring the survival of his recruits while
navigating the rounds ahead.

As soon as the last applicant left the Death Church’s headquarters, Heo Tae-
seok and Em Jun-seok approached Ryu Min.

“Thank you for your hard work, Black Scythe.”

“You too, Sect Leader Heo. And you as well, Cardinal Em Jun-seok.”

“Thank you, Black Scythe.”

For a brief moment, Heo Tae-seok’s expression shifted subtly, but Ryu Min
had already turned his head away.

“I’ll be leaving now. Take some time to rest until I contact you again.”

“Understood. Safe travels, sir.”

“Very well.”

With that, Ryu Min unfurled the wings on his back and soared high into the
sky.

On his way back home, he suddenly paused and descended onto a nearby
building’s rooftop.

“I need to meet Min Juri. I can’t keep avoiding her.”

It was high time to mend their relationship. Returning to their old
camaraderie was crucial to avoiding complications during future rounds.

Tap, tap, tap.

His fingers moved quickly across his phone, typing a text message. A reply
arrived shortly after.

[Min Juri: Sure, let’s meet.]

The short response left Ryu Min feeling a little uneasy.

“I should bring something to ease the awkwardness. Maybe a crafted item?”

Rummaging through his inventory, he recalled he had been meaning to use
the Infinite Material Pouch for some time.

“A god-tier item is out of the question without Aether, but a legendary-tier
item should be enough to impress her.”

With his sky-high luck stat, he was confident in obtaining excellent
materials.

[You used the Infinite Material Pouch.]

[Congratulations! You’ve obtained 5 material items!]

[The items have been added to your inventory.]

As he inspected the materials, Ryu Min tilted his head in confusion.

“Not a single legendary-tier material? And what are these unfamiliar ones?”

To his dismay, there wasn’t even a god-tier material among them, leaving
him unable to craft a legendary item for Juri.

“Well, nothing I can do about it.”

Slightly disappointed, Ryu Min took off, heading to their agreed meeting
place.

---

Meanwhile, in a Different Dimension.

Rumble.

A dimensional portal opened, revealing an enormous repository of
knowledge—the Akashic Records.

[Welcome, Michael.]

[Greetings, Luvaiah.]

The archangel Michael entered the grand space, his expression grim.

[There’s a problem.]

[Is it about the Demon Resurrection Codex?]

[You’re well-informed, I see.]

[Are you worried about the gods’ wrath?]

[No.]

Michael shook his head decisively. The gods’ anger could be pacified
eventually, but this was not the issue weighing on him.

[That’s trivial. The real problem is that the gods want Black Scythe
captured before the 18th round.]

[Understandable. Giving the demon duke a reason to intervene isn’t
something they’d want. For the gods, his involvement would ruin their
game.]

[Do you have a solution?]

[…]

[I skipped the 15th round to buy time, but there are no excuses left. If I
delay any further, Gabriel and Raphael will grow suspicious.]

[In that case, the only option is to strike Black Scythe during the 16th
round.]

[Do you mean I should be involved personally?]

[What would you do? Pretend to lose and retreat?]

[…]

[If you fail, the gods will doubt your competence. Instead, send Gabriel and
Raphael.]

[You want me to send both?]

[Raphael isn’t a combat specialist, but in this case, you’ll need them both.]

[That pair is practically invincible together.]

[Don’t worry. If Black Scythe’s abilities are as formidable as we’ve
observed, he’ll be able to fend them off.]

Michael’s eyes widened slightly in surprise.

[Is Black Scythe truly that powerful? Even now?]

[Yes. He’s slain numerous angels already—don’t you think it’s time to have
faith in his strength?]

[Still, Gabriel and Raphael are on a different level. If Black Scythe isn’t
careful, he could be killed.]

Luvaiah smiled faintly, a silent assurance.

[Believe in Black Scythe, Michael. The scenario you fear will never
happen.]

Volume 6

Chapter 254: Doubt (1)

Ding-a-ling—

Ryu Min opened the door to the café and glanced around.

Seeing Min Juri sitting there, he raised his hand slightly in greeting.

Sitting across from her, he felt slightly relieved by the determined look in
her eyes.

‘Thankfully, she seems okay.’

She wasn’t lowering her head or avoiding his gaze as before. Instead, her
eyes carried a determined confidence, as if she was ready to tie up loose
ends.

“You already ordered my coffee? Thanks.”

“It’s nothing.”

“…….”

“…….”

The awkwardness between them lingered.

Although Ryu Min was the one who rejected her confession and suggested
they remain friends, he never thought it would be easy.

‘If we keep meeting like this, things will gradually improve. Juri doesn’t
seem to want to leave things awkward between us either.’

That must be why she so readily agreed to meet him today.

“Min-ah.”

“Yeah?”

Juri fell silent after being called. Her lips quivered slightly as if she was
internally debating something. After a moment, she seemed to make up her
mind and spoke.

“You told me before that you wanted us to remain friends, right?”

“I did.”

“I was honestly confused back then, but now I’ve made up my mind.”

Her eyes sparkled with determination.

“Let’s stay friends. But…”

She dropped her gaze slightly, as if embarrassed.

“Let’s pretend my confession never happened. Can you do that?”

“Of course. Absolutely.”

Did he answer too quickly?

Juri’s eyebrow twitched slightly, her expression showing a hint of bruised
pride.

Before any misunderstandings could deepen, Ryu Min added quickly.

“I might have answered too fast, but don’t misunderstand. It’s not that your
confession didn’t mean anything to me. Forgetting it completely would be
impossible. But if that’s what you want, I’ll do my best…”

“No.”

Her eyes flared with pride.

“I’ve changed my mind.”

“Huh?”

“Don’t forget it. Don’t erase it from your memory. I confessed to you, and
you rejected me. That’s the truth, isn’t it?”

Her voice trembled slightly. It felt like she was speaking impulsively, driven
by hurt pride.

“Let me be honest. I haven’t given up yet. The reason I agreed to remain
friends is because I don’t want to lose you. Think about it. Do feelings fade
so easily? I still… like you.”

Her voice softened as she finished, and her gaze dropped to the table.

“I’m not going to give up. I’ll make you like me. So let me stay by your
side as a friend. And give me a chance to become something more. That’s
how I truly feel. Can you at least do that for me?”

“…….”

Ryu Min’s lips didn’t part easily. He wasn’t hesitating because he was
thinking of rejecting her.

‘Rejection isn’t an option. I can’t lose my buffer.’

He was just caught off guard by her raw sincerity.

“Alright.”

“Huh?”

“Do as you like.”

“Really?”

“One way or another, we’re friends.”

“…….”

Though his words drew a boundary, Juri didn’t back down. She recalled the
advice of the Black Scythe: ‘Keep challenging him.’

“That’s enough for me.”

Finally, a smile spread across Juri’s face.

“That settles it, right?”

“Yeah.”

“Good. Now let me tell you about the strategy for the 16th round.”

To change the atmosphere, Ryu Min hurriedly shared the strategy details.
During his explanation, Juri’s eyes widened.

“Is the next round really going to play out like that?”

“Yeah. So you need to be careful and try not to get caught up in it. The
Black Scythe will probably gather his followers soon to share the strategy.”

“You told the Black Scythe about the future?”

“I did.”

“I was wondering if you two share information…”

“We’ve always shared information.”

“Then why does the Black Scythe use his rewards to gain information about
the next round? He could just ask you.”

“I can’t predict the future at will. If there’s a round I can’t foresee, the Black
Scythe uses his rewards to fill in the gaps.”

It was a bold-faced lie, but Juri nodded as if it finally made sense.

“That’s a relief. I was worried you two might not get along…”

‘Not get along? We’re practically one and the same.’

He couldn’t reveal his true identity to her yet. Right now, it would only
create unnecessary problems.

‘If she finds out I’ve been deceiving her all this time, she might feel
betrayed.’

There was nothing to gain from revealing the truth, so he kept it tightly
hidden.

“Sorry about earlier.”

Juri’s sudden apology made Ryu Min tilt his head.

“For what?”

“For… losing my cool.”

“It’s okay. Don’t worry about it.”

From Ryu Min’s perspective, he was just glad they seemed to be back on
friendlier terms.

‘Technically, it’s different.’

In a way, he had given her another chance while putting her confession on
hold.

“But Min, you’re part of the Death Church too, right?”

“Huh? Yeah, I am. Why?”

“I haven’t seen you around much lately.”

“I’m just a nominal member. If people found out about me, it would cause
problems.”

“True. If they knew you were a Prophet, they’d cling to you.”

“Exactly.”

Juri sipped her coffee and studied him with curious eyes.

“If you have any more questions, just ask.”

“Oh, it’s nothing… But were you called by the Black Scythe in the 15th
round? Your nickname was Lost Yak, right?”

“Huh? Oh, yeah.”

“Then why don’t I remember hearing it?”

‘Because I never called that name.’

Ryu Min replied calmly.

“You probably didn’t hear it. Otherwise, how would I still be alive?”

“Hmm, I guess so…”

Since it was impossible to remember all 576 names, Juri brushed it off
without suspicion.

“Shall we wrap up now?”

“Sure.”

Outside the café, the two exchanged a wave.

“Thanks for the strategy details. Let’s meet again soon.”

“Sure. I’ll stay in touch.”

Chapter 254: Doubt (2)

Outside the café, the two exchanged a wave.

“Thanks for the strategy details. Let’s meet again soon.”

“Sure. I’ll stay in touch.”

As he walked away, Ryu Min thought to himself.

‘Thank goodness. Juri seems to be in a good state of mind.’

It seemed she had taken the Black Scythe’s advice to heart.

Though her declaration to keep pursuing him felt a bit burdensome…

‘At least it’s better than awkwardness.’

For the upcoming rounds, Juri needed to be mentally stable. A rejection
lingering in her mind would only hold her back.

‘Especially in the 16th round. She’ll need to stay sharp.’

A small mistake could have massive consequences in that round.

‘After the 16th round, players’ value will skyrocket. The public perception
will change too.’

The Death Church’s reputation—and even in reality, runes—would become
highly coveted.

‘I should gather the Reaper Church members soon and share the strategy.
But first, I need to clear things up with Christine.’

She likely misunderstood why he saved John Delgado. And Christine, like
Juri, was a crucial supporter who needed emotional stability.

Ryu Min pulled out his phone and called Christine.

“Christine.”

—“Ah, Black Scythe?”

“I’ll get straight to the point. I want to meet to discuss the next round’s
strategy.”

—“Uh… Can’t we do this over the phone?”

“Phone calls aren’t secure enough.”

—“I thought so…”

“Why? Is there a reason you can’t meet?”

—“N-No, not at all…”

“Then I’ll come to you. A quiet church is the best place to talk privately.”

—“No need… I’ll—”

“I’ll fly first class, so don’t worry. I’ll call once I arrive.”

Ryu Min preferred moving rather than waiting idly.

‘Time to explain things properly.’

He thought as he booked a ticket to the U.S.

---

Christine sat frozen with her phone in her hand.

Her face was etched with fear—not excitement.

‘Could he have noticed? Could he have figured it out?’

Christine had a suspicion—one she couldn’t voice.

That the Prophet and the Black Scythe… were one and the same.

‘No, it’ll be fine. I’ve hidden it well over the past few days. I didn’t show
any signs in the otherworld either.’

She had tried her best not to reveal anything, but she knew the truth deep
down. Or rather, she suspected it.

No, suspicion was too weak a word now.

‘The Prophet and the Black Scythe are the same person…’

It was a dangerous assumption. An absurd one, even.

‘Who would ever match the frail-looking Prophet with the terrifying Black
Scythe?’

Their images were polar opposites, and no one could have made that
connection.

But Christine had her reasons for believing it.

When the Prophet had come to America recently, Christine had witnessed
something.

A killing.

While being carried on his back.

‘He used his abilities to kill the thugs pointing guns at us.’

At that time, she had been in a hazy state and wasn’t very surprised. She’d
thought it was a dream and went back to sleep.

‘When I woke up, I was in the church.’

The Prophet was gone by then.

Later, she wondered if it hadn’t been a dream after all, but there was no
evidence left at the scene.

‘And I couldn’t connect it to the Black Scythe at the time.’

But in the otherworld, when she saw the Black Scythe using his shadow
abilities, her thoughts changed.

‘Maybe… maybe what I saw that day wasn’t a dream. Maybe the Prophet
and the Black Scythe are the same person.’

Of course, it was all just suspicion and conjecture. There was no concrete
evidence.

‘No, it can’t be. There’s no way… Their abilities might just be similar.
Their images don’t overlap at all.’

Christine muttered to herself, her face full of unease.

She didn’t even notice someone entering her detection range.

“What’s ‘no way’?”

“Eek!”

Christine flinched, her shoulders jumping as Jeffrey appeared silently.

“Why are you so startled? You look like you’ve seen a ghost.”

“N-No, it’s nothing.”

“You don’t look fine. Did something happen?”

“It’s nothing. Really.”

Christine firmly shut him down, but Jeffrey only grew more suspicious.

“Come on, I know something’s up. If something’s bothering you, just tell
me. I’ll listen.”

“I said it’s nothing.”

“Are you still mad at me?”

“Who’s mad? I’m not mad at you!”

“If you keep denying it like that, do you think I won’t notice? I’ve been
watching over you for over ten years now.”

“……”

“Come on, tell me. What’s bothering you?”

Faced with Jeffrey’s persistence, Christine let out a long sigh. She felt she
had to say something to get him off her back.

“If someone who seemed weak turned out to be hiding immense power,
what would you do?”

“Hiding power? Who?”

“I asked first. Answer me.”

“Hm…”

Jeffrey thought for a moment before replying.

“I’d pretend not to know.”

“Why?”

“Because if they’re hiding it, it means they don’t want others to know. If I
respect them, I shouldn’t expose their secret.”

“Right… That’s what I thought too.”

Christine’s expression softened slightly. It was comforting to hear someone
share her perspective.

“So, who’s the secret powerhouse? Someone you know?”

“Don’t call them a ‘powerhouse.’ Watch your words!”

“Oh? You’re defensive. Must mean you care about them.”

“That’s enough! I’m not telling you anything. Stop asking. Problem
solved!”

With that, Christine quickly stood and walked away, her steps hurried as if
fleeing the scene.

“Hm…”

Jeffrey watched her retreating back with a suspicious look.

Then, he pulled out his phone and typed a message.

[To Yamti: There’s something unusual going on.]

He had been ordered to report immediately if anything out of the ordinary
happened.

Chapter 255: A Secret Between
Two (1)

On his way to Incheon Airport to meet Christine, Ryu Min received an
important phone call.

“Christine suspects me?”

— Yes. I definitely heard it from Jeffrey.

It was about the possibility that the Prophet and the Black Scythe might be
the same person.

“Understood. I’ll handle the rest myself.”

— Alright. Please be careful, Master.

“What a load of nonsense.”

Ryu Min hung up the phone with a faint laugh. But his expression quickly
turned serious as he fell into thought.

‘Christine suspects me…’

This wasn’t something to take lightly.

‘How did she find out? I haven’t done anything suspicious lately… Oh!’

A scene suddenly flashed in his mind.

When he killed the three thugs targeting Christine using the Dark Dagger.

‘It must have been then. I thought she was asleep because I couldn’t read
her thoughts… Was she awake?’

Despite his caution, it seemed she had found out about his actions.

‘This is troublesome. It’s not ideal for anyone else to know my true identity
yet…’

He’s been living a double life until now. If he admits that both identities are
the same, Christine might feel a sense of betrayal. She might even turn
away from him, feeling deceived.

‘Christine turning her back on me… Just imagining it is dreadful.’

Without Christine’s help, he’d essentially lose one of his resurrection
chances. In this final regression, Christine’s abilities were indispensable.

If he admitted the truth, their relationship would surely deteriorate.

He had to deny it, no matter what.

‘The problem is, what excuse should I use…?’

Even as he arrived at the airport and prepared to board his flight to the US,
he couldn’t come up with a suitable excuse.

‘I’ll just have to flat-out deny it. Worst case, I could use the Memory
Erasure Potion.’

It felt wasteful to use such a valuable potion for this, but he had two. Using
one might not be too much of a loss.

‘Sigh… I don’t know. I should try to sleep.’

But Ryu Min couldn’t catch a wink of sleep on the flight to the US.

---

“Christine.”

“Black Scythe!”

Christine greeted the masked Ryu Min with a bright smile. But he could tell
immediately.

‘It’s true. I can feel it when I read her thoughts.’

Behind her warm facade, her mind was filled with suspicion.

‘She suspects that I’m the Prophet.’

She was also nervous, possibly because she had witnessed him kill
someone.

‘I get it. From her perspective, it must have been terrifying. I acted
nonchalantly while killing three people.’

When he read her thoughts, it seemed she had somewhat rationalized his
actions. After all, the thugs had pointed a gun at her. But she didn’t know
the full details.

“Was the journey difficult?”

“No.”

In truth, he hadn’t been able to sleep a wink because of his worries.

“I could have come to see you instead…”

“No need. I was free anyway.”

“Let’s not talk here. It’s not even prayer time, so this place isn’t ideal for
conversation. Let me take you to a quieter spot.”

Christine began leading him to the chapel, but Ryu Min stopped her.

“No, an open space like the chapel won’t do. We need somewhere more
private where our conversation won’t be overheard.”

“Oh… In that case…”

After a moment of hesitation, Christine spoke.

“I have a room where I stay… Would you like to go there?”

“Lead the way.”

---

Christine’s room was cozy and equipped with a private bathroom.

“Th-this is my room.”

“It’s tidy.”

Christine blushed faintly, possibly embarrassed about bringing a man into
her personal space.

Ryu Min glanced around and remarked:

“There’s only one chair.”

“Ah, y-you’re right. Please wait, I’ll bring another one!”

Christine quickly dashed out and returned with a chair.

After placing the chair, Ryu Min quietly locked the door.

Click—

The faint sound of the lock seemed to echo in the small room. The
atmosphere grew subtly awkward.

But Ryu Min, as always, spoke calmly.

“Do you know why I’m here?”

“To share information about the 16th round strategy…?”

“That’s one reason. But there’s another.”

“Another reason?”

“To clear up a misunderstanding.”

Christine’s heart skipped a beat.

‘Does he know I suspect him?’

But Ryu Min’s words had a different meaning.

“I wanted to explain why I summoned John Delgado.”

“Oh…”

Christine’s expression shifted, indicating genuine curiosity.

“I was surprised, honestly. You saved John Delgado in the 15th round. I
wondered if you forgot about my history with him.”

“Of course not. I was the one who saved you from him, remember?”

“Then why did you save him? The man who tried to kill me?”

“Because John Delgado is now under my control.”

“What?!”

Chapter 255: A Secret Between
Two (2)

“Because John Delgado is now under my control.”

“What?!”

“I recently took control of him. He’s my subordinate now.”

In truth, it was through a duel, not direct control. But the result was the
same.

“Why…?”

“The Prophet told me that a necromancer’s abilities would be useful in the
future. That’s the only reason.”

Though the prophecy was a lie, the reasoning was valid. Christine seemed
to accept it.

“So, the undead attack in the second mission of the 15th round… Was that
your doing too?”

“Yes. I gave the necromancer orders to make that happen.”

“Oh, so that’s why you told us to stand by…”

Christine nodded in realization. The explanation had worked.

But Christine still seemed hesitant, her mind filled with lingering doubts.

She finally spoke:

“Black Scythe, could you show me your shadow ability one more time?”

“Why?”

“I can’t explain in detail, but… I need to confirm something. Please.”

Her serious expression left Ryu Min with no room to refuse.

“Fine.”

Using the Rune of Darkness, he created a shadowy barrier.

“This is the same ability you used to block bullets, right?”

“Correct.”

“Can you transform it freely? For example, into something sharp for an
attack?”

Ryu Min hesitated. He could lie, but if he ever used Dark Dagger in front of
her, it would backfire.

“Yes, I can.”

He summoned a dagger formed from shadows.

Christine’s thoughts raced.

‘It’s exactly like the Prophet’s ability… Could it be…?’

Despite her suspicion, she had no concrete proof.

Christine took a deep breath and asked directly:

“Are you… the Prophet?”

Ryu Min was about to deny it. But then, the Rune of Future Sight activated.

He saw Christine’s disappointed face in the future.

‘She actually wants me to be the Prophet?’

“Yes.”

Christine’s eyes widened.

“You… you’re admitting it?”

“Yes. I am the Prophet.”

With those words, Ryu Min removed his mask and revealed his true
identity.

Christine’s eyes widened in shock as Ryu Min’s body began to transform.
His build grew smaller, his facial structure changed, and his true appearance
as the Prophet was revealed.

“Oh my god!”

Christine gasped and instinctively jumped up from her seat.

“You… You’re really the Prophet?!”

“Shh. Keep your voice down. Someone might hear.”

Ryu Min, now fully in his true form, gave her a wry smile.

“I guess you’re quite shocked.”

“S-shocked doesn’t even begin to describe it… You can change your
appearance?!”

“It’s nothing that strange. If you can bring people back to life, is
transforming my appearance that surprising?”

“I-I suppose that makes sense.”

Christine, now slightly more composed, examined him with an almost
incredulous expression.

“So, this is the real you?”

“Yes, this is my true form. What you’ve known as the Prophet is my actual
identity. The other one—Black Scythe—is a facade.”

“I see…”

Christine’s gaze lingered on him, her disbelief slowly fading into
understanding.

“You look… different from what I imagined under the mask. I suppose this
means you’ve been hiding your true self all this time.”

“Exactly. I had my reasons. And now you know the truth.”

Christine hesitated, her thoughts racing. Her instincts told her there was
more to this revelation than he was letting on.

“Why are you telling me this now? Why reveal this to me of all people?”

Ryu Min looked her directly in the eye and answered without hesitation.

“Because I don’t want to lose you.”

“W-what?!”

Christine’s face turned a deep shade of red at his unexpected response.

“What do you mean by that?”

“Exactly what I said. Christine, you’re an essential part of my plans. You’re
a valuable ally, and I trust you. I couldn’t keep lying to you and risk ruining
our relationship. That’s why I’m telling you the truth.”

Christine stared at him, stunned. It was as if she had just been confessed to,
though not in the way she had ever imagined.

“So… You’re not going to kill me, right?”

Ryu Min let out a chuckle.

“Kill you? Of course not. If I wanted to do that, I wouldn’t have gone to the
trouble of revealing my identity. Besides, I’ve already protected you once,
haven’t I?”

“Protected me?”

“The thugs who pointed their guns at you—they were targeting you
specifically. They demanded I hand you over or else. I couldn’t allow that,
so I dealt with them first.”

Christine’s eyes widened as the truth dawned on her. The incident that had
initially sparked her suspicion had actually been Ryu Min protecting her.

“You… did that for me?”

“Of course. You’re too important to lose.”

Christine’s doubts began to melt away. What little fear remained was
replaced by a growing sense of trust and gratitude.

“So, can you believe me now? That I have no intention of harming you?”

“Yes… I believe you now, Black Scythe—no, Prophet.”

“Stick to calling me Black Scythe for now. Officially, that’s the identity I’m
using. My true identity should remain a secret for the time being. Can I trust
you to keep it that way?”

“Of course. I’ll keep it a secret. You can count on me.”

Ryu Min nodded, reassured by her response. He shared with her the full
strategy for the upcoming 16th round before preparing to leave.

“That’s all you need to know for now. I’ll be on my way.”

As he turned to leave, Christine called out to him hesitantly.

“Black Scythe…”

He glanced back, his expression curious.

“Yes?”

“Thank you… For saving me back then, and for being honest with me
now.”

A faint smile played on Ryu Min’s lips.

“If you’re thankful, keep my secret safe.”

“I will. I promise.”

With that, Ryu Min activated his wings and soared into the sky. Christine
watched him disappear, her heart swelling with a mixture of emotions she
couldn’t quite put into words.

“I’m glad… that I’m someone important to him.”

With a shy smile, she turned and headed back toward the chapel.

A few days later, the 16th round began.

Chapter 256: The Start Of The
16Th Round

March 31, 2023, 11:50 PM.

Ten minutes before the start of the 16th round.

Five hundred seventy-six players from around the world stared nervously at
the countdown.

Most were silent, but some chatted with each other to ease their nerves.

“I’m nervous.”

“Yeah, me too.”

“Do you think things will go as the Black Scythe said this time too?”

“Of course. Ever since we joined the Death Church, everything he predicted
has been right.”

From the 13th round up to now, Korean players who had joined the Death
Church received strategies in advance for the upcoming rounds.

Because of this, they felt no anxiety or fear—except for the recently
recruited foreign players.

“Excuse me. Can you speak English?”

A foreign believer approached and asked. A Korean player nodded.

“Yes, I can speak English. You joined after the 15th round, right? Your
nickname is…”

“Just call me Alex.”

“Nice to meet you, Alex. My nickname is Babbeojeoji (Rice Bug). Do you
have any questions?”

“I’m still a bit confused… Does the Black Scythe always share strategies
like this?”

“Yes. We joined after the 12th round, and since then, we’ve always received
the strategies.”

“That’s how we’ve survived so far. Haha.”

“You heard the strategy for the 16th round too, right?”

Alex nodded.

“Of course. That’s why I’m here.”

“But you don’t look too reassured. Are you still worried?”

Alex answered honestly.

“Yes, I am.”

“Haha, don’t worry. We all felt like that at first, wondering what if the
strategy was wrong.”

“But now, we just gratefully accept the information. You’ll feel the same
soon enough, heh.”

Despite the reassuring tone, Alex’s face still showed unease.

“Do you trust the Black Scythe?”

The sudden question made the players laugh.

“If we didn’t trust him, what else could we do? We’ve already joined the
Death Church.”

“Just relax and wait. There’s no way out of here anyway.”

Alex sighed, realizing the truth in their words.

“You’re right. That was a silly question. Thanks for the reassurance.”

“No problem.”

As Alex turned away, he observed the other followers of the Church.

The long-time believers looked calm and confident, while the newcomers
were visibly tense and anxious, despite having received the strategy.

‘They’re probably like me… They just don’t have full faith in the Black
Scythe yet.’

Alex had joined because sticking with the Black Scythe seemed like the
best chance of survival. But trust? That was a different matter.

‘We all just instinctively sided with the stronger faction to survive.’

Trusting someone you barely know was impossible.

‘The idea of getting information about the next round as a first-place
reward… is that even possible? Actually… maybe it is.’

It was hard to believe. The idea that strategies were handed down through
membership in a cult seemed absurd.

‘The only way to know for sure is to win first place myself…’

But now wasn’t the time for such thoughts.

The time had come.

“One minute left until midnight!”

With tense expressions, everyone waited for the final minute to tick away.

Was it because they knew what was about to happen? The tension felt
heavier than ever.

5, 4, 3…

2, 1…

When the clock on their phones struck midnight and switched to April 1st,
the players’ consciousnesses were supposed to transfer to another world.

Soul Transference.

A technology capable of transcending dimensions requires only a fleeting
moment.

But instead of seeing vast meadows or a desolate monochrome space—

“Huh?”

“It’s the same.”

They were still in the same place they had been before.

“We didn’t move.”

“The Black Scythe was right.”

Normally, their bodies would have transformed into avatars, and their
surroundings would have changed completely.

But this time, nothing happened.

No avatars. No dimensional transfer. They remained in their original bodies.

The players murmured among themselves, caught between confusion and
relief.

The Black Scythe’s prediction had been accurate.

[Hehehe. I can just imagine how confused you all must look right now.]

A beautiful, melodic voice echoed in their heads.

But the source was the vile angel, its voice drilling into their minds.

[Hello, 576 players. Surprised to hear me like this? Or are you more
shocked that you’re still on Earth? Pfft.]

The angel’s smug expression was almost visible through the tone of its
voice.

[You must’ve thought you escaped the death game. Sorry to disappoint you,
but no. You can’t leave until you clear the remaining five rounds. Hehehe.]

Scowls spread across the players’ faces. With no angel in sight, there was
no need to hide their expressions.

“F***ing angel bastard.”

Some players muttered curses aloud. The angel, as always, continued
speaking as if it couldn’t hear them.

[Shall we check the 16th round mission now?]

As soon as the voice stopped, a translucent screen appeared before
everyone.

◀ ROUND 16 ▶

Exterminate all monsters summoned to the human world within 3 hours.

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

Participants: 576

Clear Condition: 0/288

Most players would normally panic after reading the quest, but they
remained calm this time.

After all, they had already received the Black Scythe’s briefing.

The angel laughed, unaware of this.

[Surprised? This round is unique. Instead of another world, it’s set on Earth.
That’s why your souls didn’t transfer. Exciting, right?]

“Shut up.”

[Oh, and since you’re on Earth, there are no avatars. You’ll have to fight
with those pathetic real bodies of yours. But don’t worry—you can still use
your abilities.]

“Crazy angel bastard.”

[Because this round is set on Earth, I’ll only communicate with you through
my voice this time.]

The angel continued explaining.

[Monsters will spawn every 30 minutes for a total of six waves. The number
of monsters will scale with the number of players. Oh, and…]

The rest of the rules were similar to what the players had already heard
from the Black Scythe.

Waves of increasingly powerful monsters. The number of monsters
corresponding to the player count.

But one detail stood out:

[Monsters will spawn randomly within a 100-meter radius of each player’s
current position. In other words, wherever you are is effectively a spawn
point.]

“Our location is a spawn point?”

“That’s exactly what the Black Scythe said.”

[So don’t worry about searching for monsters. Just keep an eye on your
surroundings.]

If players were spread out, that meant monsters could spawn worldwide.

[Oh, one more thing: monsters will harbor intense hostility toward humans,
whether they’re players or civilians.]

The angel’s voice dripped with mockery.

[This round might keep you pretty busy if you want to minimize civilian
casualties. Hehehe.]

It was as the angel said. If monsters spawned randomly, civilians could
become unintended victims.

[Well then, let’s begin. Good luck, everyone. Pfft.]

The angel’s laughter faded away.

But instead of fear, the players’ faces were filled with relief.

They were on an isolated island with no civilians in sight.

“Whew, thank goodness.”

“The Black Scythe was right. Coming to this island was the best choice.”

“Otherwise, people could’ve been hurt.”

Among them stood Ryu Min, wearing his mask.

‘At least my brother is safe.’

If he had been lying in bed like usual, his entire city could have been
thrown into chaos by spawning monsters.

‘But starting here on an isolated island ensures no civilian casualties.’

The players could relax, knowing their loved ones were safe.

But Ryu Min knew something they didn’t.

‘This round isn’t just about monsters… Battle Angels will appear too.’

Chapter 257: Choice (1)

In his first attempt at reaching the 16th round during his 68th regression,
Ryu Min fought against the battle angels.

‘No, it wasn’t a fight. It was a massacre.’

At that time, ten battle angels had appeared.

Their purpose was simple.

‘They aimed to stand on the side of the monsters and obstruct the players.’

It was the first time that angels, who had previously never interfered with
quests, had intervened.

‘It was absurd and frustrating.’

Their sudden interference was frustrating, and their unexpected weakness
was baffling.

Of course, if they had used Shisal, Ryu Min wouldn’t have been able to
resist and would have died instantly.

‘But back then, the angels couldn’t use Shisal.’

From what he had gathered, Shisal couldn’t be used in the 16th round.

The reason was unknown.

‘It’s probably a restriction set by the system to maintain balance. With
Shisal, anyone can be killed in one strike.’

The reason for the angels’ obstruction was unclear.

What mattered was that they couldn’t use Shisal.

For Ryu Min, who didn’t have the Supreme Being title at that time, this was
a stroke of luck.

‘It was ridiculously easy. Not only did they lack Shisal, but they were
merely sixth-class battle angels.’

A sixth-class angel was roughly equivalent to a max-level player with
standard gear.

At the current level of 70, five players could probably take down one.

‘But I did it alone.’

Ryu Min in the 68th regression was strong.

Strong enough to massacre ten sixth-class angels alone.

‘After killing all the angels, an archangel appeared.’

The archangel, presumed to be ranked first in the angelic hierarchy, neither
threatened nor attacked Ryu Min.

Ryu Min, overwhelmed by his strength, couldn’t even think of challenging
it.

‘It just said some cryptic words and left. I can’t quite remember what it
said.’

This time, sixth-class angels would probably appear again.

They would only show up during the final sixth wave, so there was still
plenty of time.

“Those foolish angels didn’t expect us to be gathered on the island, did
they?”

“Lord Black Scythe predicted it correctly this time too.”

“If we hadn’t come to the island beforehand, who knows what would’ve
happened to our families…”

“It’s all thanks to Black Scythe. Thank you!”

The followers of the Death Church around him each expressed their
gratitude toward Ryu Min.

Even Alex, who had initially seemed skeptical of Ryu Min’s strategy, now
had a look of trust in his eyes.

‘Good. It seems I’ve earned the trust of the newcomers.’

The new followers would now truly dedicate themselves to him after this
event.

That included Alex standing before him.

Behind his mask, Ryu Min’s lips curled into a satisfied smirk.

But then…

‘Huh?’

His expression stiffened as he noticed Min Juri conversing with Alex.

He knew she was searching for the Prophet.

---

“Here, have some buffs.”

Min Juri raised her hand, casting a set of three buffs on a group of
followers.

“Ooh, thank you so much!”

Nodding politely, Min Juri quickly turned to another player.

With 576 players gathered here, she had no time to rest if she wanted to
buff everyone.

At that moment, she noticed a player standing alone.

An obvious foreigner.

Using slightly awkward English, she greeted him.

“Hello? Are you new here?”

“Yes. My name is Alex.”

“I’m Democracy. May I have a moment?”

Alex seemed puzzled but quickly fell silent as Min Juri cast the three-buff
set: Bless, Swift, and Safety Barrier.

“Th-this is…”

“They’re buffs. They’ll be useful for you. I’m busy, so I’ll move on…”

Leaving Alex staring in awe, Min Juri began scanning the crowd.

‘Where is he?’

All the players across the world had been united under the Death Church.

Among them was the Prophet class, Ryu Min.

‘But I don’t see him anywhere?’

She had buffed everyone, scanning each face carefully, but Ryu Min wasn’t
among them.

Even using the tracking skill yielded nothing.

[Target ‘Ryu Min’ cannot be found.]

[Face and name do not match.]

‘Why does it keep saying they don’t match?’

She knew his real face and his name.

And yet, the skill couldn’t locate him.

‘Did he change his name without telling me? Or… plastic surgery?’

The thought was ridiculous, but she had no other explanation.

‘I should’ve insisted that he come with me when we boarded the island…’

Back then, Ryu Min had refused to join her, saying he had something to do.

But now, even after scanning the entire island, she couldn’t find him.

She continued to buff people, counting each one.

“Thank you for the buffs, Miss Min Juri!”

“Yes…”

But by the time she finished, Min Juri was certain.

‘How can this be? All 576 players are here.’

She had carefully observed everyone as she cast her buffs.

Except for one person.

‘Ah…!’

Her eyes landed on a man wearing a white mask.

‘Could it be… Black Scythe…?’

But she quickly dismissed the thought with a sigh.

It was an absurd notion.

‘There’s no way Black Scythe is Ryu Min. Their builds are completely
different.’

Black Scythe was tall and muscular with tanned skin.

The two couldn’t possibly be the same person.

‘Then where is he? Why doesn’t the tracking work?’

With a heavy sigh, Min Juri approached Black Scythe.

“Black Scythe, I’ve finished buffing everyone here.”

“Well done.”

Min Juri hesitated for a moment, then asked cautiously.

“Black Scythe… have you seen the Prophet anywhere?”

“The Prophet?”

“Yes… The numbers match, but I can’t find him.”

Ryu Min’s eyebrow twitched beneath the mask, but only for a split second.

“If you can’t find him, why not use your tracking skill?”

“Well… it keeps saying the target doesn’t match.”

Ryu Min smirked internally.

‘Of course, it won’t work. The Assassin’s Mask alters my appearance and
prevents tracking.’

Tracking only worked if one had both the correct appearance and name.

“I don’t know. Maybe it’s a bug.”

“…I see.”

Min Juri looked visibly disappointed but refused to give up.

However, at that moment, a system message appeared.

[The 1st Summoning will begin shortly.]

[Prepare for the monster assault.]

“Stop looking for the Prophet and prepare for the assault.”

“But…”

“Don’t get stabbed while being distracted.”

“…Understood. I’m sorry.”

Seeing her droop in disappointment made Ryu Min feel a pang of guilt.

But there was no time for that now.

Chapter 257: Choice (2)

“Black Scythe.”

At the sound of his name, Ryu Min turned his head and saw Russell and
Victor approaching.

“I’ve finished reinforcing players’ weapons and distributing equipment
buffs, as you instructed.”

“I’ve also completed the distribution of healing potions.”

“Well done, both of you.”

“Black Scythe?”

This time, it was Christine who approached him.

“I’ve blessed all 576 players with Saintess’s Blessing.”

“Well done.”

“Thank you.”

Christine smiled brightly. Min Juri, watching this interaction, hesitated for a
moment before speaking up.

“Um, Chrissy?”

“Yes, Miss Min Juri?”

“You said you buffed all 576 players just now. Are you sure about the
number?”

“Yes, including me, the total was 576. Why do you ask?”

“Well, the thing is…”

Min Juri glanced around cautiously before lowering her voice.

“Did you… by any chance, see the Prophet? I’ve been searching for him,
but I can’t seem to find him anywhere.”

“Ah…”

Christine paused, seeming to think for a moment, before shaking her head.

“I didn’t see him either. I wasn’t checking everyone’s faces as I cast the
buffs… I’m sorry. I can’t be of more help.”

“Oh, no, it’s okay. You don’t need to apologize… I understand.”

Satisfied with Christine’s answer, Min Juri disappeared back into the crowd,
still determined to keep searching.

Unaware that Ryu Min was watching her from behind his mask.

‘Persistent. She really won’t give up until she finds me.’

Through his ability to read thoughts, he could tell why she was so
determined.

—If we fight monsters together, we could get even closer…

Her motive was clear: to deepen their relationship.

Not just as friends, but something more.

‘Even in this otherworldly hell, you’re still thinking about me.’

Between Ryu Min and Min Juri, there was no room for Black Scythe to
exist.

To her, Black Scythe was simply an object of admiration—a hero, an idol.

At that moment, Christine caught Ryu Min’s eye and winked playfully.

—Did I do well, Prophet?

Reading her thoughts, it was clear she was seeking praise.

But Ryu Min deliberately turned his head away, pretending not to notice.

There was no time for casual banter. The monsters were coming.

[1st Summoning]

[Players: 576 VS Blood Orcs: 5,760]

[Next Summoning Begins in: 30 Minutes]

[Time Remaining Until End of Round: 02:59:59]

Thousands of orcs appeared, wielding crude weapons.

Normally, they would have appeared near a city, slaughtering countless
civilians.

But here…

“Krrreeek!”

“Kreeeek?”

Surrounded on all sides by the sea, the orcs hesitated, looking around in
confusion.

They had clearly not expected to be summoned into such an isolated place.

“Filthy orc bastards!”

“No need for talk. Kill them all!”

“Waaaaah!”

“Kreeeek! Krrreeek!”

On this remote island, the players and orcs clashed fiercely.

Despite being outnumbered ten to one, the Death Church followers did not
falter.

Because numbers weren’t everything.

Thrust—Thrust!

Slash—Slice!

“Kreeeek!”

“Kuaaak!”

The air filled with the anguished cries of orcs as they fell one after another.

[You have slain a Blood Orc!]

[Title effect: Experience increased by 1.5x.]

[Rune of Gluttony effect: Experience and gold increased by 2x.]

[Experience gained: +0.0006%]

[Gold obtained: +3]

[Additional Gold: +1]

[With too many party members, stat points and Gluttony stacks are not
awarded.]

[Current Kill Count: 36/100]

[Rune of Massacre effect: All stats increased by 36%.]

[Number of enemies within 100m: 2,491]

[Rune of One vs. Hundred effect: All stats increased by 100%.]

Ryu Min swung his black scythe with fluid precision.

BOOOOM!

“Kreeeek!”

“Kuaaaagh!”

With a single sweeping motion, fifty Blood Orcs fell simultaneously.

The enemy numbers visibly decreased with each swing.

‘This is comfortable. With a party applied, I don’t need to worry about
allies getting hurt.’

Ryu Min massacred the orcs without holding back.

Unlike the 14th round, where rankings were based on contributions, there
was no need to hold back his power here.

‘It’s a shame that I can’t accumulate stat points or stacks with the Rune of
Gluttony.’

The Rune of Gluttony granted stat points based on the monsters slain.

But with hundreds of players in the same party, those bonuses couldn’t be
obtained.

Still, Ryu Min wasn’t bothered.

‘It’s fine. There will be more opportunities in the next round.’

For now, he could simply focus on wiping out the monsters without worry.

Until the fourth summoning ended.

‘During the fifth summoning, I plan to leave the island.’

The reason? A Sub-Quest.

‘The sub-quest for this round is saving civilians. The first player to save a
civilian under threat will earn the reward.’

The reward was a Rune of Yin and Yang—an essential item.

To claim it, Ryu Min planned to leave during the fifth summoning.

‘During the fifth wave, flying monsters called Little Drakes will appear. If I
can lure one out of the island and lead it to the city before killing it…’

The system would recognize him as the one who saved the civilians,
securing the sub-quest reward.

‘Until then, I’ll keep mowing them down.’

With that thought, Ryu Min continued his rampage as the end of the third
wave was nearing, suddenly, a message popped up.

[A target under Hero’s Protection is under attack!]

[You can use Hero’s Touch for 10 seconds.]

[Please select one of the following options:]

1. Move to the target.

2. Summon the target.

[Time Remaining: 00:00:10]

Chapter 258: My Younger Sibling
Is In Danger (1)

Ryu Min had previously placed the “Hero’s Protection” skill on his younger
sibling.

This skill granted invincibility for 10 seconds upon being attacked—a
broken protection ability.

And now, that skill had activated.

The meaning was clear.

“My brother… is in danger.”

Ryu Min had never expected that the precautionary skill he set up would
actually come into effect.

[Time until choice: 00:00:09]

“I don’t have much time.”

He didn’t know who was attacking his sibling, but there was only one
certainty:

He needed to act quickly to ensure their safety.

[Please choose one of the following:]

└ 1. Teleport to the target.

└ 2. Summon the target.

[Time until choice: 00:00:08]

“I have to choose one right now.”

Option 1 allowed him to teleport instantly to the target, with the added
benefit of immediate retaliation.

“But there’s a risk my sibling could get caught up in the fight.”

On the other hand, Option 2 would bring his brother to him, completely
removing them from danger.

“Option 2 is safer, but immediate retaliation becomes impossible.”

[Time until choice: 00:00:06]

There was no time left.

It was decision time.

Ryu Min’s lips moved.

---

Ten Minutes Before the 16th Round Began

[Gabriel, are you sure it’s wise for just the two of us to go?]

Gabriel’s elegant brow furrowed at the words that pricked at his pride.

[What are you implying, Raphael? Are you doubting my abilities?]

[No, of course not. I just thought… involving Michael might make things
more definitive.]

Raphael trailed off, seeing Gabriel’s expression darken to something
fearsome.

[You already upset me by convincing me not to go alone, and now you
think two of us aren’t enough? Do you find me that unreliable?]

[My apologies if I offended you.]

Though he was irritated, Gabriel wasn’t entirely unsympathetic.

[I understand. The human wielding the Scythe has proven unexpectedly
dangerous, even to us archangels.]

[…]

[But a human is still just a human. No matter how high a lizard climbs, it
will never become a dragon. Nothing will go wrong.]

[I don’t doubt that. After all, I witnessed your brilliance firsthand during the
Fifth Heavenly Demon War. Moreover, you have the ability to foresee your
opponent’s movements.]

[Calling it foresight is an exaggeration. It’s merely predicting the enemy’s
actions.]

[Still, that ability earned you the titles of Hero and Archangel of Prophecy,
didn’t it?]

[If you know that, why are you speaking as though you’re worried?]

[Because previous attempts by other archangels have failed. I wanted to
ensure that this time we bring the matter to a complete and decisive close.]

[Don’t worry. With the two of us together, it will be.]

It wasn’t empty reassurance.

Though Raphael lacked combat abilities, he was the third-ranked archangel,
bearing the title “Archangel of Healing.” With his support, Gabriel feared
nothing.

[We don’t need Michael to overwhelm him. I guarantee it will only take a
minute—no, ten seconds—to kill him.]

[Not subdue, but kill?]

[This is a human who has already slain four archangels. Summary
execution is more than warranted.]

Raphael nodded, though the decision was entirely Gabriel’s. Michael had
ordered them not to kill, but to capture.

“There’s no way I’ll let that filthy worm climb to the heavens.”

Gabriel intended to crush the human’s head on sight using his divine power.
While he doubted it would work given the fates of the other archangels, it
wouldn’t matter.

“Even if my initial strike is blocked, killing him will be easy.”

If questioned later, he would simply claim that the human’s death was
unavoidable due to the threat to his life. Michael would have no choice but
to accept his reasoning.

[Gabriel, the 16th round has begun.]

[Since the stage is set in the human realm, descending requires no divine
cost.]

Gabriel smirked and drew his golden chains.

[Good. Let’s end this quickly.]

[Understood.]

[Wait!]

Just as they were about to descend, Gabriel suddenly stopped.

[What’s wrong?]

[A revelation.]

[What?]

[The deity is calling me.]

It wasn’t surprising. As the “Archangel of Prophecy,” Gabriel occasionally
heard the voice of the divine.

[We’re to meet the deity together.]

[Who exactly are we meeting?]

[You’ll see when we arrive.]

Gabriel led the way, and Raphael followed closely. They passed through the
highest realms, arriving at a location shrouded in a barrier.

Passing through, they entered a void so still it seemed time itself had frozen.

[Aah…]

[There is no need to fear.]

Gabriel’s voice was calm, but Raphael trembled. What lay before him was a
presence far beyond his comprehension.

Gabriel, maintaining his composure, bowed deeply.

[May I ask why you summoned us?]

[A certain human is proving troublesome. So I did a little investigating.]

[Investigating?]

[The strength and weaknesses of the human called the Black Scythe.]

[Ah…]

[Would you like to know the results?]

[Yes.]

After a brief pause, the voice from the void continued.

[The two of you alone cannot handle him.]

[…]

Even together, the second-and third-ranked archangels were no match for a
single human? It was a blow to their pride, but Gabriel didn’t show it. In the
presence of such a deity, even pride must be set aside.

[You would have lost in direct combat. Without my intervention, you would
have ended up like the others—your bodies destroyed, reduced to nothing.]

[…]

[Excuse me for saying so, but we are confident. We will avenge our fallen
comrades and restore the honor of heaven…]

[You sound just like the archangels who’ve already died.]

[…]

[Do you think they lacked confidence? No. They died because they were
outmatched in strength. They underestimated their opponent.]

[…]

[The ignorant are always overconfident. If you cannot accurately gauge
your foe’s power, how are you any different from those already fallen?]

[I’m sorry. My thoughts were short-sighted.]

Gabriel bowed his head, but the deity remained composed.

[Raise your head. I did not summon you to quash your confidence.]

[Then…]

[I called you to aid in your strategy. I’ve uncovered the human’s weakness.]

[A weakness?]

Chapter 258: My Younger Sibling
Is In Danger (2)

[I called you to aid in your strategy. I’ve uncovered the human’s weakness.]

[A weakness?]

What the deity revealed was startling—a method so underhanded it seemed
unbecoming of divine will.

[Every creature treasures its family. The Black Scythe has only one family
member. I will give you their location. Take them hostage, and the Black
Scythe will have no choice but to submit.]

[Using a hostage would indeed shift the balance in our favor.]

Gabriel’s lips curved into a malicious smile. Underhanded or not, this was
no time for scruples. Gabriel was not one to care for such things anyway.

[This is an excellent strategy. Hehe.]

[Then our discussion is over. Report to Michael and depart.]

[Understood. Thank you.]

The void dissolved, and the heavenly light returned. Gabriel turned to
Raphael.

[Let’s go.]

Before leaving, they informed Michael of the deity’s revelation. Michael,
for once, looked visibly surprised.

[The deity suggested this?]

[It was not a suggestion—it was a command. And I agree this approach is
the most appropriate.]

[Hmm…]

Michael hid his unease.

“The deity has intervened… This is becoming far more serious than I
anticipated.”

Direct confrontation would have favored the Black Scythe, but with a
hostage, the situation would drastically change. Gabriel and Raphael
departed, leaving Michael deep in thought.

└ Content: Hello, I’m a father of a 24-year-old son. Recently, I discovered
my son has joined an organization called the Death Church. He always used
to stay in his room until midnight, but now he says he needs to leave the
country for some mission and refuses to share details. He claims it’s an
order from the Death Church and that revealing anything could jeopardize
their safety. Is this organization trustworthy?

[Comments: 9 Total]

└ I’m a mother of a 20-year-old daughter. She’s also a member of the Death
Church and had to leave for an overseas mission. Glad to see I’m not the
only one in this situation.

└ So, it’s true that the Death Church sends its members abroad?

└ Seems like it.

└ My younger brother’s part of the Death Church too. He got a similar
message, saying he had to leave but couldn’t disclose where because the
Black Scythe warned that revealing their location would put others at risk.

└ At least my son wasn’t lying. Thanks for the confirmation.

└

└ I have a friend in the Death Church, and from what I hear, they seem
trustworthy. Apparently, the strategies shared by the Black Scythe have
helped many survive.

└ Seriously, people still doubt the Death Church?

└ It’s trustworthy. After all, the Black Scythe himself runs it. If he’s behind
this, there must be a good reason. Just have faith and wait.

└ Heard the Black Scythe even helped protect the Death Church members
in the 15th round. He wouldn’t lead them into danger.

As Ryu Won read through the comments on the community board for
players, he nodded in agreement.

“There are lots of people worrying just like me.”

He had been searching online because his older brother had suddenly left
home, only to find this post.

“So, it’s not because he went to meet a girlfriend?”

It made sense. Why else would someone who had stayed home during every
round suddenly decide to leave?

“There’s nothing to worry about, then. Since he’s with the Death Church,
he’ll be fine.”

Feeling a bit more at ease about his brother’s safety, Ryu Won closed the
door to his room and lay down on his bed.

Click.

As he closed his eyes, he tried to relax, but his thoughts kept drifting back
to his brother.

‘He’ll survive again, right? After all, he’s a prophet.’

Though he was still worried, it wasn’t as overwhelming as before.

‘Nothing will happen. The Black Scythe will protect him since he’s part of
the Death Church.’

He believed that, as usual, his brother would return home safely once the
round was over.

With that thought in mind, Ryu Won drifted off to sleep, unaware of the
approaching danger.

[Muffled noises…]

‘What’s that sound?’

Just before falling asleep, faint murmurs reached Ryu Won’s ears. At first,
he thought it was noise from the neighbors, but soon realized it was closer
than that.

[Muffled voices…]

There were at least two distinct voices coming from the living room.

‘Could it be a thief?’

The idea of a thief sneaking in without making any noise sent a chill down
his spine. He froze, unsure of what to do.

Crash!

The door to his room burst open, flooding the space with light.

[So, this is where you were hiding.]

What entered wasn’t a thief but angels.

Their appearances were dazzlingly beautiful—but Ryu Won was aware of
the truth. The angelic image most people had was now overshadowed by
tales of their atrocities. To the general populace, angels were more fearsome
than demons.

Shivering uncontrollably, Ryu Won found himself unable to speak. The
male angel smirked.

[Even a creature as insignificant as you can recognize strength, it seems.]

[Is this human the Black Scythe?]

[No, the Black Scythe is on the island. Which means…]

Gabriel’s lips curled into a sinister smile.

[This is the perfect situation to take the hostage.]

With that, Gabriel extended his hand toward Ryu Won.

“No, no!”

Ryu Won’s body was lifted off the ground and suspended in midair like a
puppet.

[Instead of just taking him, maybe I should remove an arm as a warning.]

“No! Please!”

Ryu Won screamed, but Gabriel ignored him, brandishing his glowing
golden chain.

Swish—

The chain coiled around Ryu Won’s arm like a snake, burning with a bright,
fiery light.

Sizzle!

“Aaaaaah!”

The sound of sizzling flesh and Ryu Won’s agonized screams filled the
room. Gabriel and Raphael both smiled at his suffering, but the smiles soon
faded.

[What’s this? His arm isn’t severing.]

[Strange.]

Despite the intense heat and force, Ryu Won’s arm remained intact. Even
more oddly, there wasn’t a single wound on his skin.

[No injuries?]

Though Ryu Won was screaming in terror, he slowly realized that he wasn’t
feeling any pain.

[What’s going on, human? How are you resisting the Chains of Judgment?]

“…”

[Speak. I know you understand me.]

“I-I don’t know…”

Of course, he couldn’t answer. He had no idea why this was happening.

[Fine. I’ll rip it off myself.]

Just as Gabriel reached out to grab Ryu Won’s arm—

Boom!

Gabriel was hurled through the wall, crashing into the living room.

The chains binding Ryu Won unraveled, and he fell to the ground.

“Ugh…”

As he rubbed his sore backside, Ryu Won looked up, his eyes widening in
shock.

Standing before him, protecting him, was a masked figure.

Chapter 259: Controlling Power (1)

The Hero’s Touch allowed for two choices:

Move to the target or summon the target.

Among these, Ryu Min chose:

“Option 1.”

He chose to move to his younger sibling.

Not only did he want to protect him, but he also needed to confirm the
identity of his enemy.

Flash—

In the moment of his choice, Ryu Min saw a great archangel intimidating
his younger sibling.

“This won’t do. I’ll have to tear your arm off myself…”

BOOM!

Overwhelmed by rage, Ryu Min lost control and slammed the angel into the
living room wall.

‘I adjusted my strength at the last second, so it shouldn’t have killed him.’

If it had, things would become problematic.

He hadn’t had the chance to use the Blessing of the Demon yet.

“G-Gabriel!”

An angel hurriedly rushed toward the living room in panic.

‘So, the one I hit is named Gabriel.’

Ryu Min only learned the other angel’s name—Raphael—after reading the
other one’s thoughts.

He also learned that they were ranked second and third among the
archangels.

While Raphael tended to Gabriel, Ryu Min turned around.

He saw his younger sibling staring at him blankly.

“What’s your name?”

“Ryu… Won.”

“I’m the Black Scythe.”

“Ah, I know. I’ve seen you on TV a lot.”

Sometimes, media exposure was useful—it saved him the trouble of a
lengthy introduction.

“This might be overwhelming, but you need to focus. The situation is
urgent.”

“What’s going on…?”

For Ryu Won, it must have been a whirlwind of confusion.

One moment, an archangel appeared, binding him with chains and issuing
threats.

The next, the Black Scythe appeared out of nowhere.

“There’s no time to explain. What’s important is that you need to escape
from here immediately.”

At that moment, a message appeared.

[The ‘Hero’s Protection’ on your target has expired.]

The 10-second invulnerability cast on his younger sibling had ended.

Without hesitation, Ryu Min activated the Rune of Sacrifice.

[You have designated a target for protection.]

[You will take all damage intended for the target.]

[The rune deactivates if the distance between you and the target exceeds
100 meters.]

‘Good. The Rune of Sacrifice is in place.’

This meant his sibling was now virtually invincible.

‘He won’t get caught in the battle and die. At least, not until I die first.’

Even so, Ryu Min couldn’t let his guard down.

Two archangels stood before him.

‘The earlier attack dealt some damage, but it wouldn’t have been fatal.’

As expected, Gabriel rose nonchalantly, brushing off his wings.

“Raphael, it seems I’ve embarrassed myself in your presence. To think I
couldn’t dodge a mere human’s attack.”

“Are you all right?”

“Thanks to you, I’m unscathed.”

It wasn’t bravado. Gabriel’s body bore not a single scratch.

‘Even though I adjusted my strength, he’s completely unharmed?’

Ryu Min’s astonishment faded after he read Gabriel’s thoughts.

‘It’s because of that Raphael.’

Raphael wasn’t much of a combatant, but his array of support skills was
unparalleled.

The shield he had cast earlier had prevented Gabriel from taking damage.

‘This won’t work. I’ll have to target Raphael first…’

But Gabriel seemed aware of this and moved Raphael behind him.

“Stay behind me. This human warrants some caution.”

“I agree.”

Seeing Gabriel protect Raphael, Ryu Min knew.

‘This won’t be easy.’

That didn’t mean he lacked confidence.

He was certain he could win.

The problem was protecting his younger sibling while fighting in such a
confined space.

Without taking his eyes off the archangels, Ryu Min spoke.

“Listen carefully, Ryu Won. This is an emergency. Stay in your room and
don’t move an inch.”

“You mean just sit here?”

“Exactly. Moving around will only make it more dangerous. I’ll protect
you, so stay put.”

He didn’t wait for him reply.

Gabriel, chains extending from his hands, was closing in.

“So, you’re the infamous Black Scythe. I must admit, you’re stronger than I
expected. However…”

Without warning, Gabriel hurled his chains.

Ryu Min couldn’t dodge—his sibling was behind him.

Clang—!

The chains wrapped tightly around Ryu Min’s body.

“You need to understand that there’s always a greater power.”

The chains glowed red-hot, melting through Ryu Min’s armor.

Sizzle—

Smoke rose as his flesh burned and disintegrated.

“Hiiik!”

Ryu Won gasped, retreating in horror.

He couldn’t believe what he was seeing.

Gabriel and Raphael, on the other hand, laughed gleefully at the grotesque
scene.

“So pathetic. Had I known he’d die this easily, I’d have played with him
longer.”

“Indeed, Gabriel.”

“I guess there was no need to take a hostage after all…”

Chapter 259: Controlling Power (2)

“So pathetic. Had I known he’d die this easily, I’d have played with him
longer.”

“Indeed, Gabriel.”

“I guess there was no need to take a hostage after all…”

But Gabriel froze mid-sentence.

In his mind, he saw a grim future:

The Black Scythe appearing from the side, cutting him down in three
seconds.

Whoosh—!

Gabriel dodged just in time.

Ryu Min’s scythe sliced through the air.

“You avoided it?”

“So, it was only a clone after all.”

Ryu Min didn’t respond. He simply swung his scythe again.

Gabriel scowled, his pride wounded.

“You arrogant human! I’ll crush you in ten seconds!”

The golden chains slithered like snakes, pursuing Ryu Min.

But none found their mark.

Clang! Clang—!

‘Those chains are dangerous. If they wrap around me, I’ll be in trouble.’

Ryu Min knew he couldn’t block them with his scythe either—it risked
getting entangled.

He had to either dodge or deflect them briefly.

Gabriel’s mocking voice echoed.

“How long will you keep dodging? Attack me like you did before, coward!”

But Ryu Min wasn’t struggling.

With his agility stat maxed at 588, dodging was effortless.

‘I’m studying your abilities.’

Ryu Min was gathering information using his Rune of Insight.

Every move, every ability—they were all being analyzed.

The moment he had all the information he needed, Ryu Min changed
tactics.

Whoosh! Whoosh!

Gabriel’s eyes widened.

“What—!”

Ryu Min’s movements became too fast for even Gabriel’s foresight.

Thwack—! Crash—!

Gabriel was flung into a wall, coughing dust.

“You filthy human…”

But there was no time for insults—Ryu Min had already targeted Raphael.

Slash—!

Thunk—!

Ryu Min’s scythe struck Raphael’s barrier, bouncing off with a surprising
amount of force. The weapon rebounded, as if it had hit something soft yet
impenetrable, like a balloon.

“Cowardly scum! Attacking an unarmed opponent?”

“Unarmed, huh? You’ve been buffing Gabriel from behind this whole
time.”

Gabriel’s recent surge in speed and strength had all been due to Raphael’s
blessings. No wonder he was so intent on keeping him safe.

Even so, Raphael’s buffs couldn’t make up for the difference in skill.

Crash!

Once again, Gabriel was hurled across the room, this time slamming into a
piece of destroyed furniture. His wings flared as he stabilized himself mid-
air, his expression twisted in fury.

“Damn you, human… I’ll grind you to dust!”

“Didn’t you say that 10 seconds ago? Still not done?”

Ignoring the taunt, Gabriel charged forward, his golden chains flaring with
an even more chaotic energy.

Clang! Clang! Crash!

The living room was quickly devolving into a battlefield. The sofa was
obliterated, the television smashed to bits, and the marble floors cracked
under the force of the attacks.

Thwack!

“Gah!”

Yet, Gabriel had not landed a single effective hit.

Only Ryu Min’s scythe sent him flying again and again.

“You bastard!”

As Ryu Min set his sights on Raphael, Gabriel pounced on him like a feral
beast.

Gabriel clung to him with desperation, knowing that if Raphael wasn’t
protected, they would lose any chance of victory.

‘Why? Why am I losing when I can see three seconds into the future?’

Even with his foresight ability, Gabriel was feeling the frustration of battle.

Predicting the path of Ryu Min’s scythe and using his chains to block it
shouldn’t have been difficult.

But as Ryu Min’s movements accelerated, even reading the future became a
challenge.

It was like his mind couldn’t keep up with his body.

Thwack!

The scythe struck Gabriel, sending him skidding across the room.

He barely managed to stabilize himself with his wings, avoiding a complete
fall, but his pride had already taken a devastating hit.

“G-Gabriel,! Your mana reserves are…!”

“You said you’d kill me in ten seconds. Is ten seconds ten hours by your
standards?”

“Your arrogance knows no bounds!”

Whether or not he heard Raphael’s warning, Gabriel focused solely on
killing the Black Scythe.

The chains lashed out, yet they couldn’t even graze Ryu Min.

Gabriel’s frustration grew as his attacks failed to connect.

Clang! Clang!

Blows were exchanged, but Ryu Min had no intention of killing him yet.

He hadn’t activated the Demon’s Blessing.

‘It’s not that I’m choosing not to use it; the situation doesn’t allow for it.’

To fully benefit from the blessing, Ryu Min needed to activate Reaper
Transformation and amplify his stats to their maximum potential.

But using the transformation required equipping Thanatos’s Helmet, which
meant removing his current Assassin’s Mask.

‘If I take off the mask, my Lost Ark disguise will disappear. My sibling
might discover my identity.’

Although his younger sibling admired the Black Scythe, revealing his true
identity at this moment was not ideal.

He planned to explain everything after this ordeal was over.

‘For now, I need to get Won to safety. If I switch helmets here, he’ll see
everything.’

To do that, he needed to weaken the archangels significantly, enough to buy
his brother time to escape.

However, Gabriel was holding up better than expected.

Even though his collapse seemed imminent, he stubbornly endured.

Suddenly, a message appeared:

[The Curse of Slowing has been applied.]

[Attack speed and movement speed reduced by 30% temporarily.]

Ryu Min felt his movements slow noticeably.

It was Raphael’s doing.

‘He’s been trying this for a while, and he finally succeeded, huh.’

Ryu Min’s Blessing of the Saintess offered resistance to status effects and a
50% chance to negate debuffs.

‘My resistance only works against status effects. It doesn’t protect me from
debuffs.’

It was fortunate the blessing was active. Without it, he would have been
hindered by the debuff from the very start.

‘Annoying support.’

Even knowing Raphael was responsible, he couldn’t approach him easily.

No matter how many times he sent Gabriel flying, the archangel returned
like an unyielding wall to protect him.

Clang! Clang!

While dodging the swinging chains, Ryu Min noticed Gabriel’s eyes flash
ominously.

“Die already, human!”
