Chapter 260: It'S Time To Tell You
(1)

Even though the angel had used their unique authority, Sishal, out of
frustration, it was ineffective as long as the Supreme Being Title existed.

[A human who is immune to Sishal? This is absurd.]

Gabriel sighed and resorted to telekinesis.

Ryu Min felt an invisible force gripping his body, but only for a moment.

‘Telekinesis? That’s nothing.’

Breaking free with sheer strength, Ryu Min swung his scythe with
precision.

Crash!

Gabriel rolled across the ground, smashing into objects. The house was now
a complete mess, bearing the scars of battle.

“Aaaaargh!”

Clearly enraged, Gabriel lost his composure and began swinging his chain
recklessly.

Although dodging wasn’t difficult, the weapon itself was annoying to deal
with.

‘I’d like to break that chain, but it won’t be easy.’

Even though he was holding back, Gabriel had managed to block every one
of Ryu Min’s attacks so far. A half-hearted strike wouldn’t cut it.

‘If I can’t disable his weapon, I’ll have to neutralize something else
instead.’

Ryu Min’s movements suddenly sped up.

Even Gabriel, who could read the future, found it difficult to keep up with
his speed.

For the first time, Gabriel looked visibly flustered.

That was understandable—knowing what was coming was one thing, but
being unable to stop it was another.

Shwick—!

For the first time, golden blood sprayed from Gabriel.

Thud—!

His two arms, which had been holding the chain, were cleanly severed.

“Argh!”

Simultaneously, Raphael coughed up blood.

‘So, Raphael was absorbing the impact for Gabriel all along.’

Ryu Min had been wondering why Gabriel hadn’t sustained any injuries
despite being pushed back by his attacks.

He knew Raphael had buffed Gabriel to nullify damage, but a buff that
overpowered couldn’t come without a cost.

‘And the cost was absorbing the shock into his mana.’

The more Ryu Min attacked Gabriel, the faster Raphael’s mana drained
away.

The moment Ryu Min realized this, he changed his strategy, targeting
Gabriel instead of Raphael.

Without Raphael’s support, Gabriel wasn’t much of a threat.

“Khhhhh…!”

Gabriel’s face contorted in pain as he lost his arms, but Ryu Min didn’t have
the luxury to savor the sight.

Shwoooosh—

In the blink of an eye, Gabriel’s arms regenerated.

“Thank you, Raphael.”

“It’s nothing, but my mana is nearly depleted.”

“Already? How much do you have left?”

“At best… 5%.”

“What?!”

Gabriel was genuinely shocked.

Raphael possessed an ocean of mana. During the Celestial-Demonic War,
he had provided protective shields to hundreds of battle angels and had
lasted three full days without faltering.

But now, just five minutes into the fight, his mana reserves were nearly
empty?

“I can barely block one or two more attacks. I need time to recover my
mana…”

“Damn. This is bad.”

Ryu Min smirked as he watched the two angels exchange words.

‘They’re reaching their limits. If that’s the case…’

Glancing at Raphael, who was sweating nervously, Ryu Min vanished.

He reappeared instantly right in front of Raphael, whose eyes widened in
shock.

“Ah…”

That was the last word Raphael uttered in Ryu Min’s home.

CRASH—!

Ryu Min’s attack hit Raphael squarely, sending him crashing through the
living room window.

Thanks to the little mana he had left, Raphael avoided a fatal injury, but he
couldn’t stop himself from falling out of the building.

“R-Raphael!”

Gabriel, now panicked, realized he was next.

It was inevitable—his reliable shield was gone.

‘The Goddess was right. The two of us alone can’t handle this.’

Cornered, Gabriel sought a way to turn the situation around.

It didn’t even take him a second to come up with a plan.

‘Why didn’t I think of this earlier?’

Gabriel focused intently on the movements of the black scythe.

At first glance, Ryu Min seemed to be attacking recklessly, but Gabriel
could sense it—Ryu Min was paying close attention to his surroundings,
particularly to his younger sibling.

‘Let’s test my theory.’

Whip!

Ignoring the black scythe aimed at him, Gabriel hurled his chain.

Its target? The younger sibling trembling in the corner of the room.

‘If my guess is correct, the black scythe will…’

Clang—!

‘…prioritize protecting them.’

As expected, Ryu Min deflected the chain to shield his sibling.

“Humans truly are foolish creatures.”

Gabriel scoffed.

It made sense for him to protect Raphael, who was vital to their plan. But
why would a human go out of their way to protect a mere bystander?

Because they were family? Because they were important to him?

What use were such feelings in the middle of a battle?

Wouldn’t they just be a liability?

‘Now that I’ve found your weakness, I’ll exploit it thoroughly.’

Gabriel no longer paid any attention to Ryu Min’s attacks.

He aimed all his focus on Ryu Min’s sibling, ruthlessly swinging his chain.

Clang—! Clang—!

Each time, Ryu Min intercepted the chain, but the shockwaves from the
attacks continued to destroy the house.

Boom—! Boom—!

“Ugh, ugh…!”

The chaotic destruction terrified Ryu Won.

Even a fool could tell that the angel was targeting him.

‘W-What do I do? Because of me, the black scythe is in trouble.’

Ryu Won cowered in the corner, helpless, as Ryu Min stood protectively in
front of him.

Gabriel’s relentless attacks only made him feel guiltier.

‘I-It’s my fault. I’m the one holding him back…’

However, Ryu Min, who had read his sibling’s thoughts mid-battle, shook
his head inwardly.

‘No, it’s not your fault.’

The archangels were here to kill him, not his sibling.

Unable to win through sheer strength, they had resorted to using his family
as leverage.

‘I had prepared for something like this by casting the Hero’s Protection
spell, but…’

He hadn’t expected the situation to escalate so quickly.

Clang—! Clang—!

“Heh, foolish human. You’re barely managing to defend.”

Gabriel’s chain coiled tighter, like a snake closing in on its prey.

It wouldn’t be long before a single slip would lead to his sibling getting
hurt.

‘Fighting while holding back is proving to be more difficult than I thought.’

If Gabriel were an ordinary archangel, Ryu Min would’ve counterattacked
by now.

However, Gabriel’s ability to read three seconds into the future complicated
things.

‘If I leave even the slightest opening, my sibling will get hurt.’

Technically, it wasn’t his sibling who would get hurt—it would be him, but
the resulting impact wouldn’t be easy to endure.

‘He’s stalling for time.’

Gabriel’s reckless attacks weren’t without reason.

Deep down, Gabriel was calculating that even if he fell, Raphael would
recover and rejoin the battle.

‘I’ll finish this before that happens.’

Having no other choice, Ryu Min decided to use more of his power.

Chapter 260: It'S Time To Tell You
(2)

‘I’ll finish this before that happens.’

Having no other choice, Ryu Min decided to use more of his power.

‘Amplify.’

The rune of lightning granted him the ability to double both his attack and
movement speed.

In an instant, Ryu Min vanished.

[Huh?!]

Gabriel gasped, startled, and instinctively tried to react. But it was too late.
By the time he made a move, Ryu Min’s scythe had already sliced through
his lower body.

Screech—!

The cleanly severed lower half of Gabriel’s body fell to the ground, golden
blood pouring out in torrents and pooling beneath him.

“Khhh…!”

Gabriel’s face twisted in anguish, his expression crumpled like a piece of
paper.

How long had it been since he had last felt such excruciating pain? Not
since the Celestial-Demonic War had he experienced agony like this.

“Looks good on you.”

Ryu Min sneered, offering a curt, mocking evaluation of Gabriel’s
condition.

Gabriel’s body was a pitiful sight—his upper and lower halves separated,
golden blood gushing out. But Ryu Min knew better than to let his guard
down.

‘He can’t die yet. Not until he uses his Blessing.’

Ryu Min had a plan: first, ensure his sibling’s safety, then equip the Helmet
of Thanatos to finish off both angels once and for all.

He glanced back at his younger sibling.

“Let’s go, Ryu Won.”

Ryu Won, still trembling, hesitantly stepped out of the ruined room. He
avoided looking at the chaotic scene in the living room, where Gabriel lay
incapacitated. Instead, he focused on following Ryu Min.

But just as they were about to leave through the front door—

Flutter—

Through the shattered window, another angel descended.

It was Raphael.

Gabriel, still lying on the floor, managed a weak, relieved smile at the sight
of his ally.

“R-Raphael…”

“Gabriel!”

Without wasting a moment, Raphael chanted a Restoration Spell.

Immediately, Gabriel’s upper and lower halves reattached seamlessly.

“Tsk, I’ve lost too much blood. I feel lightheaded.”

“Are you all right?”

“What about you?”

“I’ve restored a bit of my mana, but not all of it. At this point, I can barely
defend against one or two more strikes.”

Gabriel groaned and glanced toward the front door, where Ryu Min and his
sibling had already disappeared.

“What should we do?”

“What else? We chase them.”

“But can we really handle him on our own?”

“We have no choice. We can’t return empty-handed.”

Gabriel’s gaze darkened as he recalled their recent exchange.

Ryu Min could’ve finished him off but didn’t. That alone had revealed his
weakness.

‘His sibling is his Achilles’ heel. If we target the younger one, the Black
Scythe will inevitably expose openings.’

With Raphael still at his side and their strategy now clear, Gabriel was
confident they could turn the tide of battle.

“Let’s move.”

“Yes, sir.”

-

There was no time to take the elevator.

Ryu Min and Ryu Won sprinted down the corridor, putting as much distance
as possible between themselves and the angels.

“This way.”

Ryu Min gestured as he led the way.

Panting and running frantically, Ryu Won suddenly realized where they
were headed.

“W-Wait! This is a dead end!”

The hallway ended at a large window with nowhere else to go.

But Ryu Min’s voice remained calm.

“Who said there’s no way out?”

Crash—!

Using his scythe, Ryu Min shattered the window. The sharp sound of
breaking glass filled the air, followed by the rush of wind from outside.

“W-What are you doing?! That’s insane! We’re on the 43rd floor!”

Ryu Won’s voice trembled as his fear reached its peak. But Ryu Min
remained unfazed.

“There’s no reason to be scared. I’m not planning on dying just yet.”

“W-What do you mean…?”

“Just hold on tight. No time to explain.”

Without further warning, Ryu Min grabbed Ryu Won.

“Wait, what are you— Aaaahhhh!”

Ryu Min leapt through the shattered window.

For a brief moment, it felt like they were plummeting toward certain death.

But then—

Flutter—

Black wings unfurled from Ryu Min’s back, stabilizing their descent.

Ryu Won, now clutching Ryu Min tightly, let out a sigh of relief.

“Phew… I thought we were going to die…”

From behind, Ryu Won’s trembling voice reached Ryu Min’s ears.

However, Ryu Min wasn’t as relaxed.

‘We’ve escaped for now, but the angels might still be able to track us.’

If Raphael had healed Gabriel and set out in pursuit, they wouldn’t have
much time.

‘On the other hand, if they’ve lost track of us and decided to wait back at
the apartment… that would be ideal.’

The best plan would be to get Ryu Won to safety, then return to deal with
the angels.

But his thoughts didn’t last long.

“W-We’re being followed! The angels are catching up!”

Ryu Won’s panicked voice confirmed Ryu Min’s worst fears.

‘So they can track us, huh?’

Ryu Min sighed. It seemed there was no other option.

He would have to fight while protecting his sibling.

‘Not here, though. I can’t risk innocent civilians getting caught up in the
fight.’

He adjusted their trajectory, heading away from the city center.

But the angels were faster than expected.

As Ryu Min glanced back, Ryu Won’s voice rang out in alarm.

“T-They’re almost here! They’re right above us!”

“I know.”

Ryu Min’s response was short, but his actions were decisive.

He suddenly dropped altitude, bringing them closer to the ground.

‘Before I can deal with them, I need to buy some time to talk to my sibling.’

Once they landed, the angels were right overhead.

“They’re here!”

“I told you, just hold on tight.”

Ryu Min scanned the area ahead, making sure there were no obstacles.

He activated another rune.

‘Light Speed.’

In an instant, a burst of light propelled them forward, covering 2 kilometers
in the blink of an eye.

The angels, caught off guard by the sudden acceleration, were left behind—
at least for now.

“W-What was that? Did we just teleport? How did you do that?”

Ryu Won stammered in disbelief.

“That’s not important right now. What matters is that the angels are still
chasing us. They won’t stop until we’re dead.”

“Then… what do we do?”

“What else? We kill them.”

Ryu Min’s words were confident, but Ryu Won hesitated, his face filled
with doubt.

Seeing this, Ryu Min chuckled softly.

“You’re probably wondering why I didn’t kill them earlier if I could.
Right?”

“…Yes.”

“Don’t worry. What you saw back there? That wasn’t even half of my
strength.”

“Can… can you really win?”

“Of course. But to do that…”

Ryu Min paused, removing his mask.

The Assassin’s Mask he had been wearing vanished, revealing his true face.

“I need to show you something first. It’s about time you knew.”

“Huh?”

Ryu Won’s confusion quickly turned to shock.

As Ryu Min’s body began to change, his sibling could only stare in
disbelief.

His height shrank, his tanned skin turned pale, and his muscular frame
became lean and slender.

Finally, his face took on a familiar appearance.

“Hyung…?”

Chapter 261: Vs Gabriel (1)

When people encounter something beyond reason, they instinctively start
doubting themselves.

That’s exactly what Ryu Won was doing at this moment.

‘Am I dreaming right now? Why does the Black Scythe look like my
brother?’

Even if it was a dream, it was astonishing.

Not because someone had changed, but because that changed appearance
looked identical to a member of his family.

“Snap out of it. This isn’t a dream.”

“Hyung…?”

“I’m the Black Scythe.”

Regardless of whether his younger brother believed him or not, Ryu Min
calmly spoke his truth.

“You probably know me as a prophet, but my actual class is Grim Reaper.
My nickname is the Black Scythe. Sorry for hiding it until now.”

“……”

“The situation’s too dire to keep it hidden. If I want to kill those angels over
there, I have to drop my disguise and use my skills.”

Ryu Min said this and turned his gaze skyward.

Gabriel and Raphael had chased them all the way here.

“You… you’re really the Black Scythe? I can’t believe it…”

“We’ll talk about the details later. Right now, we deal with them.”

Ryu Min switched his helmet to Thanatos’ Helm and activated Reaper
Mode.

[You have entered Reaper Mode.]

[All stats, damage, attack speed, and movement speed increase by 44%.]

[All damage received is reduced by 44%.]

[The probability of enemies detecting you decreases by 44%.]

Strength: 848,108

Intelligence: 850,179

Agility: 848,108

Luck: 852,379

The stats that had been 580,000 soared to 850,000.

‘With one last enhancement…’

He’d be fully prepared to hunt angels.

[You are now under the effects of Demonic Blessing.]

[Based on your current total stats (3,398,774), the following effects apply:]

[For each angel defeated, you will gain gold equal to 1x your total stats
(3,398,774). Depending on the angel’s rank, this amount can increase up to
1,000x (3,398,774,000).]

[For each angel defeated, you will gain stat points equal to 0.01% (339) of
your total stats. Depending on the angel’s rank, this can increase up to 10%

(339,877).]

[Reputation with the Demon Faction will increase slightly upon defeating
an angel.]

[This buff will last until the end of the current round.]

After confirming the buff, Ryu Min lifted his gaze to see the archangels
slowly descending.

“I’ll be right back. Stay here.”

“……”

Leaving only those words for his younger brother, he strode forward.

As the black figure approached, the archangels tilted their heads in
confusion. It wasn’t until they saw the scythe’s silhouette that they realized
his identity.

[Black Scythe? You’ve changed so much in such a short time, I almost
didn’t recognize you.]

[Judging by your aura, you must’ve used some skill.]

[Not that it changes anything.]

Gabriel sneered with a self-assured smile. It seemed they were ready to
combine their strength and target his weaknesses this time.

[You’ve put in quite the effort running this far. I’ll grant you peace by
killing you now.]

“You think targeting my younger brother will give you a chance at
victory…”

A devilish grin spread across Ryu Min’s lips.

“If I decide to kill you, it won’t take me more than ten seconds.”

[Don’t be ridiculous…]

In an instant, Gabriel’s eyes widened in shock.

His future vision had just shown him his own death.

[Hah!]

He gasped and instinctively backed away. Desperately flapping his wings,
he soared into the sky to escape the looming death he’d seen.

[G-Gabriel!?]

Raphael panicked when his superior retreated like a terrified animal.
Gabriel had confidently declared they would kill the Black Scythe this time.
Yet now, he was fleeing?

Gabriel’s future vision activated again, showing him the next three seconds.
He saw a grim future: his wings being slashed, leading to his inevitable fall.

Only three seconds left.

Now just two.

There was no time to think. He frantically changed directions.

But no matter how much he struggled, the same future repeated before his
eyes.

Death.

Death.

Death.

No matter how much he writhed, he couldn’t escape the predestined
outcome.

Flash!

A blinding light momentarily obscured his vision.

[Ack!]

When he opened his eyes, the Black Scythe was right in front of him.

There wasn’t even time to realize he had been dragged there.

Slash!

[Aaaaagh!]

Dozens of his wings were severed in one sweep, sending him plummeting
to the ground.

Thud!

A dull impact rang out, followed by waves of pain. But what came next was
far worse.

Stab! Stab! Stab!

[Ughhh!]

Dark daggers shot out like shackles, pinning his limbs to the ground.

And then—

Stab!

[Gahh!]

Ryu Min landed gracefully, plunging the scythe into Gabriel’s abdomen.

Stab! Stab! Stab! Stab!

Again.

And again.

Ten times in total.

Every part of Gabriel’s body, except for his head and heart, was riddled
with holes.

[Hngh… Nghhh…]

Chapter 261: Vs Gabriel (2)

[Hngh… Nghhh…]

Gabriel had no strength left to resist. Even moving was impossible.

And Raphael? He wasn’t in much better shape. Having lost too much mana,
he staggered and wiped the blood dripping from his lips.

‘He wasn’t lying about killing us in ten seconds. The damage is insane.’

Raphael was using the last of his mana to shield Gabriel, but it was draining
far too quickly.

Even healing magic was beyond his reach now.

As he looked down at Gabriel, who lay helplessly on the ground, Raphael’s
hope crumbled.

Their main damage-dealer was incapacitated. What could a support possibly
do in this situation?

‘I need reinforcements. Someone has to come.’

No matter how pathetic it looked, he had to escape.

The best option was to flee and prepare for the future.

Muttering under his breath, Raphael began chanting a recall spell, carefully
hiding it from the Black Scythe.

He needed only ten seconds.

Just ten seconds of focus, and he could return to the Celestial Realm.

Stab!

[Kyahhh!]

“Where do you think you’re going?”

Ryu Min extended his scythe, stabbing Raphael’s thigh. He sighed as he
watched the angel continue chanting through gritted teeth.

“Gabriel. Say your goodbyes.”

Stab!

“Raphael is heading to heaven first.”

As the scythe pierced Raphael’s heart, the chant stopped.

Thud—

Raphael collapsed, lifeless. Gabriel’s eyes widened in shock.

[Y-You devil… You’re worse than any demon!]

“Oh, so you still have enough energy to talk?”

Ignoring the reward messages flashing across his vision, Ryu Min turned
his gaze to Gabriel, who was now reduced to just his upper body.

“Did you know? To us, you angels are the real demons.”

[You filthy wretch! What have we ever done to deserve this!?]

“What have you done?”

Ryu Min felt a hollow laugh bubbling up inside him. Was this some sort of
twisted joke?

“You don’t know? You forced 1.8 billion people into a death game, and
you’re asking what you did wrong?”

[But we offered rewards! If you cleared the 20th round, you’d get a wish
granted! And we’ve let you enjoy powers humans could never even dream
of!]

“……”

Ryu Min was momentarily speechless.

This was beyond absurd. It was like being thanked for taking out the trash
only to get scolded for doing so.

[You should feel honored, yet you dare turn your blades against us angels
who’ve given you this opportunity? You filthy pests deserve to burn in
sulfur!]

“Looks like you’ve lost your grip on reality.”

Stab!

[Aaargh!]

“There’s still plenty of places left to stab, you know?”

Though Gabriel writhed in agony, his gaze remained unyielding.

[You’ll regret this. If you kill me, Lord Michael won’t let you off.]

“And if I don’t kill you, will Michael spare me?”

[……]

“Whether you live or die, Michael will come after me regardless.”

Gabriel’s expression twisted at the truth of his words.

[Then do it. Kill me. Lord Michael will avenge me.]

“If Michael shows up, I’ll kill him too.”

[Then someone even higher will come for you!]

“Who? God?”

Gabriel’s eyes widened in shock. Did he not realize his thoughts were being
read?

“Tell Him to come. I’ll kill Him too if He wants to fight.”

With that, Ryu Min drove his scythe into Gabriel’s heart, silencing him
forever.

[You have slain the Archangel Gabriel!]

[Stat Points +237,913]

[Gold +2,379,141,800]

[Reward: Refined Aether obtained.]

[Reward: Rune of Chains obtained.]

[Demon faction reputation greatly increased.]

[Demon faction reputation with Black Scythe: ‘Very Friendly’ → ‘Eternal
Ally’.]

Ryu Min reviewed the rewards. Thanks to the Demonic Blessing, the stat
points and gold he gained were immense.

‘237,000 stat points and 2.3 billion gold… The Demonic Blessing really
lives up to its name.’

The reputation he lost in the 14th round after killing Plunictos’ avatar had
also been restored. But amidst the satisfaction, a new mystery emerged.

‘What is this? Refined Aether? It’s not Condensed Aether.’

Since it was the first time he had killed an archangel of this rank, it made
sense that he would encounter unfamiliar items. Curious, Ryu Min scrolled
up through the messages to confirm the rewards from Raphael’s death.

[You have slain the Archangel Raphael!]

[Stat Points +203,926]

[Gold +2,039,264,400]

[Reward: Refined Aether obtained.]

[Reward: Rune of Resurrection obtained.]

[The rune has been automatically inscribed on the player’s body.]

‘Raphael also dropped Refined Aether.’

Though he wasn’t sure what it was, he decided it wasn’t a priority right
now. Something far more pressing demanded his attention.

Ryu Min had uncovered crucial information during his brief interaction
with Gabriel. The 6th wave of angelic summons was set to include 1st-
Class Combat Angels. This was a major escalation.

‘Those 1st-Class Combat Angels…’

Even if the entirety of the Grim Reaper Church gathered, they wouldn’t
stand a chance against just one of them.

‘If I don’t make it in time… the Grim Reaper Church members will all be
wiped out.’

He closed his eyes and activated the temporary skill he had obtained:
Clairvoyance. His vision expanded, allowing him to see a remote island
thousands of kilometers away.

The players gathered there were locked in battle with a swarm of monsters.
It was the 4th wave of summons.

‘The 4th wave has just begun.’

This meant there was still about an hour before the 6th wave—and the
appearance of the 1st-Class Combat Angels.

However, that also meant he had only one hour to travel over 4,000
kilometers from Korea to the remote island.

Chapter 262: Is This The Human
World? (1)

At that moment, a message appeared.

[The duration of Reaper Transformation has ended.]

Simultaneously, another message regarding a side quest popped up.

[A hidden side quest has been discovered!]

└ Be the first to rescue a civilian in Round 16.

└ Reward upon success ▶ Rune of Yin and Yang

[You have completed the side quest!]

[As a reward for the side quest, you have received the Rune of Yin and
Yang!]

[The acquired rune is automatically engraved onto the player’s body!]

It seemed saving his younger brother from the angel fulfilled the conditions.

‘Originally, I planned to lure the Little Drake into the city… but in the end,
I still got the side quest reward.’

The Rune of Chains, the Rune of Revival, and now even the Rune of Yin
and Yang.

He wanted to check out all of these rewards immediately but now wasn’t
the time.

He had to return to the isolated island as soon as possible to stop the battle
angels that would appear in an hour.

‘The corpses of the archangels need to be hidden. There’s no time to
summon John Delgado.’

Ryu Min moved the bodies of Gabriel and Raphael.

Though their bodies were riddled with holes, he had deliberately restrained
his power to leave the corpses intact.

This was so he could resurrect them as undead and claim another round of
rewards.

Had he not restrained himself, the Moonlight combo attack would have
reduced them to mere dust with no trace left behind.

Thunk- Thunk-

Digging into the ground with his scythe, Ryu Min buried the bodies of the
archangels. He marked the spot in a way only he could recognize and then
approached his brother.

“Won-ah.”

“Hyung…”

“I know there’s a lot you want to say, but let’s save it for later. The people
on the island are in danger right now.”

“The island?”

“I’ll explain everything once it’s over. For now, take this.”

Ryu Min handed him a master card.

“It’s dangerous, so don’t go home. Find a nearby motel and rest there. Use
this to pay for everything, including food.”

“Oh, okay. But I didn’t even bring my phone. How will you know where I
am?”

“There’s no need to tell me. I’ll track you. I’ll come find you once it’s all
over.”

With those words, Ryu Min switched to his Assassin’s Mask.

Wriggle-wriggle-

As his appearance shifted to the bronze-colored Lostyak, his brother looked
at him with wide, amazed eyes.

“Even seeing it happen right in front of me, I still can’t believe it. My
brother is Black Scythe…”

“Sorry for hiding it. I didn’t tell you because I was afraid you’d be in
danger if you got involved with me. But now, it seems that’s meaningless.”

The angels already knew all about his family ties. They even knew how
much he cared for his brother.

Otherwise, they wouldn’t have resorted to such a cunning scheme.

Ryu Min smirked bitterly and spread the wings on his back.

“For now, it’s a secret to everyone else that I’m Black Scythe. Can you keep
it for me?”

“Of course. My lips are sealed, but…”

Ryu Min shot him a sharp glare, making his brother smile awkwardly.

“I-I’m kidding.”

“I’m busy, so I have to go. Get some sleep in the meantime.”

With those words, Ryu Min soared into the night sky and sprinted forward,
kicking off the ground.

KWAANG!

After the deafening roar faded, Ryu Won could only stand there, still
looking up in amazement at his brother disappearing into the distance.

The universe was divided into five dimensions.

The Divine Realm, the Celestial Realm, the Demonic Realm, the Human
Realm, and the Netherworld.

Among them, the weakest species, without question, were the humans of
the Human Realm.

The strongest were, of course, the divine beings.

[A degenerate race with no wings…]

Ironically, the race that despised humans the most was none other than the
Celestials, whom humans revered as angels.

Though they had beautiful appearances, their insides were filled with
jealousy and selfishness.

[Filthy humans, more pathetic than insects. Let’s take this opportunity to
wipe them all out.]

[Why are you so angry, Baruel?]

[Why am I angry?]

When his comrade asked, 1st-class angel Baruel snorted as if it were
obvious.

[Because we’re doing the work that those 6th-class weaklings should have
handled! On top of that, I barely have time to breathe from training, and
now this?]

[But it’s a special order from Lord Gabriel. If he commands, we obey. What
else can we do?]

[If those damn humans hadn’t survived until the 16th round, we wouldn’t
even be wasting our time like this!]

Hearing this, the nearby angel Demiel chuckled.

[Hey, Baruel. Just admit it. You’re mad because you lost that bet with me,
aren’t you?]

[W-What? I-I’m not mad because of that!]

[A bet? What kind of bet did you two make?]

Curious, their comrade turned to Demiel, who grinned and explained.

[We bet on how many humans would survive the 15th round. I said over
100 would survive, while Baruel said less than 100. Well, you know the
result, right? Hah.]

[Over 500 survived. An all-time record.]

[So, Demiel, you won? What was at stake?]

[He has to take over all my night shifts for a month.]

[Seriously? Pfft! Hahaha!]

[No wonder Baruel’s mad. Hahaha.]

[D-Don’t laugh at me, you bastards!]

Baruel’s face flushed red.

It was humiliating enough to lose the bet, but now his comrades were
mocking him as well.

‘This is all because of those damn humans.’

The humans had survived far more than expected, which led to his current
disgrace.

[…I’ll kill them all. Every last one of those wretched humans.]

[Whoa, look at Baruel’s eyes.]

[He’s seriously pissed off now.]

[Why don’t you use this opportunity to vent your anger?]

[Yeah, when else are you going to get a chance like this?]

When Celestials crossed into the Human Realm, they lost 90% of their
power.

This was due to a special barrier designed to protect the weaker humans
from otherworldly invaders.

As a result, humans rarely had opportunities to encounter beings from other
dimensions.

There was no reason for Celestials to visit a bug-infested planet while
suffering immense power loss.

However, there was one exception: when the system permitted it.

During the rounds, Celestials could cross into the Human Realm without
paying the price of power loss, as allowed by the system.

[If not now, when will I get the chance to slaughter them? Don’t you
agree?]

[I’ll even give up my share for you, so go all out.]

[Same here.]

[Me too.]

[Go on, have a proper showtime, Baruel. Hah.]

[…Thanks, you bastards.]

Baruel gritted his teeth, his anger boiling over thanks to his comrades’
teasing.

Soon, the door to the Human Realm would open, and he would descend
without any restrictions on his power.

[Oh, right, you know that Sishal won’t work, right?]

[I know.]

Not that he planned to use Sishal in the first place.

‘Those filthy insects. I’ll tear them apart, limb by limb, while they’re still
alive.’

Baruel vowed to kill every last one of them.

Chapter 262: Is This The Human
World? (2)

The remote island was littered with corpses.

Not human corpses, but monsters.

“Is everyone okay?”

“Yes, we’re fine!”

“Is anyone injured? If so, I’ll heal you!”

“No one’s hurt, and no one’s dead!”

Fortunately, among the pile of monster corpses, there were no human
casualties.

Relieved, Christine let out a sigh as Min Juri approached her.

“Christine, have you seen Black Scythe?”

“Black Scythe?”

“I haven’t seen him for a while now…”

Christine also began looking around for Black Scythe, realizing she hadn’t
noticed his absence while she was busy healing.

“I don’t know.”

“Did he say anything about going somewhere?”

“Not at all.”

Min Juri frowned as she counted the remaining people.

Including herself, there were 575 players. No matter how many times she
counted, one was missing.

‘Where could he have gone?’

She didn’t have time to ponder further.

[Time remaining until the end of the round: 01:10:27]

The 5th wave would begin in just 10 minutes.

Realizing there wasn’t much time left, Min Juri began casting buffs on
everyone.

Though the buffs had become familiar, the players didn’t forget to thank
her.

“Thank you.”

“Of course. Now…”

Before Min Juri could finish, someone called out to her.

“Excuse me. Is your name Democracy?”

It was the Archmage Alex. Min Juri turned to him, her eyes wide.

“Yes, why?”

“If it’s not too much trouble, may I stay by your side?”

“What? Why…?”

“Based on my judgment, there are two most important players on this
island.”

Alex pointed his staff at Christine.

“That Priest over there…”

Then he pointed directly at Min Juri.

“And you, the Buffer.”

“……”

“If the two of you fall, it’s safe to say there’s no chance of victory. That’s
my assessment, so I’ll protect you.”

“You’re saying… you’ll protect me?”

“Yes. Protecting the supporters is a fundamental rule in party play, isn’t it?”

Min Juri was slightly flustered.

This was the first time someone had stepped forward to say they’d protect
her.

“Uh, I’m fine, really. Please protect Christine over there instead.”

“That spot’s already taken, as you can see.”

Near Christine, a female player armed with a bow had taken up a protective
stance, acting like a bodyguard.

“May I stay by your side to protect you?”

“Ah, well, sure. If you do, I’d appreciate it.”

As soon as Min Juri said the words, Alex nodded and moved next to her.

It felt a little awkward having him follow her like a bodyguard, but Min Juri
didn’t see any harm in his proposal.

Besides, Alex didn’t seem like a bad person.

[5th Wave Summon]

[Players: 576 vs. Little Drakes: 1,152]

[The 6th wave summon will begin in 30 minutes.]

[Time remaining until the end of the round: 00:59:59]

As the 5th wave began, countless Little Drakes appeared in the sky.

Though they were called “Little Drakes,” each one was the size of a car,
making them impossible to ignore.

“It’s starting!”

“Everyone, focus!”

“Just follow the strategy!”

“KIIIIIIIIII!”

“KYAAAAAH!”

The Drakes filled the sky, swooping down with bared fangs toward the
ground.

“Fire ranged attacks first!”

“Take down the ones that get close!”

Despite the sudden appearance of flying monsters, the players didn’t panic.

After all, they’d already received a detailed strategy from Black Scythe
beforehand.

Swishhh-!

Crackle-crackle-!

Fwooosh!

Thunk! Thunk!

Magic and arrows flew everywhere.

Players targeted the Drakes’ wings with ranged attacks, causing them to fall
to the ground. Once grounded, the melee attackers rushed in to finish them
off.

“It’s a fire attack!”

“Dodge it!”

When one of the Drakes opened its jaws and unleashed a blaze of fire, the
players quickly scattered out of harm’s way.

Thanks to the Swift buff increasing their movement speed, they could avoid
the attack with ease.

That didn’t mean there were no injuries at all, though.

“Ahh! It burns!”

“Over here!”

Christine cast a wide-area healing spell, instantly soothing the burn injuries
on the players’ skin.

The players, reinvigorated, dove back into the fray, hunting the Drakes with
renewed determination.

Perhaps disturbed by this efficient teamwork, one of the Drakes fixed its
sights on Christine.

“Kyaoooo!”

It lunged at her with murderous intent, but its assassination attempt ended in
failure.

Thunk! Thunk!

“KYAAAAGH!”

Arrows, fired in rapid succession by Dorothy, blinded the Drake by piercing
both of its eyes.

“Not a chance.”

Dorothy smirked as she shot another arrow directly into the blinded Drake’s
eye socket.

The magically enhanced arrowhead drilled into the creature’s brain,
finishing it off.

Thanks to the players’ coordinated efforts, it didn’t take long for the
thousand-plus Drakes to be completely annihilated.

“Phew, finally, we can rest a bit.”

“This round was tougher than the others.”

The players collapsed onto the ground, exhausted, and began to take a brief
rest.

Once again, no lives were lost in the battle—a miracle, given the odds.

Still, no one could erase the worry etched on their faces.

That was because they already knew what would come in the final wave,
thanks to Black Scythe’s briefing.

“It’s going to be the battle angels, right?”

“Yeah, he said 10 of them would show up.”

“Now we even have to fight angels… This is insane.”

“Can we really win against them with our strength?”

“We can. Black Scythe said it’s possible, didn’t he?”

But what they didn’t know was that when Ryu Min said he could handle the
angels, he was referring to 6th-tier angels.

[Is this the Human Realm?]

When the 6th wave summon began, 1st-tier angel Baruel descended,
grinding his teeth in fury.

Chapter 263: Ten 1St-Class Angels
(1)

[6th Summon]

[Players: 576 vs High Orcs: 576]

[Round will end in 30 minutes.]

[Time remaining until the round ends: 00:29:59]

Along with the summoning message, High Orcs with dark, rough skin
appeared, snorting violently.

But no one paid any attention to the orcs.

This was because the ten angels who appeared with halos on their backs
were overwhelmingly more intimidating.

[Is this the human world?]

Baruel, who was visiting the human realm for the first time, something he’d
only heard about, looked down at the swarming humans as if they were ants
and ground his teeth.

‘I can’t believe I have to dirty my hands because of these bug-like
creatures.’

The irritation bubbling within him subsided quickly.

Upon seeing the humans clashing with the High Orcs, he found it
entertaining.

[Shall I enjoy the view while I’m here?]

[Sure, Baruel. No need to rush, is there? Keke.]

The ten first-class angels leisurely observed the battle from the sky.

They knew enough to recognize that High Orcs were far inferior monsters
compared to themselves.

[To think humans are struggling so desperately against such trivial
monsters.]

[Humans truly are frail and weak.]

[There aren’t even many of them, and yet they drag things out like this.]

[If it were us, we would’ve killed them all with a single blow.]

Though they sneered and ridiculed, they still found the sight amusing.

Watching beings of a similar level fight each other was a perfect source of
entertainment.

At that moment, Demiel asked Baruel:

[Aren’t you going to step in? Our original purpose is to assist the monsters
and disrupt the humans, isn’t it?]

[That’s the official reason. But do we really need to get involved in this
battle? I could clean up all the humans here by myself if I wanted to.]

Baruel had no intention of helping the monsters or interfering in the battle.

[Let’s allow the humans to enjoy themselves for a bit longer.]

He wanted to reserve the time solely for himself—

The time to massacre the humans after the battle ended.

[Do as you wish. The humans are all yours, anyway.]

[You’ve got 25 minutes left. Kill or spare them however you like. Keke.]

Baruel smirked without needing further instruction.

‘I’ll tear them apart limb by limb, one by one, and make them die in agony.’

Even 25 minutes wouldn’t be enough for him to vent his frustrations.

Hwarrrk—Bang, Bang!

“Chweeeek!”

“Kiiiiik!”

For players who weren’t even level 70, High Orcs were tough opponents.

Had they faced them one-on-one, there would have been casualties for sure.

However, they were a team.

With the exception of Black Scythe, 575 players cooperated, guarding each
other’s backs and coordinating their movements.

Thanks to that synergy, the number of High Orcs quickly dwindled.

“Phew. Looks like they’re all dead?”

“Anyone injured?”

They glanced around to see if there were any casualties, but everyone was
unharmed.

Only the corpses of monsters littered the island.

“Thankfully, it doesn’t seem like we have any deaths.”

“Then, what’s left now is……”

All eyes turned toward the sky in unison.

Was it because of the hundreds of gazes focused on them?

One of the angels slowly descended.

[I enjoyed watching your fight, humans. Such a child’s play…]

Baruel stopped speaking and shielded his body with his wings.

Bang! Bang!

“We hit it!”

“That landed perfectly, didn’t it?”

The mages who had launched fireballs cheered, their faces lighting up with
excitement.

But their smiles vanished when they saw that not a single feather had been
singed.

No, to be precise, it wasn’t an entirely unscathed face.

His expression was twisted in anger, enough to resemble a demon.

[Y-you filthy trash…… How dare you attack me, the noble one, while I’m
speaking…….]

“We don’t have time to stand around!”

“Shoot again!”

Lightning magic, ice spells, fireballs, arrows, thrown spears, and even
daggers—Every long-range attack they could muster was directed at
Baruel.

There was no other reason for their actions:

Don’t wait until they descend to the ground.

Don’t give them a chance to speak; launch a preemptive strike.

Focus all attacks on the first angel to appear.

It was a strategy for fighting combat angels as instructed by Black Scythe.

Fwoosh—!

Sssssk—!

Crackle—!

The barrage of attacks bombarded Baruel’s wings.

If he were a sixth-class angel, he would have been reduced to a pulp
already.

But Baruel was a first-class angel.

The strongest among the trained elite, second only to the seven archangels,
Baruel was the pinnacle of angelic warriors.

[Playtime is over.]

The moment Baruel, who had been shielding himself with his wings,
vanished, people froze in confusion, having lost their target.

But Baruel reappeared in an instant.

[Here.]

“Gasp!”

Before a player could even turn around,

Slash—!

Their head was severed and fell to the ground.

The ‘Feather Blade,’ a weapon distributed exclusively to first-class angels,
emitted a menacing aura.

As the horrified onlookers stared, Baruel smirked.

[Did you humans really think you could challenge someone like me?]

“Ki-kill……”

The nearby player, who had tried to say something, could not finish their
sentence.

The Feather Blade slashed through their body, armor and body.

A player who swung their arm in panic had their weapon cut clean in half.

Another who raised an axe to strike was decapitated along with their arms.

One who tried to flee in terror was impaled through the back, dying
instantly.

There wasn’t even time to scream.

In less than ten seconds, 15 players around Baruel had fallen, reduced to
corpses.

An ambiguous level of power could inspire a desire to fight, but
overwhelming power could only instill fear.

Baruel’s power was, without a doubt, in the latter category.

He slaughtered people so mercilessly, making it clear that anyone who
dared approach him would be torn apart.

“S-stop!”

“E-everyone, stop attacking him!”

Had they realized they were nothing more than moths rushing into a flame?

The players hesitated, backing away.

Seeing this, Baruel sneered.

[What’s the matter? Won’t you come any closer?]

“……”

[I was just starting to have fun, but now you’re ruining it by giving up so
easily? Are you really not going to come at me anymore?]

“P-please stop this.”

One brave player stepped forward and tried to plead.

“Why are you doing this to us? We’re not just ordinary people—we’re
players.”

[I know.]

“Aren’t angels supposed to avoid interfering with players? That’s the
unspoken rule, isn’t it?”

[Who told you that?]

Baruel chuckled.

[You’re nothing but vermin. If we angels want, we can kill you anytime we
please.]

“If that’s true, then why bother with this survival game…”

[That’s none of your business. What matters is that all of you will die here
today.]

That statement was effectively a death sentence.

Despair cast its shadow over the players’ faces.

“W-what did we do to deserve this…?”

[You attacked me first, and now you’re asking what you did wrong?]

Baruel let out a mocking laugh and closed the distance in the blink of an
eye.

“Gasp!”

The terrified man’s sharp intake of breath became his final words.

Thunk—roll.

[I was already furious, and you humans had the audacity to attack me first.
Doesn’t it make sense for me to snap? Killing every last one of you here
won’t even begin to satisfy me.]

Baruel raised his Feather Blade, infusing it with divine power.

Woooom—

The feathers on the blade’s edge stiffened, transforming into razor-sharp
spikes that shimmered like deadly needles.

[I won’t let a single one of you live.]

With that, Baruel unleashed his magic-infused feathers in a wide arc.

Puk— Puk-puk—!

“Urk!”

“Aaargh!”

The feathers shot out like a barrage of spikes, piercing through the players.

Many collapsed instantly, riddled with holes, while some miraculously
survived.

It was thanks to Christine’s area-wide healing spell that a handful managed
to cling to life.

“Everyone! At this point, we have no choice but to fight back!”

“That’s right! That angel doesn’t plan to let any of us live!”

The players, choosing to make a final stand rather than die helplessly,
charged at Baruel with all they had.

[Foolish human scum. Have you still not learned your lesson?]

Baruel sneered and prepared to unleash his Feather Blade again.

But this time, he was forced to abandon his attack, quickly raising his blade
to protect his face.

Two arrows came flying straight at his eyes.

Ting! Ting!

Had he reacted even a fraction of a second slower, he might have lost both
eyes.

[You filthy insects… Who dares…?]

Baruel’s gaze burned with rage.

Someone had not only targeted his eyes but had done so with unerring
precision.

He deflected another arrow aimed at his temple and scanned the crowd.

His sharp eyes immediately located the source—a player calmly drawing
their bowstring.

[There you are, you little worm.]

Chapter 263: Ten 1St-Class Angels
(2)

[There you are, you little worm.]

While effortlessly blocking the attacks from the rest of the players with his
wings, Baruel dashed toward the archer at incredible speed.

“Hah!”

Seeing the angel appear right in front of her in an instant, Dorothy released
her arrow.

Thunk—!

The arrows struck his wings but fell harmlessly to the ground.

Before she could react further—

[You pathetic worm. Die.]

Puk!

Baruel’s Feather Blade pierced through Dorothy’s chest, skewering her
heart.

“D-Dorothy!”

Christine screamed in shock, but Baruel didn’t even glance in her direction.

He merely leapt into the air to dodge the concentrated bombardment of
attacks aimed at him and began charging another skill.

Fwoosh— Fwoosh— Fwoosh—!

Puk— Puk— Puk!

“Kuhhh!”

“Gaaah!”

The number of fallen players increased with each passing moment.

Despair seemed inevitable, but all hope was not lost.

Slash—!

A piece of Baruel’s wing was suddenly cut off, feathers scattering into the
air.

‘What…?’

For the first time, Baruel felt a sense of danger.

He quickly retreated and searched for his attacker.

[No way…?]

His eyes widened as he recognized the figure before him.

It was another angel—or so it seemed at first glance.

Their body bore the same celestial features, but their skin and face showed
decay, with patches of bone visible. Their form was semi-transparent,
ghost-like.

It was none other than Sariel, the Death Archangel, or rather, an undead
imitation of him.

[Sariel?]

[What?]

The other angels, who had been watching from a distance, were just as
shocked as Baruel.

How could Sariel, one of the seven archangels, appear in this place?

[Wait, that’s not Sariel.]

It was Demiel who corrected the others.

Strictly speaking, this was not Sariel.

His appearance was similar, but the decaying body and ghostly nature made
it clear: this was an undead version of the archangel.

[Damn humans. They turned an archangel into an undead puppet.]

Baruel didn’t feel anger—he felt pity.

How weak must Sariel have been to allow himself to be turned into a toy
for these lowly humans?

[For a noble being like him to be turned into a plaything of such vile
creatures… I shall grant you peace, Sariel.]

But regardless of Baruel’s words, the undead Sariel didn’t hesitate.

He swung his massive curved sword directly at Baruel, driven solely by the
orders of the summoner, John Delgado.

[How pitiful.]

Although Baruel spoke words of pity, he couldn’t afford to stay relaxed.

He was entirely focused on deflecting Sariel’s strikes.

Clang—! Clang—!

The undead Sariel, ranked 6th among the archangels in life, still retained
50% of his former strength, even as an undead puppet.

For Baruel, a first-class angel, he was a formidable opponent—someone he
could not easily overcome.

[What are you all standing around for?! Help me, you idiots!]

Baruel finally called out to his fellow angels for help.

The other first-class angels, who had been leisurely watching the spectacle,
burst into laughter.

[That’s what we were waiting to hear.]

[Sure, we’ll help you out.]

The ten angels joined the fray, surrounding Sariel.

Although Sariel was powerful, he was still only half of his former self—and
now, he faced ten fully intact first-class angels.

The balance tipped almost immediately.

Slash—! Slash—!

Feather Blades sliced into Sariel’s body, cutting his limbs apart.

Unable to endure the combined assault, the undead Sariel faded into mist,
vanishing.

Though he could be resummoned once the cooldown expired, for now, he
was out of the battle.

[Hmph, even an archangel isn’t that big of a deal, huh?]

[It’s just a half-baked undead spirit.]

[Still, Baruel, you owe us one. We saved your hide.]

[Shut up! From here on out, I’ll handle things myself—]

Baruel stopped mid-sentence.

It wasn’t because of what his comrades had said.

It was because another arrow had been fired at him.

Ting!

He deflected the arrow with his blade and immediately turned his gaze to
the source.

Once again, the archer was there, calmly drawing their bowstring.

[What the—?! That human should already be dead! How are they still
alive?]

Baruel’s confusion was quickly resolved by one of his fellow angels.

[I saw it earlier. That human in white robes—she used a resurrection spell to
bring the archer back to life.]

[What?!]

Baruel’s face twisted in frustration.

A human capable of resurrection?

That information alone was enough to make his expression darken.

[How annoying. That one needs to die first.]

[Do you want us to help?]

[Don’t touch them! Every single one of these humans is mine to deal with.]

Leaving those words behind, Baruel shot toward his new target like an
arrow.

His goal was the healer.

Christine, realizing she had become the target, froze in terror.

[Die, you white-clad insect.]

Baruel raised his Feather Blade, ready to strike—

Boom—!

Suddenly, a fiery explosion struck the back of Baruel’s head.

The attack caused him to falter, halting the swing of his blade.

Turning around with a furious glare, Baruel saw the culprit: a mage who
was still pointing their staff at him.

Swoosh—!

At the same time, an ice spear shot toward Baruel’s face, aiming directly for
his eyes.

Clang! Clang!

Baruel managed to block the spear with his wings, but he felt a sharp sting.

These attacks were different.

The damage was far greater than anything he had experienced from the
players earlier.

[You damned humans are starting to annoy me…!]

He planned to kill the healer first and then rip that mage to shreds.

But when he turned back, the healer was already gone.

[What?! Where did she go?!]

Baruel trembled with rage.

Realizing the mage had distracted him long enough for the healer to escape,
he redirected his focus.

His new target was now the mage.

Baruel closed the distance in an instant, aiming his Feather Blade straight
for the mage’s heart.

Puk—!

“Ugh!”

Although the mage had a magical barrier in place, it was pierced through as
though it didn’t exist.

The mage, Alex, let out a pained groan as blood spurted from his chest.

“Alex!”

Min Juri, standing nearby, cried out in shock.

Baruel turned his attention toward her without hesitation.

[Annoying pests.]

Puk!

The Feather Blade pierced Min Juri’s body just as easily as it had Alex’s.

Her lifeless body collapsed to the ground.

It was such a swift and meaningless death.

And then,

Boom—!

With a deafening sonic boom, someone descended from the sky.

[What’s this? Another human?]

Baruel looked up, his gaze locking onto the figure who had appeared.

It was a human standing atop the night sky, as if the air itself were solid
ground.

The figure wore a strange white mask, their appearance eerily calm.

“Ah……”

The masked figure surveyed the battlefield.

The scene of carnage is reflected in his eyes.

And then, he spotted it.

“……Min Juri?”

His gaze fell upon the lifeless body of the woman lying on the ground.

Tap.

The masked man descended to the ground, his attention focused entirely on
Min Juri.

He walked slowly toward her, as if trying to confirm her condition.

Baruel, noticing this, sneered.

[I don’t know where you came from, human, but your luck has truly run out
—]

Before Baruel could finish his sentence, he felt a strange sensation.

The world seemed to spin around him, and then—

Thud.

His head hit the ground, separated from his body.

Before his corpse could even collapse completely, blood spurted out,
staining the earth.

[B-Ba…ruel……?]

The other first-class angels froze in place, their expressions hardening.

Not one of them had seen how it happened.

The only clue was the golden blood dripping from the blade of a scythe—
one held in the hands of the masked man.

Chapter 264: End Of The 16Th
Round (1)

Demiel couldn’t believe the situation unfolding before his eyes.

‘Ba, Baruel went down so easily…?’

Baruel, despite his foul temperament, was renowned for his exceptional
skill even among the 1st-class combat angels.

He wasn’t someone who would fall so effortlessly.

[“E-Everyone, be cau—”]

Demiel suddenly realized that no sound was coming out of his mouth.

Something blurred past his vision, and then his entire view spun.

Snap!

[You have defeated the 1st-class angel ‘Demiel’!]

[Stat points +10,876]

[Gold +108,760,768]

[Angels defeated: 4/100]

Demiel wasn’t the only one with a broken neck.

Snap! Crack! Pop!

In an instant, without anyone having the chance to react, the angels’ heads
twisted one by one.

Some collapsed instantly, struck in the chest by daggers of darkness.

Ten corpses soon littered the ground.

It was a pitiful end for the 1st-class combat angels.

‘Damn angel bastards.’

Behind his mask, Ryu Min was seething with rage.

If he had arrived just a little earlier, Min Juri’s death could have been
avoided.

‘No, it’s not too late yet.’

Ryu Min retrieved a life potion from his inventory.

A legendary potion capable of resurrecting the dead.

Fortunately, he still had one in his possession.

While it couldn’t revive someone who had been dead for more than 10
minutes or whose body was more than 30% destroyed…

‘Thankfully, Min Juri meets the conditions.’

Seeing a glimmer of hope, Ryu Min laid Min Juri’s corpse across his lap
and uttered the activation words.

“Use.”

The effect manifested immediately.

Her pierced heart and shattered armor mended as if it had all been a lie, and
warmth returned to her body.

Seeing her eyebrows twitch, Ryu Min let out a sigh of relief.

She had barely returned from the brink of death.

“Ugh…”

“Are you conscious?”

When Min Juri opened her eyes, she saw the familiar mask in front of her.

“B-Black Scythe…?”

“You seem fine, luckily.”

“When… when did you get here?”

“Just now.”

Still dazed, Min Juri looked around and began to grasp the situation.

“Ah, the angels—!”

“Don’t worry. I’ve taken care of them.”

Turning her head, she spotted the corpses of the angels, just as he said.

“Phew… It’s such a relief. You showed up just in time.”

“…”

Although Min Juri smiled in relief, Ryu Min couldn’t bring himself to smile
back.

Because of him, a 6th-class angel had become a 1st-class one.

This wasn’t how things were supposed to turn out.

‘If I had been on the island from the beginning, not a single casualty
would’ve occurred…’

He felt guilt toward the countless followers of the Death Church who had
died.

And toward Min Juri, who lay before him.

“Ah.”

Realizing that she was in Black Scythe’s arms, Min Juri quickly stood up,
flustered.

“Um, what exactly happened to me? I distinctly remember being stabbed by
an angel…”

She examined the spot where the sword had pierced her, but there wasn’t
even a scratch. Even her armor was as good as new.

“I revived you.”

“What?”

“You were dead, but I brought you back using a revival potion.”

“Oh…”

Min Juri fell silent for a moment as if only now realizing the gravity of
what had happened.

“Th-thank you, Black Scythe. You saved my life.”

“It’s nothing.”

Ryu Min brushed it off nonchalantly.

He’d already saved more lives than he could count.

But for Min Juri, this was far from a trivial matter.

After all, she had literally come back from the dead.

“Um, Black Scythe! Do you happen to have another revival potion?”

“Why do you ask?”

“There’s someone I want to save.”

Min Juri’s gaze shifted toward something—or someone.

Following her eyes, Ryu Min saw Alex’s lifeless body.

“He died protecting me…”

‘Alex died for Min Juri?’

The same Alex who had survived up to the 18th round without anyone’s
help—had sacrificed his life to save her.

The combat angels had changed the course of fate.

“I know it’s selfish, but… can you save him?”

Ryu Min had no intention of turning a blind eye to Alex’s death.

“I don’t have any more life potions.”

“Oh…”

“But I can still save him.”

Alex was a talent too valuable to lose.

“Chrissy!”

At his call, Christine approached, and Ryu Min pointed at Alex.

“Can you revive this man?”

“I’m sorry. I’ve already used my revival spell…”

Ryu Min read her thoughts and confirmed that she was telling the truth.

‘She used it to revive Dorothy.’

Revival spells had a cooldown of 60 minutes.

Considering that they could only be used on a corpse within 10 minutes of
death, this was the only window of opportunity.

‘What should I do? Ah!’

Ryu Min’s eyes scanned the group of people before him.

Finally, his gaze landed on someone.

“The alchemist.”

“Victor, do you have a life potion? There’s someone we need to save.”

“I’ve just finished making one.”

“Can you use it on this person?”

“Of course.”

Victor gladly complied with Ryu Min’s request.

As the potion was applied to Alex’s chest, his wounds healed, and he
regained consciousness.

“Ugh, w-what happened? The angels…”

“Black Scythe took care of them. I used a potion to save you.”

“Ah…”

Alex stared blankly before offering his gratitude to Victor and Ryu Min.

“Thank you. Thank you so much.”

Seeing Alex breathe a sigh of relief, Ryu Min smiled beneath his mask.

Chapter 264: End Of The 16Th
Round (2)

Alex stared blankly before offering his gratitude to Victor and Ryu Min.

“Thank you. Thank you so much.”

Seeing Alex breathe a sigh of relief, Ryu Min smiled beneath his mask.

With this, everyone he needed to save had been saved.

‘But far more people have died.’

Close to fifty people had been slain by the combat angels.

This massacre had occurred in mere minutes of his delay.

Even though half of them would eventually vanish, it didn’t sit well with
him to let them die at the hands of angels.

[Time remaining until the end of the round: 00:00:00]

[The round has ended!]

As the timer hit zero, the familiar voice of the guide angel echoed in their
minds.

[Time’s up. The round is now over. So, how did you do? Did you manage to
fend off the monsters? That little surprise during the sixth summon must’ve
caught you off guard, right? Hehe.]

“Did you know combat angels would appear?”

“So the guide is in on it too.”

“Fing angel b*!”

Assuming the angel couldn’t hear them, people muttered curses under their
breath.

And it was understandable.

The sudden appearance of the combat angels had led to countless deaths.

[There’s no need to be so shocked. It’s not like it’s your first time getting
blindsided by the system, is it? Hehe. Let’s see how many of you died. Hm?
528? Considering you were up against a 6th-class angel, more survived than
I expected.]

It wasn’t a 6th-class angel but a 1st-class one, though the information
transmitted to the angels seemed to say otherwise.

[In any case, since the majority survived, we’ll now move to the elimination
phase. Just like before, the first-place player will determine the rankings.]

“First place?”

People murmured, their eyes turning to Ryu Min.

They wondered if he would once again take the top spot.

[And what determines first place, you ask? It’s the player who dealt the
most damage to the angels.]

“It’s Black Scythe, then.”

“As expected…”

No one seemed surprised anymore. Everyone had already resigned
themselves to the inevitable.

As expected, a message appeared before everyone’s eyes.

[The player who dealt the most damage to the combat angels in the 16th
round is ‘Black Scythe.’]

[The player ‘Black Scythe’ has been given the authority to adjust the
rankings for the 16th round.]

[The player ‘Black Scythe’ has been given the authority to adjust the
rankings for the 16th round.]

[First place cannot assign themselves as the 1st rank.]

[Please assign ranks from 2nd place to 288th place.]

[2nd and 3rd place will receive special rewards, while the rest will receive
the same rewards regardless of rank.]

[Please say the name of the player you wish to assign as 2nd place aloud.]

Faced with this heavy responsibility once again, Ryu Min spoke the name
without hesitation.

“Min Juri.”

[2nd place is ‘Min Juri.’]

[Please assign the 3rd place.]

“Chrissy.”

As always, the 2nd and 3rd places were assigned to these two. They were
crucial party members and needed to be developed more intensively than
the others. Considering their contributions to the group, it was only natural
for them to hold those positions.

From 4th place to 15th, Ryu Min called names without much deliberation.

These were the key allies he intended to bring to the 20th round. Among
them were Alex and Dorothy, whose names also came up.

The two looked surprised, clearly not expecting to be ranked so high so
soon.

‘I’ll fill the remaining spots with Jo Yong-ho’s mercenaries.’

From 16th onward, he named mercenaries one by one. Afterward, he simply
assigned ranks to anyone who came to mind.

As the rankings neared the limit, the room filled with desperate pleas.

“Black Scythe! Please call my name! I’m begging you…”

“My name is ‘KoboldBlue’! Just once, please, just once…!”

Some of the Death Church members even knelt on the ground, begging
tearfully.

But Ryu Min remained resolute, calling names without wavering.

‘It’s not like this is easy for me. All of them are followers of the Death
Church who pledged themselves to me.’

For every name called, another would be left behind. The tickets were
limited, and the burden weighed heavily on him.

[Please assign the 288th place.]

“KoboldBlue.”

“Gasp! Thank you! Thank you so much!”

“Agh… no!”

“Why… why?!”

“Save me! I don’t want to die!”

As people screamed and pleaded, the final bus had already departed.

[The rankings have been finalized. The remaining 240 players who did not
make the top 288 will now be eliminated.]

“Ahhhhhh!”

“Save me!”

Fwoosh—

As the grim process of elimination unfolded, the cries of despair gradually
faded away. Finally, silence returned, leaving behind only the survivors.

With that, it was time for rewards to be distributed.

★ 16th Round Results ★

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

└ 1st: Black Scythe (Lv97 Reaper)

└ 2nd: Min Juri (Lv69 Buffer)

└ 3rd: Chrissy (Lv69 Priest)

[As a reward for clearing the 16th round, all surviving players will receive
experience points and gold.]

[EXP +113.4%]

[Gold +1,000,000]

[You have leveled up!]

Ryu Min’s level rose to 98.

‘Just one more level, and I’ll hit max level.’

Although he could use his points to immediately reach max level, he didn’t
intend to do that just yet. He wanted to save the invincibility buff granted at

max level for the perfect moment.

‘If I even get a chance to use it.’

[Congratulations! You’ve achieved 1st place in the rankings for this zone!]

[Your current rank is 1st in Unified Zone CA-EA001.]

[As a reward for ranking 1st in this zone, you’ve received the Infinite
Materials Pouch!]

[As a reward for ranking 1st in this zone, you’ve received the Special
Reward Selection Box!]

Once again, Ryu Min received the Infinite Materials Pouch. Though he
didn’t urgently need it, he had no intention of discarding it, especially since
it sometimes yielded rare materials he hadn’t seen before.

‘Maybe I’ll get something new this time, too.’

Deciding to check it out later, he focused on the Special Reward Selection
Box instead.

[Please choose one of the following special rewards.]

[Touch the reward you desire to select it.]

└ 1. Temporary Skill – Commander (Limited to Round 17)

└ 2. 5,000,000 Gold

└ 3. Information about Round 17

Chapter 265: Tell Me In Detail (1)

Commander.

A temporary skill useful in the 17th round.

‘Others might be tempted by Option 2, the 5 million gold, but I have no
reason to be.’

He had just surpassed 7 billion gold after defeating first-tier angels
moments ago.

With so much gold, he was more worried about when he’d even manage to
spend it all.

‘That’s why my choice is Option 1, Commander.’

When he selected the temporary skill, a conclusion message soon appeared.

◀ END OF ROUND 16 ▶

[Unified Zone CA-EA001]

└ Survivors: 288

[The 17th round will begin at midnight on May 1, 2023. See you in the next
round. Congratulations on surviving.]

---

Michael strode through the grand hall with an exceptionally grave
expression.

He had been summoned by none other than Nemesis, the Goddess of
Vengeance.

‘Damn it. Gabriel and Raphael are dead, too.’

Ordinarily, he might have welcomed their deaths, relieved that the Black
Scythe had not fallen.

But…

‘This leaves only me.’

The fact that there were no other archangels left to take the reins left
Michael in an agonizing bind.

Clunk, creeeak—

As he pushed open the grand doors and entered, the purple-skinned goddess
Nemesis glanced at him briefly.

[You summoned me, Nemesis.]

[Michael. Have you heard the news?]

[Yes. Even Gabriel and Raphael were defeated without much resistance.]

[That mere human is putting up more of a fight than expected.]

Nemesis’s face betrayed no signs of anger as she said this.

She simply looked down on him with a pitiful gaze.

[…I apologize.]

[There is no longer any honor left in the Heavenly Realm. Time is short,
and so are our opportunities.]

Letting out a sigh, Nemesis’s eyes sharpened.

[Archangel Michael, it is now your turn. You are all that remains.]

[…]

[When the 17th round begins, descend to the human realm and subdue the
Black Scythe. That will be your one and only chance. To ensure that
Plunictos receives the Black Scythe before the 18th round begins.]

Michael wanted to refuse, wanted to come up with excuses.

But…

[Understood. I will follow your command.]

Michael could only comply. He had no grounds left to make excuses.

---

Returning home, Min Juri felt strangely unsettled.

Typically, when she returned from the Otherworld, she would find herself
staring at her bedroom ceiling. But not this time.

This time, she could simply take a plane ride back home.

“I’m home.”

“My daughter! You survived again!”

Maybe it was because she had been overseas?

Her father greeted her even more warmly than usual, but Min Juri couldn’t
bring herself to smile wholeheartedly.

“What’s with your expression? Did something bad happen?”

“Not really… I’m just feeling a bit off.”

“Why? What is it? Tell me, Juri.”

After hesitating for a while, Min Juri cautiously opened up.

“I’m glad to be alive, but… seeing my teammates vanish right before my
eyes makes it hard to feel happy.”

Just a few hours ago, players who had fought alongside her as one team
were erased with a single word from the Black Scythe.

‘It wasn’t Black Scythe’s fault. It was inevitable.’

She understood that, but witnessing their eradication up close still left a
bitter aftertaste.

“I’ve seen others disappear so many times before, and I usually just felt a
little pity… But this time, it felt different.”

“How was it different?”

“I guess… I feel guilty for surviving? Like I owe an apology to the ones
who died.”

It was only natural for her to feel that way.

This time, her survival wasn’t thanks to her own efforts. She had lived
because the Black Scythe chose her.

Her father, Min Dohun, was at a loss for words, unsure of how to comfort
his melancholy daughter.

“Why don’t you go rest in your room for a bit? You’ll feel better after that.”

“…Okay.”

Click.

Closing the door behind her, Min Juri changed clothes and lay down on her
bed.

Staring at the ceiling for a while, she placed her hand on her chest.

The spot where her heart had been pierced was now perfectly healed.

There wasn’t even a trace of pain left.

It felt like a dream, as though she had never died in the first place.

‘If not for Black Scythe, I would’ve been…’

No matter how she looked at it, meeting the Black Scythe had been a stroke
of luck.

The image of herself in the Black Scythe’s arms flashed in her mind.

Blushing furiously, she pulled the blanket over her face.

‘I’ve lost it. What am I even thinking…?’

The Black Scythe was her benefactor, someone who had saved her life.
Nothing more.

‘The Black Scythe is a hero. The leader of the Death Church. I need to think
of him that way.’

As she cooled her flushed cheeks by tossing aside the blanket, a new
thought crossed her mind.

‘But what about Min?’

When the Black Scythe had ranked the players from 1st to 288th, Min Juri
had strained her ears to hear.

She had been fully prepared to catch the name “Lostyak,” Ryu Min’s
nickname.

‘But I didn’t hear it.’

What could have happened?

Did the Black Scythe deliberately leave the Prophet’s name out?

The thought gnawed at her, and as soon as the round ended, she searched
for Ryu Min on the island.

The results? Nothing matched.

The system kept saying his name and face didn’t align—a ridiculous claim.

‘Then what about now?’

With a glimmer of hope, Min Juri tried searching for Ryu Min again.

And then…

‘Huh?’

[Name and face match confirmed. Tracking target’s location.]

[Target “Ryu Min” is located 16,488 meters away.]

[Follow the arrow to pursue the target.]

The tracking system was working.

‘What’s going on?’

On the island, it had shown a mismatch. But now, it matched perfectly?

‘So he survived the 16th round…?’

Yet the Black Scythe hadn’t called out his nickname.

She was certain—she had listened carefully.

‘This doesn’t add up.’

She resolved to ask Ryu Min directly.

When she sent a text to arrange a meeting, his reply came soon after.

[Ryu Min: Now’s not a good time. Let’s meet later.]

[Min Juri: Why? What’s going on?]

[Ryu Min: My house got destroyed, and I’m busy sorting it all out.]

[Min Juri: What?! How did that happen?]

[Ryu Min: I don’t know the details either ㅠㅠ]

Worried, Min Juri decided to call him.

Chapter 265: Tell Me In Detail (2)

Worried, Min Juri decided to call him.

“Min, can you talk for a moment?”

“Yeah, sure.”

“What happened? Your house got destroyed?”

“I don’t know. There’s no footage on the CCTV either…”

“What about your younger sibling? Are they okay?”

“They’re safe. Thankfully, he was staying over at a friend’s house.”

“That’s a relief.”

“By the way, you said you had something to talk about earlier? Is it
urgent?”

“Oh? No, it’s nothing urgent. It’s just something I’d rather talk about when
we meet in person.”

“Alright then. Let’s talk once I get things sorted here.”

“Got it. But what about where you’ll stay? Do you have somewhere to go?”

“I’m already looking into decent hotels nearby. I’ll stay at one until the
repairs are done.”

“Okay, let me know once you’ve settled somewhere. Send me the address,
and I’ll come by.”

“Alright.”

“Take care for now. Talk later.”

After ending the call, Min Juri still wore a concerned expression.

‘What on earth happened?’

She didn’t know the details, but she realized her questions wouldn’t be
answered anytime soon.

Reluctantly, she decided to hold onto her curiosity for the time being.

---

can’t find it again. Can anyone explain in the comments?

[Comments: 12 Total]

└ I have no idea either. Can someone else clarify?

└ Here’s the article: http://news.nover.com//20220426. TL;DR: Monsters in
Round 16 spawned at the players’ locations, but the Black Scythe moved
everyone to an island in advance, preventing civilian casualties.

└ Technically speaking, there were zero casualties. No civilians were
harmed.

└ So if they hadn’t moved to the island, the monsters would have appeared

└ Yep, that’s exactly it.

└ Wow, if monsters had spawned in the city, it would’ve been catastrophic.

└ My son, who’s a follower of the Death Church, told me angels appeared

└

Huh Tae-seok couldn’t help but smirk as he read through the online

It was natural for him to feel pleased, given that the Church was being
lauded.

‘Every time I see posts like this, I feel so proud as the cult leader.’

The decision to evacuate to the island had been revealed, and the Death
Church’s reputation had soared because of it.

Not only the Black Scythe’s prestige but the standing of players affiliated
with the cult had also risen immensely.

However, Taeseok’s mood soured almost immediately.

‘I still didn’t make it into the top 3 this time.’

Once again, he hadn’t been named by the Black Scythe as one of the top 3
players.

Strictly speaking, he had been called—but he hadn’t ranked in the top 3.

‘What’s worse is that my ranking actually dropped.’

Previously, he had ranked 10th. But this time, the Black Scythe had called
his name at 13th.

For the Black Scythe, the rankings were arbitrary and meaningless. But
Taeseok couldn’t take it lightly.

‘Does this mean I’ve been underperforming?’

Taeseok interpreted the rankings as an unconscious evaluation by the Black

And he couldn’t help but feel dejected.

‘I have to prove my worth to Black Scythe. I need to show everyone,

This thought stemmed from a sense of duty.

‘What can I do to earn Black Scythe’s praise?’

He racked his brain for ways to benefit the Death Church and earn

Managing the cult members and maintaining the current situation seemed

“What if I end up being forgotten by Black Scythe…”

As this worrisome thought crossed his mind, there was a knock at his door.

“Cult Leader.”

“One of the believers wishes to meet with you. They say they have
something to report.”

“Something to report?”

Taeseok raised an eyebrow in curiosity before nodding.

“Let them in.”

Shortly after, a foreigner entered the room.

“Greetings, Cult Leader.”

Standing between them, Cardinal Eum served as the interpreter.

“And you are?”

“My name is Philip Robertson, from Scotland. My in-game nickname is
Kobolt Blue.”

“Ah, I see. So, what is it you wish to report?”

“Yes, well…”

After hesitating briefly, Kobolt Blue finally spoke.

“There’s something strange going on among the members.”

“Strange?”

“Yes. It seems that someone is forming factions within the Church.”

“Factions?”

Huh Taeseok’s eyes narrowed sharply.

“Tell me in detail.”
