Chapter 266: Faction (1)

The explanation from Kobolt Blue was straightforward.

“A foreigner was asking others to join their side.”

Heo Tae-seok furrowed his brow.

“A foreigner? Who?”

“I don’t know. I would’ve recognized them if their nickname had popped
up.”

“When and where did you hear that?”

“I overheard it by chance while leaving the island after the round ended.
That’s all I’ve got.”

Although the information was sparse, the implications were ominous.

“I think that foreigner might be trying to form a faction…”

Kobolt Blue’s opinion made Heo Tae-seok nod in agreement.

He had been thinking the same thing.

‘Splitting up followers of the Death Church, who should be united as one
team?’

Whoever it was, Heo Tae-seok couldn’t just stand by and let this slide as the
leader of the Church.

“Would you recognize that foreigner’s face if you saw them again?”

“Of course. I never forget a face.”

As soon as Kobolt Blue answered, Heo Tae-seok opened a drawer and
pulled out a stack of profile photos of the followers.

“Search for them. Let me know who that foreigner is.”

Kobolt Blue flipped through the hundreds of profiles containing
information on the followers. After some time, his finger stopped on one
photo.

“It’s this person!”

“Him?”

Heo Tae-seok narrowed his eyes at the culprit and couldn’t help but smirk
faintly.

‘Finally, an opportunity to do something that will help the Black Scythe.’

This time, he would deliver results worth noting. A spark of determination
flared in Heo Tae-seok’s eyes.

---

Life is full of twists and turns. Dorothy had come to realize this truth early
last year, the day an angel appeared before her.

[Every month, you humans must clear quests and survive. Until you clear
the 20th round.]

At first, she had thought it was a blessing from the heavens. Even when her
career as the youngest genius archer in the Netherlands was cut short due to
a car accident that left her with balance issues, she clung to this belief. Even
as her life spiraled downwards without her wings as an archer, she had held
onto the thread of life stubbornly.

But it all changed.

She came to believe this was not a blessing, but a divine way of telling her
to let go and end her suffering.

‘But I was wrong.’

Dorothy, who had suffered from severe depression that no medication could
cure, had no lingering attachments to life. She held no expectations.

But for some reason, a chance came to her.

With the customization system, she received a new body. That body no
longer had any disabilities.

Her balance had been restored. Her physique, strengthened as she became a
player.

That was when her outlook began to change. When the downward curve of
her life began to climb back up.

[Genius Archer Dorothy survives the 16th round!]

[The Godly Archer of the Netherlands: From tragedy to triumph as a
player.]

The titles of “Genius Archer” and “Godly Archer” returned to Dorothy in
the real world.

Though she could no longer resume her career as an athlete due to fairness
policies, Dorothy was content. She regained her skill with the bow,
surpassing her former abilities, thanks to the Rune of the Sharpshooter she
had acquired as an archer class player.

‘What’s so special about surviving that it keeps making headlines?’

Murmuring to herself, Dorothy set her phone down. She was no stranger to
the media’s obsession with her, having been famous even before becoming
a player. As such, it wasn’t surprising when someone showed up at her
home.

Her address was already public knowledge.

Ding-dong.

‘Another fan, perhaps?’

Thinking she’d have to shake a hand and sign an autograph, Dorothy
opened the door to her mansion, only to widen her eyes in surprise.

“Hello, we’ve met before, haven’t we?”

A chubby man with a friendly expression was smiling at her.

“Oh… your name was Alex, right?”

“You remember me. Dorothy, right? I’m sorry for the sudden visit.”

“W-well, come in.”

Dorothy led Alex to the sofa.

“Have a seat. Would you like something to drink?”

“No, no. I can’t impose when I’ve shown up unannounced. I’ll just get to
the point and leave.”

Sitting across from her, Alex met Dorothy’s gaze.

“I saw your skills while we were hunting monsters on the island. Your
archery is truly impressive. So, I have a proposition: would you lend me
your strength?”

“What do you mean? Could you explain more clearly?”

“I’d like you to team up with me.”

Dorothy didn’t react with shock but instead frowned deeply. It wasn’t just
the audacity of showing up at her home with such a request—it was also the
implications. Forming factions within the Death Church could easily sow
discord.

Most importantly, she saw no reason to join anyone’s team.

“I refuse. I won’t see you out, so please leave.”

“Wait a moment. Don’t dismiss me just yet. Hear me out.”

When Alex refused to leave and pressed on, Dorothy became irritated. She
was about to firmly kick him out when his next words made her doubt her
own ears.

“What did you just say? Is that true?”

“Yes. Are you interested now?”

The shock that had momentarily washed over her face disappeared,
replaced by intense focus.

“What you just said—tell me more in detail.”

Chapter 266: Faction (2)

Alex Pearson.

A man of German nationality, pointed out with absolute certainty by Kobolt
Blue.

“So, this guy is coaxing followers and forming his own faction?”

Heo Tae-seok pondered how best to deal with this ungrateful little rat. He
absentmindedly rubbed his temples.

“How foolish of me. I’m already thinking about punishing him when I don’t
even have solid proof yet.”

Blinded by his desire to achieve results as a leader, he realized he was
rushing things.

The priority was to confirm whether the information was true.

“Kobolt Blue might’ve misunderstood or misheard something.”

To confirm things properly, Heo Tae-seok began tracking Alex’s location. If
he followed the man long enough, he was bound to uncover something.

With this in mind, Heo Tae-seok activated the skill Demonization, a skill he
had acquired at level 60.

His skin turned crimson, his body grew by 30%, and horns sprouted from
his forehead. Bat-like wings emerged from his back.

Though his appearance was grotesque, the skill boosted his damage output
by 20% and allowed him to turn invisible while flying.

Flap-

Soaring into the sky, Heo Tae-seok carefully tailed Alex. Following the trail
eventually led him all the way to the Netherlands.

“Why is Alex here?”

The question didn’t linger long. The moment he spotted Alex, everything
clicked.

“He’s meeting with Dorothy?”

Dorothy and Alex were just leaving her mansion, parting ways with
cheerful expressions.

“This is highly suspicious.”

“Why is he traveling around the world meeting followers?”

The thought deepened as Alex headed to his next destination: Lagos,
Nigeria.

There, he entered a residential area and met with Victor, an alchemist. The
two had a lengthy conversation for over ten minutes before Alex left,
smiling as always.

“No matter how you look at it, this is shady.”

Why else would Alex be traveling globally, visiting the Church followers?

“Could he really be forming his own faction?”

The rumors might not be baseless after all. The need to interrogate Alex and
report to the Black Scythe grew urgent.

But Heo Tae-seok shook his head.

“No. Not yet. It’s too soon.”

He lacked sufficient evidence. Moving hastily could backfire. He resolved
to gather more definitive proof before taking action.

Flap-

For now, Heo Tae-seok turned back. He made a silent vow not to share this
with anyone.

“Rooting out this traitor must be my achievement alone.”

---

“Here we are.”

Ryu Min and John Delgado arrived at a familiar location—the burial ground
of the archangels.

Before leaving the island, John had resurrected several first-rank combat
angels using his advanced necromancy skills. Now, he skillfully recited an
incantation.

“Rise.”

As the physical undead forms of Gabriel and Raphael emerged, Ryu Min
wasted no time. In one clean motion, he decapitated them both.

Slash-!

[You have slain Gabriel, one of the Seven Archangels!]

[Stat Points +101,963]

[Gold +1,019,632,200]

[Archangels defeated: 23/100]

[You have slain Raphael, one of the Seven Archangels!]

[Stat Points +101,963]

[Gold +1,019,632,200]

[Archangels defeated: 24/100]

Though only half of the original rewards were granted, the stats and gold he
earned were still immense.

‘That’s enough. I’ve milked this for all it’s worth. I even resurrected the
first-rank combat angels and killed them before leaving the island.’

His base stats, bolstered by the Rune of Balance, were nearing 500,000.
With various buffs applied, each stat might soon exceed 10 million.

“Good work, John.”

“Thank you, Master.”

“You may return now. Remember to track me from a safe distance when the
17th round begins.”

“Understood. I’ll make sure to maintain a sufficient gap.”

The final archangel might appear in the 17th round. His current orders were
preparations for that possibility.

“Until then…”

As John departed, Ryu Min climbed into his Lamborghini and hit the road.

‘Time to head home. I can’t risk anything happening to my brother.’

Even archangels had begun targeting his brother. Without the Hero’s
Protection Buff, it was impossible not to feel uneasy.

Vroom- Vroom-!

The growling roar of the engine accompanied Ryu Min as he arrived at
Korea’s tallest structure, the Rangdae World Tower. While his damaged
home was undergoing repairs, he planned to stay at the Rangdae Signiel
Hotel, located on the 89th floor of the tower.

With its strict security and breathtaking views, it was the best choice
available.

‘One month’s stay cost me over a billion won, but compared to my wealth,
that’s a drop in the bucket.’

After parking his car, he took the elevator to the 89th floor.

Ding-

The luxury of the suite made every won spent feel worthwhile.

“You’re back?”

His younger brother greeted him with a bright smile as he enjoyed a meal
prepared by the hotel’s kitchen.

“The food here is amazing, hyung. Come eat!”

“Alright. Let me shower first.”

After a quick shower, Ryu Min dried his hair in his room while opening the
quest window.

└ Defeat all Seven Archangels

└ Current progress: (6/7)

└ Reward: ????

‘One more to go, and I’ll receive the reward.’

The prize remained a mystery, but he couldn’t help feeling anticipation. It
wasn’t surprising, considering the difficulty of the quest, which required
defeating seven archangels.

‘Well, it wasn’t as hard as I thought it would be.’

Thanks to the Demonic Blessing, his growth had long exceeded his
expectations. It wasn’t just extraordinary—it was astronomical, as if he had
broken through the heavens and into the stars.

‘I never imagined I’d become this strong.’

Now, even facing the strongest archangels wouldn’t intimidate him like
before. Ryu Min had evolved far beyond his past self.

‘Still, why didn’t that guy show up this time?’

He had been expecting the most powerful archangel to appear during the
16th round, just like in the previous timelines. But for some reason, the
enemy seemed to have deferred their confrontation to the next round.

‘Come at me whenever you want. I won’t be the frozen prey I was in the
68th regression.’

While drying his hair, Ryu Min decided to review the rewards he’d obtained
so far.

[Rune of Yin and Yang]

Effect: When physical and magical attacks are combined, damage is
doubled.

[Rune of Chains]

Effect: Summon chains of light to use as weapons. The chains have infinite
durability and can activate additional effects.

└ Restrain: Summon additional chains to completely bind the target’s
limbs.

└ Sever: Heat the chains with divine power to sever the target. Note: This
can also harm the user.

[Rune of Near-Death Survival]

Effect: If you suffer a fatal attack, you can reflect it once. After reflection,
the ability has a 720-hour cooldown.

“Not bad at all.”

The Rune of Yin and Yang was already familiar, but the other runes were
new rewards obtained from slaying archangels.

“Speaking of which, I also got that ‘Refined Aether’ item.”

Curious, Ryu Min opened the item’s information window. What he saw
made his eyes widen in astonishment.

Chapter 267: Why Didn’T You Tell
Me? (1)

[Refined Aether]

Category: Item

Description: Aether of the highest purity, capable of crafting items beyond
the God-grade tier. Emits a rainbow-colored radiance depending on the
angle of light.

The part that astonished Ryu Min wasn’t the rarity or purity itself.

‘Capable of crafting items beyond God-grade?’

Until now, Ryu Min had believed that the God-grade was the highest
possible tier.

But there’s something even higher than that?

‘Does that mean God-grade isn’t the ultimate level?’

He was so dumbfounded that a hollow laugh nearly escaped him.

Despite having gone through 99 regressions and proudly knowing all the
strategies and information for every round…

‘An item I didn’t know existed has appeared.’

The methods for combining it weren’t clear either. He could attempt a trial-
and-error approach, but he simply didn’t have the luxury of time for that.

‘If only I had a blueprint…’

It was a pity, but regardless, this was still a gain. After all, he’d discovered
the existence of an item he hadn’t known before.

And this was all thanks to defeating a Third-Rank Archangel or higher.

‘If I take down the First-Rank, what would I get then?’

The thought intrigued him, but right now, protecting his younger brother
was the top priority.

‘I’ll have to meet Heo Tae-seok later.’

To stack Hero’s Rune again like before, he would need Heo Tae-seok’s
demon-summoning skill.

When Ryu Min walked into the living room, his younger brother, Ryu Won,
eagerly waved him over.

“Hyung, this tastes amazing! You have to try it.”

“Really?”

As Ryu Min took a bite, he mulled over the taste.

“It really is good.”

While eating in front of the TV, Ryu Won finished first, leaned back, and
patted his belly.

“Ahh, that hit the spot.”

Then, looking at Ryu Min, he grinned bashfully.

“Why are you laughing?”

“Ha ha, it’s just… I still can’t believe it. My brother is the famous Black
Scythe…”

“Don’t believe me? Should I pull out the scythe and show you?”

“No, no, I believe you!”

There was no need to pull out the eerie scythe. Ryu Won already believed it.
How could he not believe it after witnessing his brother effortlessly
slaughter Archangels with his own eyes?

“I used to think you were weak because you were just a Prophet.”

“That’s prejudice talking.”

“You’re right. I did have a prejudice about it.”

The sight of his younger brother humbly admitting this was a little strange.

Could it be that learning about the Black Scythe had sparked a newfound
respect in him?

‘Come to think of it, he’s sitting a lot more upright now.’

On the surface, Ryu Won pretended to be calm, but internally, he was as
nervous as a new recruit on their first day in the military.

“Relax, Won-ah.”

“Huh? Was it obvious?”

“We’re family. Why are you so tense? Whether I’m the Black Scythe or the
Prophet, I’m still your brother.”

At Ryu Min’s warm smile and reassurance, Ryu Won finally allowed
himself to relax, his previously rigid body becoming noticeably looser.

“Sorry, I didn’t even realize I was tense.”

“Anyway, didn’t we say we’d talk about the things we didn’t get to before?
Ask me anything you’re curious about.”

Ryu Won had been waiting for this, and he immediately threw out a
question.

“When you went overseas all those times, was it to punish bad guys, not
because you had a girlfriend?”

“Of course. What girlfriend? I’ve never even been near Japan.”

“So you just used that as an excuse because you didn’t feel like
explaining?”

“Exactly.”

“Whoa…”

The Black Scythe’s exploits were well-known to the public. Defeating KF
forces in Nigeria, founding the CPF Unit, restoring domestic peace, and
helping countries in need—these were all monumental achievements.

But for Ryu Won, discovering that his brother had used “a Japanese
girlfriend” as a flimsy excuse was mind-blowing.

“You’re the one who jumped to conclusions. I figured it was a convenient
excuse, so I ran with it.”

“Then what about the Prophet class? Was that a lie too? You’re the only one
with the Grim Reaper class, right?”

“How do you even know my class is unique?”

“There’s this thing called Player Gallery. You can look it up, you know.
There are posts summarizing every mission ever completed.”

Ryu Min’s eyes widened in surprise.

“I didn’t realize information was being exchanged so freely.”

Civilians weren’t completely clueless about Players, as he’d assumed.

“As far as I know, I’ve never heard of a Prophet class except from you. So,
was that a lie too?”

After a brief moment of hesitation, Ryu Min nodded honestly.

“Yeah. The Prophet class doesn’t exist.”

“What? Then was all that stuff about seeing the future fake too?”

“Yeah. I just needed a cover for my Grim Reaper class.”

“Then how did you predict the lottery numbers?”

“Well, that’s…”

At this unexpected line of questioning, Ryu Min found himself stumped.

Should he tell his brother the most crucial truth?

‘Do I tell him? Or not?’

He hesitated, but his deliberation didn’t last long. At this point, revealing
the truth wouldn’t be an issue.

“Do you want to know the truth?”

“Yes.”

“It might shock you. Are you sure you’re ready for it?”

“There’s nothing left to shock me now.”

Ryu Won confidently answered, chuckling, but his expression froze the
moment Ryu Min spoke again.

“I’m a regressor.”

“What?”

The bombshell revelation left Ryu Won stunned.

“Wait… what did you just say? A regressor?”

“To be precise, you could say I’m from the future. Or for me, it’s
technically the past.”

“What are you talking about? Regression? That kind of thing can’t possibly
exist…”

“There’s something called the Rune of Time Reversal. It lets you regress up
to 100 times.”

“…”

“With it, I’ve been repeating countless rounds. I made plenty of mistakes
and had many failures along the way. I didn’t have any talent or special
abilities back then.”

Ryu Won could only stare, dumbfounded, as his brother’s confession
unfolded.

“When I died, I’d return to 10 minutes before the game began. I repeated
that over and over, defeating the same monsters, clearing the same rounds,
teaming up with the same people…”

As Ryu Min reflected on his past, Ryu Won held his breath.

Chapter 267: Why Didn’T You Tell
Me? (2)

“When I died, I’d return to 10 minutes before the game began. I repeated
that over and over, defeating the same monsters, clearing the same rounds,
teaming up with the same people…”

As Ryu Min reflected on his past, Ryu Won held his breath.

At first, he’d thought it was some kind of joke. But it wasn’t.

The look in his brother’s eyes made it clear—he was recounting memories,
not spinning a tale.

“It was rough. For someone like me, who had no talent. But in a way, those
100 lives were opportunities. A chance to reach Round 20 and escape this
godforsaken survival game.”

“…”

“Everything I’ve done until now was to clear the rounds. After countless
trials and errors, I figured out the most efficient and reliable path forward.
That’s how I became the Black Scythe.”

“Ah…”

Ryu Min smirked and placed a hand on his frozen brother’s shoulder.

“Do you believe me now?”

“Sort of…”

“I’m sorry I didn’t tell you sooner. But I had my reasons.”

“Reasons?”

“There was a past round where you were kidnapped because you were the
family of a regressor. I couldn’t risk that happening again, so I kept it from
you.”

“Ah…”

Ryu Won understood now.

His brother had kept the truth from him to protect him.

“Of course, I decided it was safe enough to tell you now. Or rather, there’s
no point in hiding it anymore since the Angels are already targeting you.”

At that, Ryu Won recalled the Angel that had attacked him.

“Why are the Angels targeting me?”

“Because you’re my only family. They can’t face me in a direct fight, so
they’re trying to take hostages.”

“…”

“Don’t worry. Even if Angels come after you, I’ll protect you.”

“Hearing that from the Black Scythe is pretty reassuring.”

Ryu Won smiled, but deep down, anxiety gnawed at him.

It was only natural. After all, he was just a normal person.

“I get it, Won-ah. But you really don’t have to worry. No matter what, I’ll
protect you. Even if it costs me my life.”

Clearing the rounds hadn’t just been about his own survival.

It had always been about ensuring his brother’s safety so they could live a
peaceful life together.

‘If we could just return to a normal life, I wouldn’t want anything more.’

But to achieve that, his brother’s safety had to come first.

‘I should meet Heo Tae-seok as soon as possible.’

While Ryu Min was lost in thought, Ryu Won muttered under his breath.

“My brother… a regressor, like something out of a novel… Someone who
knows the future…”

“Don’t be too shocked. I mean, in a world where people can be resurrected,
a regressor isn’t that big of a deal.”

“Still, this feels different. You said you had 100 chances, right? Even if each
round only lasted a year, that’s 100 years… Whoa!”

Maybe it was the realization of his brother’s true age.

Ryu Won suddenly started looking at Ryu Min like he was a senior citizen.

“Be honest. How old are you?”

“What do you mean? I’m 21.”

“No, I mean if you count all the years you’ve lived!”

“Over 100. That’s all you need to know.”

Ryu Won’s jaw dropped.

“So… what round is this?”

“The 100th. The last one.”

“…”

“If I die this time, it’s over. No more chances to change the future.”

“Ah…”

At that moment, Ryu Min’s phone rang.

The caller ID read Seo Arin.

“Yes, actress.”

“Prophet, are you okay? Your place was completely wrecked…”

“I’m fine.”

“What about your brother?”

“He’s safe too. No need to worry.”

“I’m so glad. But what happened?”

Seo Arin’s voice was filled with genuine concern, not just curiosity.

“I don’t know either. I came back to find it in that state.”

“Where will you stay now?”

“Probably a hotel while repairs are done.”

“I was so shocked. I came by to visit and saw the mess… I can’t tell you
how scared I was.”

“Thank you for your concern.”

“Promise you’ll come back when it’s fixed, okay? Neighbor?”

“Of course. This house cost too much to abandon.”

“I’m relieved neither of you got hurt. Let’s talk again soon.”

“Sure.”

The moment Ryu Min hung up, Ryu Won asked, “Who was that?”

“Seo Arin.”

“She seems worried. Does she not know who you really are?”

“Of course not. Who would I tell? You’re the only one who knows.”

In truth, Christine knew, but he didn’t see the need to mention that. His
brother didn’t need to know about her.

“Why didn’t you tell Seo Arin? That you’re the Black Scythe?”

“She’d be too shocked.”

“She might take it well, like I did.”

“Did you really take it well?”

“Ha ha…”

Maybe he was remembering how he’d been too stunned to speak earlier
because Ryu Won scratched the back of his head awkwardly.

“Well, I got over it quickly. You explained your reasons.”

“That’s because you’re family. Most people wouldn’t understand.”

“But shouldn’t you try telling her? You never know.”

Ryu Min shook his head.

No matter how much he thought about it, it wasn’t a good idea.

Revealing his identity wouldn’t help him right now. It could even destroy
relationships.

‘Still… I can’t keep it hidden forever.’

It was something he’d have to think about eventually.

Just then, his phone buzzed again.

When Ryu Min checked the caller ID, his eyes widened in surprise.

Chapter 268: At The Hotel (1)

‘Christine?’

Upon answering the phone, Ryu Min heard a worried voice.

“Prophet? Are you okay?”

“What are you talking about all of a sudden?”

“I stopped by your house, and I heard it was destroyed.”

Ryu Min let out a low sigh.

There wasn’t a single person who didn’t know what had happened.

“It turned out that way somehow. But you stopped by my house? Are you in
Korea right now?”

“Yes. Not only that, I’m actually in front of the hotel.”

“…What?”

Startled, Ryu Min immediately used the tracking feature to locate Christine.

“[A match has been found for the face and name. Tracking the target’s
location.]”

“[Target ‘Christine Craig’ located.]”

“[The target is currently 78 meters away.]”

“[Follow the arrow ahead to pursue the target.]”

She really was nearby, just in front of the hotel.

It seemed like Christine had tracked him down using the same feature.

“Since I’ve come all the way here, could I see you for a moment?”

“…Fine.”

Ending the call, Ryu Min grabbed his coat and spoke to his brother.

“I’m going out to meet someone.”

“Who?”

“A colleague.”

Following the tracking arrow, Ryu Min soon spotted Christine sitting in the
hotel lobby.

“Ah, Ryu Min!”

“Why are you here without a word of notice?”

“I’m sorry. When I saw the state of your house, I got worried…”

“Come with me.”

Ryu Min took Christine to a nearby café.

“What would you like to drink? Choose whatever you want, it’s on me.”

“No, I’m the one who showed up unannounced. How could I possibly…”

“Even so, as my guest, I can’t not treat you to something. Pick whatever
you’d like.”

“T-thank you.”

Christine only ordered a simple cup of coffee.

After ordering the same for himself, Ryu Min got straight to the point.

“I thought you went back to America… What made you come to my
house?”

“Ah, it’s nothing special. Last time, you came all the way to America to
share a prophecy, didn’t you? So I thought this time it was my turn to visit
you…”

“Is that really all?”

“Yes…”

Ryu Min quietly stared at Christine, scrutinizing her like an interrogator.

Though his gaze was sharp, Christine averted her eyes, blushing slightly in
embarrassment.

‘It’s true. She really came here for no other reason.’

Ryu Min sighed internally, realizing that her reasoning was as trivial as it
seemed.

Yet, at the same time, he felt thankful.

No matter how indifferent one tries to act, it’s hard not to feel moved when
someone is genuinely worried about you.

“Um, I-I’m sorry.”

Christine, misunderstanding Ryu Min’s continued staring as anger,
apologized again, feeling flustered.

“I should’ve let you know before coming… It must’ve felt sudden.”

“It was sudden, yes.”

“I really am sorry. But what happened? Why is your house in such a
state…?”

“An angel paid me a visit.”

“…What?”

Since Christine already knew who he really was, Ryu Min decided there
was no point in hiding the truth.

“You might not know this, but the angels see me as their mortal enemy.
However, I didn’t expect they’d come to my house and target my brother.”

“Th-they targeted your brother? Is he okay?”

“Luckily, I arrived in time to save him.”

“And what about the angel? What happened to them?”

“What do you think happened?”

Ryu Min smirked slightly.

That cynical smile was enough of an answer.

“It’s a relief that no one was hurt.”

“I think so too.”

“So that’s why you returned to the island so late… You were dealing with
the angel, weren’t you?”

“That’s right.”

“This kind of thing shouldn’t happen again…”

“Exactly. Lately, I’ve been on edge because of it. The thought of losing my
brother…”

Just imagining it seemed to unsettle him, and Ryu Min turned to look out
the window.

The expanse of the clear sky and the toy block-like city below offered a bit
of solace.

But the lingering unease in his eyes didn’t fade, prompting Christine to look
at him with concern.

“Are you okay?”

“Yes, I’m fine.”

“Um, I don’t know how this will sound, but…”

Christine hesitated for a moment, then summoned her courage.

“If there’s anything you need, feel free to use me however you want.”

“…What?”

“I mean it. If it weren’t for Black Scythe, I’d already be dead. So don’t
hesitate—use me for anything. If you need someone to stay by your
brother’s side 24/7, I’ll do it. I might not have the power to stop an angel,
but isn’t something better than nothing?”

The idea of using Christine like a tool left Ryu Min momentarily
speechless.

He never imagined he’d hear such words from her.

“Use me and throw me away if you must. Whatever it is, I just want to help
you. I mean it.”

Ryu Min silently stared at Christine.

‘She’s serious. I can tell even without reading her mind.’

Her determination to help, no matter what, was unmistakable.

“I appreciate the offer, but for now, there’s nothing I need help with.”

“If I could stay by your brother’s side—”

Ryu Min shook his head firmly.

“The angel I faced was no ordinary foe. As a supporter, you wouldn’t even
be able to serve as a basic shield.”

“I see…”

Christine’s shoulders drooped at his brutally honest words, but it couldn’t
be helped.

Christine was an important asset. He couldn’t afford to lose her
meaninglessly as a shield.

Sipping her coffee, Christine looked like a puppy caught in the rain, pitiful
and dejected.

It was clear that helping Black Scythe was her only source of happiness.

Feeling compelled to add something, Ryu Min spoke again.

“That doesn’t mean I’m rejecting your offer of help. I promise I’ll call you
if something comes up.”

“Really?”

When he nodded, Christine’s face lit up noticeably.

“You promised! If there’s anything I can do to help, you’ll call me, right?”

“You’re already helping plenty.”

“No, supporting you as part of the team is a given. I want to help you
personally.”

“Alright, alright. I promise.”

Ryu Min didn’t see any harm in agreeing.

Though he couldn’t treat an important ally like Christine recklessly, keeping
her motivated was worth it.

“Shall we go if you’re done?”

“Yes.”

The two left the café.

As they stood in front of the elevator, they exchanged parting words.

“I’d like to see you off at the airport, but I can’t risk leaving my brother
alone.”

“I understand. If you need anything, call me anytime. I’ll hop on a plane
and come straight to you.”

With that, Christine stepped into the elevator, smiling and waving as the
doors closed.

Chapter 268: At The Hotel (2)

While Ryu Min entered the lobby restroom, Min Juri stood frozen,
organizing the scene she had just witnessed in her head.

‘Why did Christine meet Ryu Min?’

When Ryu Min’s name had appeared in her tracking results, Min Juri
decided to follow it to confirm if it was truly the Ryu Min she knew.

That’s how she had ended up at the hotel, where she coincidentally spotted
a woman in the lobby who looked just like Christine.

She then saw Christine meet with Ryu Min, go to a café, drink coffee, and
have a conversation.

‘What kind of conversation could they be having?’

Worried that she might get caught if she moved closer, Min Juri hadn’t
dared to eavesdrop. She had kept her distance, watching from over 30
meters away.

But seeing Christine’s expressions—from a worried frown to sudden,
radiant smiles—left Min Juri feeling unsettled.

‘What are they talking about that’s making her smile like that…?’

It was obvious to any third party that she was feeling jealous, but Min Juri
herself hadn’t realized it yet.

‘Did Ryu Min call her here? He said he’d let me know first once he found a
place to stay, so why Christine…?’

Was this what people meant by a love triangle?

Her thoughts became a tangled mess.

She felt stressed for the first time in a while, but she knew there was no
point in trying to figure it out on her own.

The clearest solution was to ask Ryu Min directly.

‘I’ll ask him when he comes out.’

And so, she fixed her gaze on the restroom entrance, waiting for him to
reappear.

But no matter how long she waited, he didn’t come out.

‘What’s going on? Is he… taking care of a big problem in there?’

“Min Juri.”

“Whaaa!”

A voice suddenly called out from behind, causing Min Juri to jump and spin
around.

It was Ryu Min.

Her heart, which had just recently been revived, nearly stopped again.

“You scared me!”

“So, you’re the one who was following me?”

“W-wait, you knew?”

Ryu Min smirked at the flustered Min Juri.

‘Of course I knew. My presence detection range is 60 meters.’

But he didn’t bother explaining that part.

“What are you doing here?”

“Uh, um, well…”

“You tracked me using the tracking feature too, didn’t you?”

“You too…? What do you mean by that?”

“Christine. She also tracked me down here using the feature.”

“Oh…”

So, Ryu Min hadn’t called Christine after all.

Just like Min Juri, Christine had used the tracking feature to find him on her
own.

That cleared up a small misunderstanding.

“I was planning to send you my address anyway, but since you’re here, we
might as well talk now.”

“Okay.”

The two of them went to sit at a café.

It was the same café where Ryu Min had just met Christine.

“Order something to drink. It’s on me.”

“What about you?”

“I already had something earlier, as you probably saw.”

“S-sorry. I didn’t mean to spy or anything…”

“It’s fine.”

Nodding as if he understood, Ryu Min waited until Min Juri’s coffee arrived
before diving into the topic.

“What did you want to talk about?”

“Huh?”

“On the phone, you said you had something to talk about. What is it?”

Min Juri hesitated for a moment, taking a deep breath before finally
speaking.

“You… lied to me, didn’t you?”

“What are you talking about?”

“Your nickname. Is it really Lostyak?”

“…”

“After the round ended when the Black Scythe called out names, I made
sure to pay attention. But I didn’t hear that nickname. What’s going on?”

“Well, that’s…”

“And that’s not the only strange thing.”

It seemed Min Juri had decided to address all her suspicions at once.

“When I use the tracking feature, even though I know your name and face,
it says there’s no match.”

“…”

“I’m not talking about the tracking feature from the Otherworld. I mean the
one in reality. I’ve never seen your Otherworld appearance, so that’s
whatever, but the fact that you can’t even be tracked in real life—doesn’t
that seem odd?”

“…”

“And there’s more. On the deserted island, no matter how hard I looked, I
couldn’t find you. Even though the rest of us weren’t customized avatars
but our real selves.”

The numbers matched, but Ryu Min himself couldn’t be seen?

It was enough to seem suspicious.

“Were you even on the island in the first place?”

Ryu Min stayed silent.

Min Juri seemed to be framing her questions as though she already had the
answers.

‘She’s right, of course.’

But they were answers he couldn’t reveal.

They were secrets he had to keep.

To explain them would mean revealing his true identity.

And yet, a particular conversation suddenly crossed Ryu Min’s mind.

-‘Would it really be so bad to reveal your identity? Not everyone would be
as shocked as you think.’

It was his brother’s voice, echoing in his memory.

Why was he remembering that now?

‘Maybe… she’ll understand.’

A sudden impulse made Ryu Min curious to test it out.

Before he knew it, he opened his mouth.

“I’m the Black Scythe.”

Chapter 269: Are You Joking? (1)

When asked if he was Lostyak, a strange answer came back.

“Black Scythe? Are you joking?”

“I’m telling you, I am Black Scythe.”

Even after repeating himself, Min Juri refused to believe it easily.

“Stop joking around. I’m being serious here.”

“I’m serious too.”

“There’s no way you’re Black Scythe.”

As if it wasn’t even worth considering, Min Juri dismissed the idea outright.

She didn’t seem to entertain even the slightest possibility that Ryu Min
could be Black Scythe.

For Ryu Min, who was being honest, the situation felt absurd.

It also bruised his pride, if only a little.

He couldn’t help but wonder: Is there really such a big gap between me and
Black Scythe right now?

“Why can’t I be Black Scythe?”

“For one, your height is completely different. Your voice, your vibe,
everything about you is just… different. You’re two completely different
people.”

“…….”

Seeing her deny it so strongly, it seemed that his effort to appear different,
as part of his persona, had been quite successful.

So there’s no room for reconsideration, huh?

While he could prove it, her strong denial made him question whether it
was even worth it to tell the truth.

Besides, he felt somewhat uneasy about what kind of fallout might occur if
he proved his claim.

“If you’re going to come up with an excuse, at least make it a convincing
one.”

“Fine. I’ll tell you the truth. I lied to you. My nickname isn’t Lostyak.”

“So I was right, huh? No wonder I couldn’t find you in the search.”

She didn’t believe he was Black Scythe but accepted this explanation
readily.

At this rate, there’s no choice. I’ll have to hide my identity until the end.

Ryu Min concealed the truth with a plausible lie.

“When I said my nickname was Lostyak, it was back when we were with
the Death Church, right? There were a lot of people around back then, so I
deliberately gave a fake name.”

“Why?”

“Because it’d be a problem if the existence of the Prophet became known. It
was my way of protecting myself. Attracting unnecessary attention
would’ve been a burden.”

“Ah….”

She opened her mouth as if she understood but still seemed unsatisfied.

“Then what’s with the mismatch between your name and your appearance?”

“I have a rune that disrupts tracking from others. Even if someone knows
my face and name, they won’t be able to track me because of it.”

“Ah….”

It was a fairly reasonable explanation.

(He’s not lying to me because he doesn’t want to tell me, is he?)

Reading her thoughts, Ryu Min could tell Min Juri wasn’t completely
convinced, though she seemed to have accepted it for now. She probably
figured he’d tell her the truth when the time was right.

I told her the truth, and she still doesn’t believe me.

To Min Juri, the idea of Ryu Min being Black Scythe seemed
inconceivable, even in her imagination.

In a way, it’s a relief. If this is how she reacts now, the shock when she
eventually finds out will be even greater….

He secretly hoped she’d continue not believing him.

Although he’d cleared up some misunderstandings, Min Juri still looked
dissatisfied.

“Then what about Chrissy? Why did she come looking for you?”

So that’s what’s been bothering her?

Well, it wasn’t unreasonable. If the man you liked met with another woman
alone at a hotel, it was bound to upset you.

“It’s nothing. She just came to hear my prophecy for the next round. Don’t
get the wrong idea.”

“She came looking for you without even saying anything just to hear a
prophecy?”

“And you came looking for me without saying anything too.”

“…….”

Min Juri, momentarily at a loss for words, finally admitted she might’ve
misunderstood.

“I’ll believe you. That there’s nothing between you two.”

“And what if there was something?”

“There can’t be! You’re mine…!”

Min Juri, flustered, quickly shut her mouth.

She’d almost said something embarrassing.

“Anyway, it’s not okay! Don’t give any attention to anyone else, got it?”

“Got it.”

Clearly embarrassed by what she said, Min Juri turned her head away
sharply and sipped her coffee.

For Ryu Min, who could see through her thoughts, her actions only seemed
sweet.

“While I’m here, I’ll share the strategy for Round 17.”

“…Uh, okay.”

---

Meanwhile, Heo Tae-seok sat deep in thought in the Church Leader’s
Office.

Currently, there was only one person occupying his mind.

Alex Pearson. Is he really dividing people from the inside?

From what he’d observed so far, Alex had met with five individuals:
Dorothy, Victor, Sophia, Russell, and Joo Yong-ho.

All of them were followers of the Death Church.

Why meet with them directly? For what purpose?

He couldn’t eavesdrop on their conversations, but it was suspicious
nonetheless.

For Alex to personally visit them while traveling around the world meant it
was likely something important.

He’s definitely up to something.

While Heo Tae-seok had a strong hunch, he lacked solid evidence.

If I could just gather evidence, it could help Black Scythe….

At that moment, his phone buzzed on the desk.

When he saw the caller ID, Heo Tae-seok hurriedly answered the call.

“Yes, Black Scythe. What’s the matter?”

“How many days until the regular gathering?”

Heo Tae-seok’s eyes shifted to the calendar on his desk.

“About four days left.”

“Move it up to tomorrow.”

“Tomorrow?”

That meant gathering all the followers by the next day.

“Is something happening?”

“Remember the work we did together last time?”

“The work… you mean planting the Black Seeds among people?”

“Yes. We need to do it again. While we’re at it, I’ll also share the strategy
for Round 17.”

To summon a demon and kill it again—such a ridiculous task.

He didn’t know why, but if it was an order from Black Scythe, it had to be
followed.

“Understood. I’ll summon the followers right away.”

Though he ended the call with a calm voice, Heo Tae-seok’s expression
shifted to one of anxiety the moment it ended.

What do I do? I’ll have to meet Black Scythe sooner than expected.

The original plan was to secure evidence that Alex was a traitor and reveal
it publicly in Black Scythe’s presence.

But with the meeting moved up, time was running out.

I have to secure evidence. No matter what.

As he racked his brain, only one method came to mind.

I’ll have to ask him directly.

Chapter 269: Are You Joking? (2)

Heo Tae-seok composed a group text and sent it to all the followers:

[Greetings, this is Church Leader Heo Tae-seok.

The regular meeting, originally scheduled for Friday, has been moved to
Tuesday at 6 p.m. I apologize for the sudden change in schedule.

Despite the short notice, Black Scythe will be sharing the strategy for the
next round at the meeting, so please ensure your attendance without fail.
Thank you.

Hello everyone, this is leader Heo Tae-seok. The regular meeting…]

Heo Tae-seok thoughtfully included a polite English translation for those
who didn’t speak Korean. However, there was one person to whom he sent
a different message: Alex Pearson.

Instead of the usual meeting location and time, Heo Tae-seok gave Alex a
separate time and address.

With this, I’ll be able to meet him alone.

It wasn’t a simple mistake. He had deliberately chosen to meet Alex
separately to extract evidence directly from him.

Upon receiving the message, Alex immediately booked a flight.

Traveling from Germany to South Korea took approximately 10 hours,
which left little time to waste.

I don’t know why they suddenly changed the time, but…

He couldn’t afford to miss the meeting.

After all, didn’t they say that Black Scythe would share the strategy for
Round 17?

Even if I’m in my underwear, I have to make it no matter what.

Fueled by such resolve, Alex arrived at Incheon International Airport as
quickly as possible and showed the meeting address to a taxi driver.

“Here. Take me here.”

“Huh? Sir, are you sure about this address? It’s just an empty field…”

“Please go fast. Okay? I’m late.”

“Late, huh? Fine, fine. As long as I get paid, I don’t care.”

Setting his doubts aside, the taxi driver drove to the specified location,
dropped Alex off, and promptly left—leaving Alex standing alone in the
middle of an empty lot.

“This is the place, right? So why is no one here?”

Even though he had arrived 20 minutes late, the field was completely
deserted.

Alex couldn’t make sense of the situation, but his confusion didn’t last long.

Someone was approaching.

“Leader!”

The person walking toward him was none other than Heo Tae-seok.

Alex greeted him with a friendly smile, but the mood quickly shifted.

What’s going on here?

Alex’s sharp instincts picked up on the tense atmosphere.

Heo Tae-seok’s expression was unusually stiff, and he was even wearing his
combat gear.

“Leader, you don’t look so good. Is something wrong…?”

“Alex.”

Cutting off Alex’s words, Heo Tae-seok spoke in English—something he’d
prepared in advance.

“Tell me the truth.”

“Excuse me? What are you talking about…?”

“No lies. Just the truth.”

Alex didn’t know what he was being asked to confess, but the heavy
atmosphere left no doubt that this was serious. He could feel a distinct
hostility in Heo Tae-seok’s gaze.

Wait, could it be…?

For Heo Tae-seok to show up in full combat gear to meet a follower—it
wasn’t a good sign.

It was as if he were warning Alex not to try anything, like showing someone
a gun to intimidate them.

Something’s definitely off. He’s hostile toward me.

Sensing the danger, Alex quickly equipped his own combat gear.

It was only natural—if you felt threatened, you had to be ready to defend
yourself.

However, Heo Tae-seok seemed to have anticipated this. A smirk spread
across his face as he activated a skill.

“Black Chains.”

Chains materialized out of thin air, wrapping around Alex and binding his
limbs.

Even though Alex had equipped his gear, he was rendered immobile. His
eyes flared with anger.

“What do you think you’re doing?!”

“If you tell the truth, you won’t have to suffer.”

Summoning a black arrow, Heo Tae-seok aimed it directly at Alex and
spoke in his prepared English:

“What are you scheming, huh?”

“Scheming? What are you even talking about…?”

“Don’t play dumb. I already know everything, so spill it!”

Heo Tae-seok growled.

The black arrow hovering above his shoulder looked ready to pierce Alex’s
heart at any moment.

“Dorothy, Victor, Sophia, Russell, Jo Yong-ho!”

Hearing the names, Alex’s eyes widened in shock.

“You met with these people, didn’t you? Why did you contact them?”

“How do you even know that…?”

Realization dawned on Alex, and his expression darkened.

“Don’t tell me… you’ve been following me?”

“Tell me the truth—”

BOOM!

Before Heo Tae-seok could finish, Alex shattered the chains binding him
with a burst of mana. The force of the explosion sent Heo Tae-seok flying
backward.

At the same time, the chains that had restrained Alex vanished.

“You were tailing me? Why? Why?!”

“Dammit, this bastard dares to attack me…?”

Heo Tae-seok gritted his teeth in frustration.

Though he hadn’t sustained any injuries, Alex’s actions were a clear sign of
hostility.

“Devil Transformation.”

As a pair of black horns sprouted from Heo Tae-seok’s forehead, his
appearance transformed into that of a demon.

Seeing the four black arrows floating menacingly around Heo Tae-seok,
Alex narrowed his eyes.

“So that’s how you want to play, huh?”

It seemed Alex wasn’t planning to back down either. A spear of ice began to
form in his hands.

The situation was on the verge of erupting into an all-out battle.

“Enough. Stop.”

At that moment, a voice interrupted them.

But it was already too late.

“Huh!”

Both men had already launched their attacks at each other.

BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!

The magic attacks collided mid-air, only to hit someone who had stepped
between them.

The destructive power of the 70-level spells could easily rip through a
human body, but the person struck wasn’t an ordinary human.

“That… that’s…!”

Where the attacks had landed, a barrier of darkness emerged, shielding the
person completely.

As the dark shield dissipated, the figure standing unscathed was revealed.

A man with bronzed skin, not a single scratch on his body, stood before
them.

“What are you doing? Fighting amongst allies?”

The man wore a mask. His deep, low voice carried an undeniable authority.

Chapter 270: The Start Of The
17Th Round (1)

“Y-You’re… Black Scythe!”

Heo Tae-seok and Alex lowered their weapons with shocked faces.

To think they had attacked the Black Scythe himself.

It wasn’t intentional, but it was an unthinkable mistake.

“Are you okay!?”

“As you can see.”

“I-I’m so sorry, Black Scythe, sir.”

“By the way, what brings you here…?”

At Heo Tae-seok’s question, Ryu Min only gave a subtle, unseen smile.

He couldn’t possibly admit that he had been tailing Alex.

‘I got a tip from Eom Jun-seok. Alex is building a faction, he said.’

Chasing Alex to confirm the impossible claim had led him here.

He hadn’t expected to find him fighting Heo Tae-seok, though.

“How I got here doesn’t matter. What matters is why allies like you two
were fighting in the first place.”

“Black Scythe, sir! I can explain everything!”

As if he had been waiting for the chance, Heo Tae-seok shot Alex a glare
and began spilling everything to Ryu Min.

“For the past week, that guy has been meeting with followers for some
reason—Dorothy, Victor, Sophia, Russell, Jo Yong-ho, and others. I
personally saw him secretly meeting these people of different nationalities.
He’s clearly plotting something malicious, trying to form a faction among
the followers to undermine our Death Church!”

It was the same as what Eom Jun-seok had reported, though Heo Tae-seok’s
account was more detailed, likely due to his personal investigation.

“I’ve heard your side. Now I need to hear the other side as well.”

Ryu Min turned his head toward Alex.

“Alex.”

“Yes, Black Scythe, sir.”

“Do you have anything to say for yourself?”

Speaking in fluent English, Ryu Min asked, and Alex furrowed his brow
before passionately explaining, pointing his staff at Heo Tae-seok.

“Black Scythe, sir! Be cautious of Heo! He lured me here with a false
message, then suddenly used a skill to restrain me and threatened to kill
me!”

“And you don’t know why?”

“I have no idea! He kept demanding that I confess to some scheme, but I
swear I’ve done no such thing!”

“Hm…”

Alex wore an expression of utter grievance.

Was he telling the truth?

This was where the Rune of Insight came in handy—it eliminated the need
to agonize over the truthfulness of someone’s words.

‘He’s telling the truth.’

Though Alex looked utterly wronged, it was easy to doubt anyone endlessly
once suspicion took root. But Alex was speaking sincerely.

“Contrary to your claim, Heo Tae-seok believes you’re plotting some sort of
sinister scheme…”

“A scheme? Me? That’s absurd!”

“He thinks so because he caught you secretly contacting followers from all
over the world. He believes you’re forming a faction behind everyone’s
back.”

“Ah…”

“Is that true?”

“It’s not true! I did plan to form a team, but…”

“A team?”

Alex confessed the reason he had been gathering people.

“During the 16th round, seeing everyone fight the monsters together made
me realize something. How strong we are when united. That’s what
teamwork really means. But then, watching my comrades get slaughtered
by the angels, I came to a conclusion. Teamwork won’t last forever. We
can’t save all 576 people. Eventually, the numbers will dwindle… until only
a small elite survives.”

Alex’s voice grew heavy, like a sponge soaked with water.

“So I made up my mind. To survive more efficiently, I decided to form a
team. If I could select skilled members and train them for teamwork, it’d
make survival easier, wouldn’t it?”

“Because it’s impossible for all 288 of us to synchronize as one team?”

“Exactly. If I pre-select people who’ll be useful in the future and form a
small elite team, we’ll be able to respond more flexibly when crises hit.”

Ryu Min nodded, signaling his agreement.

Alex’s argument was this: identify those capable of surviving until the 20th
round and get them accustomed to teamwork early.

While it sounded cold and calculated, it was also rational.

In a way, it wasn’t so different from what Ryu Min himself had been doing.

“So you were planning to gather competent people to train them in
teamwork beforehand.”

“Yes, sir. I had no ambitions for leadership or malicious intent.”

“But Heo Tae-seok thought otherwise. He assumed you were forming a
faction to betray the Death Church.”

“Ha… Absolutely not! Why would I betray anyone? What would I even
gain from betraying, especially with you around, Black Scythe, sir?”

Alex shouted as if utterly wronged, his cry brimming with sincerity.

In fact, he even hoped that forming a team would be helpful to the Black
Scythe.

“And the people you approached all agreed with your idea?”

“Yes, sir. They all understood my intent and promised to join willingly if it
was for such a team.”

Dorothy and Sophia were distant acquaintances, but Victor, Russell, and Jo
Yong-ho had all accepted eagerly?

That alone told Ryu Min that Alex was a trustworthy person.

However, allowing him to form a private team was another matter.

“I understand your intent. But it doesn’t look good. Stop forming a team.
Haven’t you already been misunderstood as a traitor?”

“Well… that’s true, but forming a team would still be more efficient…”

“No, it’s unnecessary. Teamwork isn’t an issue. I’ll be coordinating
everything myself, and all you have to do is follow my orders. The Death
Church is essentially a team already.”

“I-I see. If you say so, Black Scythe, sir… I apologize for acting on my
own.”

Alex apologized sincerely, his words genuine.

Yet, whether due to the language barrier or personal mistrust, Heo Tae-seok
still looked displeased.

“Black Scythe, sir. What excuse did that guy give you?”

“He claims he had no ulterior motives and insists he’s innocent.”

“That’s impossible. We should interrogate him until he confesses—”

“That won’t be necessary. It was a misunderstanding from the start.”

“A misunderstanding?”

“I’ll explain.”

Chapter 270: The Start Of The
17Th Round (2)

“That’s impossible. We should interrogate him until he confesses—”

“That won’t be necessary. It was a misunderstanding from the start.”

“A misunderstanding?”

“I’ll explain.”

Ryu Min summarized Alex’s explanation for Heo Tae-seok.

It was a convincing reason, but Heo Tae-seok still refused to let go of his
distrust.

“He’s lying! If he weren’t lying, why would he attack me first?”

At this, Ryu Min turned his gaze back to Alex.

“Did you attack Heo Tae-seok first?”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“I was trying to survive. He restrained me and glared at me like he was
going to kill me. How could I not fight back?”

Alex had simply responded defensively.

Ryu Min translated Alex’s reasoning, but Heo Tae-seok still didn’t believe
him.

“He must be lying…”

“He’s not. I can tell. It seems like the two of you just misunderstood each
other.”

“…”

With that verdict, Heo Tae-seok couldn’t argue further.

“Now that we know it was a misunderstanding, make peace with each
other.”

He spoke in both languages to ensure both parties understood, but silence
hung between them.

“At the very least, apologize to each other.”

“I’m sorry.”

“I apologize.”

Only after some awkward hesitation did the two mutter apologies.

Watching the tense atmosphere between them, Ryu Min clicked his tongue
behind his mask.

‘What a mess.’

Allies nearly drew swords on each other over a trivial misunderstanding.

‘This is what happens when people don’t speak the same language.’

Alex was partly to blame for his suspicious actions, but Heo Tae-seok also
shared fault for jumping to conclusions without knowing the full story.

At this point, Ryu Min had resolved the conflict but still had one last
misunderstanding to clear up. He glanced over at Heo Tae-seok, who still
seemed uneasy.

“Heo Tae-seok.”

“Yes, Black Scythe, sir.”

“Just so there are no further misunderstandings, let me clear something up:
don’t get hung up on the order in which I call names. It’s not based on how
important you are.”

Heo Tae-seok’s eyes widened. It was as if Ryu Min had read his mind.

“I-Is that so? I thought the order you called was based on… importance.”

“No, it wasn’t. For the top three, yes, I called those with the highest
contribution scores—priests and buffers who were vital to the mission. But
after that, I just called names as they came to mind. There was no specific
ranking.”

“Ah…”

“So if you thought I didn’t value you highly, I hope you’ll let go of that
misunderstanding. Do you really think I’d overlook the founder of the
Death Church?”

“Black Scythe, sir…”

A moment ago, Heo Tae-seok’s eyes had been blazing with frustration.
Now, they softened with gratitude and reverence.

‘Typical of a devout follower.’

With that, the minor misunderstanding that had caused all this drama was
finally resolved.

“Let’s go. Back to the Death Church.”

-

Building the Hero’s Rune stack wasn’t a difficult task for Ryu Min.

All he had to do was summon a demon using a Black Seed in the presence
of the Death God Church members, then kill it.

[Hero’s Rune Stack: 100/100]

[With the Hero’s Rune effect, all stats have increased by 100.]

[You can now expend 100 stacks to activate ‘Hero’s Protection.’]

‘Good. Now I can protect my brother.’

Feeling satisfied, Ryu Min passed by Heo Tae-seok, patting him on the
shoulder.

“Well done, Heo. You’ve been a big help.”

“Ah…”

Heo Tae-seok didn’t understand how he’d been helpful, but that didn’t
matter to him. The mere acknowledgment from the Black Scythe filled him
with pride and satisfaction.

‘It’s good to toss him some praise every now and then.’

Ryu Min smirked under his mask as he stepped onto the platform to address
the gathered followers.

It was time to share the strategy for the 17th round.

-

At midnight on May 1st, everyone awoke in the otherworld, unlike the
previous round.

“How many months has it been since we were in our characters?”

“Two months?”

“Only two? It feels like it’s been much longer.”

“Still, waking up in this body feels oddly comforting.”

As though slipping into a perfectly tailored suit, the players’ faces lit up
with satisfaction. By now, starting a new round in their avatar bodies had
become the norm. Anything else felt strange.

“At least we don’t need the translator this time.”

“Right? That thing was such a hassle.”

“Hi, Max.”

“Hey, Fernando.”

“Yo, Mr. Wang. You made it?”

Perhaps because their numbers had dwindled, or maybe because they had
bonded during the near-death experience of the last round, the Death
Church members greeted each other warmly, regardless of nationality.

Among them, Min Juri and Christine, who had both played prominent roles
in the party, were especially popular.

“Hello, Buffer.”

“Oh, hi there.”

“Christine, thanks again for healing me last time.”

“It’s nothing, really.”

Meanwhile, Alex and Heo Tae-seok briefly locked eyes but quickly turned
away, pretending not to notice each other.

Ryu Min didn’t concern himself with them.

‘They’ll come around eventually.’

He wasn’t worried about the future.

With Hero’s Protection applied to his brother, he felt a rare sense of peace.

‘Even if an archangel shows up, he’ll be safe.’

The only possible variable was if the archangel tried to target his brother
while he was in the otherworld. But that was unlikely.

‘Angels lose 90% of their power when they cross into the human world.’

This was knowledge he had gleaned by reading the minds of the angels.

‘The one to watch out for is likely Michael. He’ll probably appear this
round.’

Ryu Min felt both fear and anticipation.

The enemies so far had failed to live up to his expectations.

And if he managed to take Michael down, he could finally complete the
Soul Binding Quest.

He couldn’t help but wonder what the reward would be.

‘I just hope he doesn’t show up and interfere with my plan to hunt the
dragon.’

Ryu Min had decided to hunt a dragon during this round.

With a massive war looming in the 18th round, this was his best chance—
either now or in the 19th round.

Just then, a clear, resonant voice echoed from the dull, gray sky.

[Greetings, humans. All 288 of you. Welcome to the 17th round.]

Though the angel’s words welcomed them, her expression betrayed
annoyance.

[You’ve survived in surprisingly large numbers. Normally, there wouldn’t
be this many left by now…]

The angel furrowed her brows, then quickly brightened with a smile.

[Well, I suppose many of you will fall in this round. Unlike before, this one
requires brains, not brawn.]

Despite her words, none of the players appeared concerned.

They already knew what to expect, thanks to the Black Scythe.

[Shall we reveal the quest for the 17th round?]

Chapter 272: Strategy Simulation
Game (1)

If you’re a South Korean male, chances are you’ve played a strategy
simulation game at least once in your life.

“You know that game where you collect minerals, right? It’s pretty similar
to that.”

Ryu Min was explaining to the members just how easy it was to win a war.

“You don’t need to overthink it. See here? The troop menu. If you press this
and then this again…”

“It says ‘Upgrade Troops’?”

“You can use gold to strengthen the soldiers?”

“That’s right.”

When Ryu Min directly pointed at the screen and explained, they quickly
caught on.

“As the commander, you can spend your gold to upgrade or add equipment
for your troops. If you don’t have enough forces, you can also hire
mercenaries. Of course, that costs gold too.”

“So, the more commanders we have, the more advantageous it will be?”

“Exactly. The more commanders, the more gold there is to go around.”

Having more commanders on one side was naturally advantageous. Just as
a server’s performance improves with more CPUs, having more brains
strategizing in a war also provides an edge. And right now, the disparity in
gold was already significant.

Even so, the players still looked troubled.

The reason? They had taken a closer look at the prices.

“Upgrading the weapon of a single soldier costs 1,000 gold?”

“So, for 10,000 soldiers, that’s 10 million gold?”

“This… these prices are insane!”

Adding mercenaries was even worse.

“Adding just one veteran mercenary costs 10,000 gold?”

“T-That’s way too expensive!”

No matter how many people they had, the players didn’t have enough gold
to make it feasible.

“L-Let’s check how much gold we all have. What’s everyone holding
onto?”

“I’ve got 1.3 million gold.”

“I’ve got 1.1 million…”

No one had more than 2 million gold. And even that was only because they
had received 1 million gold each as the reward for completing the 16th
round.

At that moment, a player spoke in disbelief.

“Even if everyone here has 1 million gold each, we’re only looking at about
300 million gold in total…”

“300 million? What can we even do with that?”

“The kingdom’s army is 320,000 strong…”

“So hiring 30,000 mercenaries is all we can manage?”

The kingdom’s army of 30,000 versus the Holy Empire’s army of 320,000.

A gap over ten times as large.

Could they really bridge that chasm just by adding 30,000 mercenaries?
Could that alone turn the tide of the war in favor of the kingdom?

People shook their heads in disbelief.

The overwhelming difference in numbers crushed their spirits.

Some even muttered under their breath, lamenting their doomed fate.

Seeing this, Ryu Min clicked his tongue in annoyance and said, “Didn’t I
tell you? There’s no need to worry.”

“Black Scythe-nim, do you have some sort of plan…?”

“Do you know how much gold I have?”

When people shook their heads, Ryu Min smirked and revealed, “60
billion.”

“W-What?!”

“A-Are you serious?”

“T-That much…”

In truth, he had closer to 100 billion, but he deliberately understated it. He
had already budgeted 60 billion for this round.

‘Besides, it’s better to make it seem like I’m pouring everything into this
than to let them think I’m holding something back.’

Even the lower figure was enough to shock everyone present.

“Surely, you’re not planning to invest all 60 billion?”

“I will. Considering the rewards for victory, it’s worth every coin.”

The despair on their faces turned to hope.

Some even gazed at Ryu Min as though he were a saint.

“There’s no need to worry anymore. If Black Scythe-nim is spending all 60
billion…”

“No, I can’t spend it all by myself.”

“Huh?”

Though they were confused at first, the reason quickly became clear.

“There’s a cap on how much each person can use.”

“A cap? How much?”

“Each individual can only use up to 1 billion gold. I’m not sure why this
restriction exists, but it’s there.”

Although he claimed not to know the reason, Ryu Min had a good idea.

‘The system probably didn’t expect anyone to have more than 1 billion gold
at this stage.’

But here he was, a player with 100 billion in reserve. Even though he
couldn’t spend it all himself…

“Since there’s a limit, I can’t spend it all alone. So, from now on, I’m going
to distribute 20 million gold to each of you. Everyone, accept my trade
request.”

Ryu Min initiated trades, distributing 20 million gold to each player.

However, Min Juri and Christine received more than the others.

“Um, did you give me the wrong amount?”

“Why so much…?”

He had given them twice as much as he promised, which was naturally
surprising. But there was a reason for it.

“You two need to spend it all. That way, you can secure the rank rewards.”

“Ah…!”

This round’s rankings would be determined by how much gold was spent.

By giving the two of them a larger sum, he ensured they would place in the
top ranks.

‘But of course, I’m not letting go of first place.’

Using 1 billion gold himself would guarantee his spot at the top.

After distributing 20 million gold each to the 285 others, he had spent 57.5
billion gold.

“You all know what to do with the gold I’ve given you, right?”

“Yes!”

“You can use it however you see fit—upgrade weapons and armor, or hire
mercenaries. As long as you pour every last coin into this, the tide of war
will shift in our favor. Got it?”

“Yes, understood!”

Ryu Min’s words carried an authoritative power that compelled obedience.

It wasn’t just a metaphor—there was a real force behind them.

It was none other than the temporary skill he possessed.

[Temporary Skill – Commander]

Effect: A passive skill that ensures players follow your orders.

Active only during the 17th round; the effect vanishes once the round ends.

‘With this, there’s no chance of them disobeying.’

No one would dare misuse the gold for personal reasons or hoard it. The
skill’s effect was absolute.

‘Now that the war is in the hands of these 285 commanders…’

Ryu Min looked out of the barracks.

During the war, he had another task to accomplish.

‘I need to slay the dragon in its lair.’

It wasn’t every day that he had the chance to acquire a god-tier accessory on
top of titles and runes.

‘But first, I need to spend my own 1 billion gold.’

Approaching the status board, Ryu Min used his gold to recruit an
additional 10,000 troops.

Satisfied with the result, he exited the barracks and took to the skies.

To claim the dragon’s reward for himself.

Chapter 272: Strategy Simulation
Game (2)

[Player ‘Kobolt Blue’ has joined the ‘Holy Empire’ faction.]

[You have obtained the qualification of a commander in the Holy Empire
faction.]

[You will be immediately transported to the command barracks.]

Having arrived at the barracks of the Holy Empire, Kobolt Blue smiled to
himself.

This wasn’t a mistake.

He knew exactly what he was doing.

‘I betrayed Black Scythe.’

Not just Black Scythe, but the entire Death Church.

‘They probably all chose the Kingdom Alliance, except me.’

He’d heard it directly from Black Scythe himself.

The Holy Empire was overwhelmingly stronger.

Yet despite that, the others had chosen the Kingdom Alliance.

Only because Black Scythe had instructed them to.

‘But I don’t think so. Black Scythe will definitely side with the Holy
Empire.’

Black Scythe had forced others to choose the Kingdom Alliance.

Even though it was weaker, even though the odds were against it—he’d
claimed the rewards would be greater.

‘He didn’t even explain how he plans to win the war, yet he’s pushing us to
pick the Kingdom Alliance? He must be hiding something.’

From that moment on, Kobolt Blue started to doubt Black Scythe.

He was convinced Black Scythe was lying.

‘He’s throwing everyone else into the losing side while secretly aligning
with the Holy Empire himself. I’m sure of it.’

How could he be so certain?

Because if it were him, that’s exactly what he would do.

If there was a time to stab someone in the back, it would be now.

‘Though, honestly, what reason would Black Scythe even have to betray
them…?’

Kobolt Blue didn’t know for sure.

But he was sure there had to be some reason.

‘Like if the system rewards players who win against the odds with some
massive bonus… or something like that.’

Of course, it was all just speculation.

Even his report to the Death Church leader about the “faction” incident had
been based on a similar hunch.

‘To be honest, I didn’t hear anything clearly. I just overheard them chatting
about something.’

Even so, he’d exaggerated his claims, saying they were forming a faction
and adding his own assumptions to the mix.

It was only because the church leader was gullible that the lie had been
believed and acted upon.

In the end, his report hadn’t earned him any rewards, not even a shred of
acknowledgment.

‘Honestly, they should’ve rewarded me for that! Not a single thing in
return. Tch.’

He had expected some form of compensation for his “tip-off,” but it had
been a complete waste of effort.

‘This is why you can’t trust black-haired beasts.’

Kobolt Blue’s disdain for “black-haired beasts” extended to Black Scythe
himself.

And so, he became convinced.

Convinced that Black Scythe was planning to betray them.

He chose the Holy Empire faction purely out of his own baseless suspicions
and paranoia, betraying Black Scythe, who had called his name during the
16th round.

‘Some might say I’m insane for betting my life on such uncertainty.’

But Kobolt Blue didn’t regret it.

‘As long as I survive, that’s all that matters.’

In strategy simulation games, he considered himself unbeatable.

It was then that he noticed movement.

Tsssshhh—

A figure materialized before his eyes.

Someone else had entered the barracks.

‘Could it be… Black Scythe?’

He felt a thrill of satisfaction.

His suspicion had been correct. Black Scythe had deceived everyone and
chosen the Holy Empire after all.

But that satisfaction quickly turned to disappointment.

It wasn’t Black Scythe. It was someone else.

“Oh? I didn’t think anyone else would be here.”

“And you are…?”

“My name’s Chris. My username is [Chris Tian].”

It was a name Kobolt Blue didn’t recognize.

At least the newcomer wasn’t one of the “black-haired beasts,” which was a
small relief.

“So, why did you choose the Holy Empire?”

“Well, why did you?”

“I asked first.”

“Fair enough…”

As Kobolt Blue listened to Chris Tian’s explanation, a small smirk formed
on his face.

It seemed they shared the same reasoning.

“You doubted Black Scythe, didn’t you?”

“Yes. Telling us to choose the weaker Kingdom Alliance… I couldn’t help
but wonder what would happen if we all just ended up dead.”

“So, you decided to trust your gut instead?”

“Exactly. Plus, I couldn’t shake the feeling that Black Scythe might actually
side with the Holy Empire.”

In the end, Chris Tian had made the same gamble as Kobolt Blue.

Out of doubt and paranoia, they had both abandoned the Kingdom Alliance.

“But it’s just us here. What about Black Scythe?”

“He’ll show up soon, I’m sure of it.”

But contrary to their expectations, the system announcement revealed a
different outcome.

[The faction selection period has ended.]

[Faction Selection Results:]

└ Holy Empire: 2 players

└ Kingdom Alliance: 286 players

“W-What? Aside from us, everyone chose the Kingdom Alliance?”

“Does that mean Black Scythe is on their side too…?”

Chris Tian was stunned, but Kobolt Blue quickly composed himself.

“Well, there’s nothing we can do about it now. We’ll just have to kill them
all ourselves.”

“You’re joking, right? How are we supposed to beat 286 people?”

“Why not? This is a strategy game, not a brawl.”

Kobolt Blue grinned.

In terms of strategy simulation games, he considered himself as skilled as a
pro gamer.

“No matter how many outdated CPUs you slap together, garbage is still
garbage. A high-performance CPU like me will outperform them all. Heh.”

But just as he was smiling confidently and looking at the battle interface,
his face twisted in confusion.

“W-What the…?”

His eyes darted across the screen.

The enemy’s red markers were increasing at an alarming rate.

“This… this doesn’t make sense. Is the screen broken?”

He tapped the display, thinking it was a malfunction.

But the red dots kept multiplying in real time, almost like cells dividing.

“W-What is this? Why are the enemies multiplying?”

“I… I don’t know!”

“They’ve doubled our numbers already!”

The Kingdom Alliance, originally estimated at 300,000 troops, now boasted
over 600,000.

Cold sweat trickled down both their faces.

‘W-Wait a minute. Is the Holy Empire really supposed to be the stronger
side here?’

Kobolt Blue began to doubt everything, unaware that his suspicions had
already brought ruin upon him.

At that moment, the Kingdom Alliance troops began their advance.

Chris Tian panicked and shouted, “T-They’re coming! Aren’t you supposed
to be good at this? Do something! Come up with a strategy!”

“W-Well… uh… th-the thing is…”

How could he strategize? The enemy had double their forces and superior
equipment. There wasn’t much strategy to come up with in such a lopsided
scenario.

Kobolt Blue could only watch as the situation spiraled further out of
control.

‘O-Our forces are being wiped out so fast.’

The disparity in numbers was staggering, but it wasn’t just that. The quality
of the Kingdom Alliance’s weapons and armor also far outclassed their
own.

Otherwise, their soldiers wouldn’t be falling so quickly, like blades of grass
cut down by a scythe.

‘W-We’re doomed. If this keeps up, we’ll be annihilated.’

Kobolt Blue hastily gave the order to retreat. There was no time to think
about terrain advantages or clever strategies.

The only priority was escaping.

The first battle of the Holy Empire ended in a devastating defeat.

Chapter 273: Dragon Subjugation
(1)

A player who has become a commander usually stays in the barracks.

Why?

Because they cannot directly interfere in the war anyway.

Not only do they have no way of knowing the exact location of the
battlefield, but the system also blocks access to those areas.

That is the rule of the 17th round.

Even if a player leaves the barracks, there is nothing much they can do.

‘Or so I thought. Until I actually stepped outside the barracks.’

In the past, Ryu Min had explored the surroundings to confirm whether he
truly couldn’t participate in the war.

The area was nothing but mountain ranges, with rugged terrain and no
roads, but it wasn’t completely isolated.

‘Beyond the mountains, there was a city. A small kingdom called Dekan.’

However, as the system had warned, an invisible barrier blocked access to
the war zone.

Still, it wasn’t a complete loss.

He could make use of the kingdom’s mercenary group.

[Golden Eagle Mercenary Corps – Dekan Branch]

Although the sign was written in an otherworldly language, it was
automatically translated.

‘If I use the mercenary group, I can hunt the dragon.’

Of course, he had to do it before the war ended.

‘No need to worry. There are still more than three hours left.’

Stepping inside, Ryu Min was greeted by a smiling receptionist.

“How can I help you?”

“I’m here to request a subjugation mission.”

“Just a moment… Oh my, you have a [Master] rank mercenary badge. Let
me check for suitable requests…”

The receptionist searched through the records, but Ryu Min already knew.

There was only one request available for a Master rank mercenary.

“There is a Dragon Subjugation request… Would you like to accept it?”

[You are eligible to undertake the Black Dragon Karsainox Subjugation
Quest.

Do you accept? Y/N]

“If you don’t wish to take it, I can recommend a lower-tier mission instead
—”

“I’ll take it.”

There was no reason to refuse.

As soon as he accepted, the receptionist nodded and instructed him to wait
outside, as the subjugation team would arrive shortly.

Sure enough, not long after, the subjugation team arrived in front of the
mercenary headquarters.

“Are you the Black Scythe? I am Antonio Richardson, Captain of the
Golden Eagle Mercenary Corps’ Second Subjugation Unit. You volunteered
to hunt the Dragon of Death?”

“Yes.”

“Impressive courage. These are your fellow brave volunteers—introduce
yourself to them.”

Ryu Min glanced at the twenty mercenaries gathered.

Judging by their appearances, they were a diverse party of mages, archers,
and warriors.

But in the end, they were all just NPCs.

‘I can’t rely on background characters.’

The task of hunting the dragon was solely his responsibility as the
volunteer.

“Introductions are done, so let’s move out.”

Following the mercenaries, they arrived at a warp gate nearby.

“Brace yourself.”

In the blink of an eye, the scenery around Ryu Min changed.

They had arrived at the Valley of Death, where the Black Dragon’s lair was
located.

---

A dragon’s lair is not a place just anyone can enter.

Even if one knows its location, entry is blocked unless they have reached
the ‘Master’ rank—the highest tier within the mercenary group.

This was why Ryu Min hadn’t brought Ju Seong-tak, despite his 10x boss
drop rate ability.

‘Not that I would have brought him anyway, because of titles and runes.’

The first player to kill a dragon earns a unique title and rune.

That was non-negotiable.

Giving up such rewards just to increase item drop rates? Impossible.

‘Besides, my Luck stat is high enough to get all the items anyway.’

Luck influenced not only gacha draws but also item drop rates.

Even with only Min Juri’s Blessing applied, his Luck stat exceeded
870,000.

At this level, even the rarest items had a 100% chance of dropping.

“Monsters ahead!”

“Prepare for battle!”

“Stay alert!”

The mercenaries tensed as monsters appeared at the entrance of the valley.

Dark Illusions—monsters that had first appeared in the 15th round.

“Uuuuuuuh—”

Draped in tattered robes, they moved freely in the darkness.

Faced with them, the mercenaries trembled.

They had been struck by fear.

Still, as a dragon subjugation squad, they recovered quickly.

But it was already too late.

The monster’s claws were just inches away.

However—

Schwik!

‘I can’t let the guide die.’

Ryu Min’s scythe was faster.

The Dark Illusion was sliced apart like paper and vanished.

[Dark Illusion defeated!]

[Title effect: EXP increased by 1.5x.]

[Devourer Rune effect: EXP and gold increased by 2x.]

[Devourer Rune: Gained 5 stacks and 1 stat point.]

[Total Devourer stacks: 5]

[EXP +0.47%]

[Gold +20,000]

[Additional Gold +10,000]

[Heroic Rune Stack: 1/100]

[Heroic Rune effect: All stats +1.]

[Current Kill Count: 1/100]

[Slaughter Rune effect: All stats +1%]

[100m radius: 19 enemies detected.]

[One-vs-Hundred Rune effect: All stats +19%]

A flood of notifications appeared just from killing a single monster.

‘Maybe it wasn’t a small fry?’

Dark Illusions were stronger than High Orcs, so calling them minor
enemies might be a stretch.

Then again, to Ryu Min, even boss monsters were no more than small fry.

‘In the 15th round, they were invincible, so I couldn’t kill them, but…’

Schwik!

With a single slash, another Dark Illusion disintegrated.

‘That’s no longer the case.’

It didn’t matter how many appeared.

He would cut them all down.

As he relentlessly killed every enemy in sight, the mercenaries had no
chance to intervene.

“Y-you’re incredible.”

“So this is the Black Scythe? No wonder he’s a Master rank.”

Ryu Min didn’t smile at the NPCs’ praise.

Laughing at pre-programmed dialogue would be embarrassing.

‘Besides, killing small fry isn’t exactly praise-worthy.’

After defeating 20 Dark Illusions, he had already accumulated 20 stat
points.

A small amount for him, but an objectively enormous gain.

In level terms, it was like leveling up ten times.

‘This is why the Devourer Rune is great. It just throws stats at me.’

And that wasn’t all.

[Devourer Rune stacks reached 100!]

[Bonus effect: Strength and body size increased by 10%.]
